commands.purpose: Check the computer's current network configuration and confirm it has a valid IP address and connection
commands.expectedResult: Shows a valid IP address and active network adapter
commands.abnormalResult: No valid IP address, or a self-assigned 169.254 address, indicating a broader network connectivity problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the computer has a working internet or network connection independent of Notes, such as by browsing a website
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This determines if the problem is specific to reaching the Domino server, or a broader network issue affecting everything

troubleshootingSteps.action: If working remotely, confirm the VPN connection is active, since many organizations require VPN to reach internal Domino servers
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Without an active VPN, remote computers typically cannot reach internal company servers like Domino at all

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the Domino server by its configured name to test basic network reachability
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly confirms whether a network path currently exists to the server from this specific computer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with coworkers, especially those in the same office or using the same VPN, to see if they are experiencing the same connection issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This quickly indicates whether the problem is isolated to this one user or affects the server more broadly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the Notes location document currently in use (shown in the status bar) to confirm the correct server name and connection settings are configured
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect or outdated server name in the location document will prevent Notes from finding the correct server, even with a working network connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the Notes client completely to clear any temporary connection state issues
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A fresh restart can resolve connection problems caused by a stuck or corrupted session state within Notes itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the problem affects multiple users, contact the Notes or Domino administrator immediately, since this likely indicates a server outage or network infrastructure problem
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A widespread connectivity issue requires administrator-level investigation into the server and network infrastructure itself

possibleSolutions: Restore a working internet or network connection
Reconnect the VPN for remote users
Correct the server name in the Notes location document
Restart the Notes client to clear a stuck connection state
Report a widespread outage to the Notes/Domino administrator
prevention: Maintain a stable VPN connection when working remotely
Keep location documents correctly configured with accurate server information
Stay informed of scheduled server maintenance windows
Report connectivity issues to IT promptly for faster resolution

description: The user is connected to the network normally, but the Domino server itself seems unresponsive, with requests to open databases or send mail taking a very long time or timing out completely.
symptoms: Long delays when trying to open any server-based database
Error message after a long wait saying the server did not respond
Sending and receiving mail becomes extremely slow or fails
Other users on the same server report similar symptoms
possibleCauses: The Domino server is experiencing very high load or resource usage
A specific server task or process has become stuck, affecting overall responsiveness
Network congestion between the user's location and the server
The server is undergoing maintenance or a restart
A hardware issue on the physical server affecting performance
diagnosticQuestions: Are other users experiencing the same slowness or unresponsiveness with this server right now?
Does this happen with all databases on this server, or just specific ones?
Has the server administrator mentioned any planned maintenance or known issues?
Does the problem happen consistently, or does it come and go?

commands.purpose: Check basic network response time to the server to distinguish between a network delay and a true server performance issue
commands.expectedResult: Fast, consistent reply times
commands.abnormalResult: Very slow or inconsistent reply times, or request timeouts, suggesting either network congestion or server-side overload

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are also experiencing slowness or unresponsiveness with the same server
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This quickly confirms whether the issue is server-wide, affecting everyone, or isolated to this one user's connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the server to check basic network response times
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps distinguish between a network path problem and the server itself being genuinely overloaded or stuck

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note whether the unresponsiveness affects all databases on the server, or seems limited to a specific one
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A problem limited to one specific database may point to something more localized, such as a stuck task related to that database specifically, rather than the entire server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for any recent communication from IT about planned server maintenance, restarts, or known ongoing issues
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Scheduled maintenance activities commonly cause temporary server unresponsiveness that resolves once the work is finished

troubleshootingSteps.action: Wait a reasonable amount of time, such as 10 to 15 minutes, in case the server is temporarily overloaded and will recover on its own
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Server load spikes can sometimes resolve naturally as the underlying cause, such as a batch job, completes

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the problem continues or affects multiple users, immediately report it to the Notes or Domino administrator with specific details about when it started and which server is affected
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Server performance issues require administrator-level access to the server console and logs to properly diagnose and resolve

troubleshootingSteps.action: Avoid repeatedly retrying the same failed operation many times in quick succession while waiting for the server issue to be addressed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Repeated retries can add additional, unnecessary load to an already struggling server, potentially worsening the situation for all users

possibleSolutions: Wait for a temporary server load spike to resolve naturally
Wait out scheduled server maintenance
Report the issue immediately to the Notes/Domino administrator with specific details
Avoid excessive retry attempts that could add load to a struggling server
prevention: Stay informed of scheduled server maintenance windows
Report server slowness patterns to IT so they can monitor server load proactively
Avoid running unusually heavy tasks against the server during peak usage times

problem: Database is unavailable when trying to open it
description: The user tries to open a specific database, whether mail or another application, but receives a message stating the database is unavailable, preventing any access to its contents.
symptoms: Error message stating 'Database is not available'
Icon for the database may appear on the workspace but cannot be opened
Other server databases may work normally while this specific one fails
Problem may be temporary or persistent
possibleCauses: The database has been temporarily taken offline for maintenance
The database file has been moved, renamed, or deleted on the server
A server-side task, such as a compact or fixup operation, is currently locking the database
The Domino server itself is experiencing connectivity or performance issues
The user's access rights to this specific database have been changed or removed
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen with only this one database, or with others as well?
Have you been able to access this database successfully in the past?
Do you know if any maintenance work was scheduled for this database or server?
Are other users able to access this same database right now?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try opening a different, unrelated database on the same server to see if the problem is specific to this one database or affects the whole server connection
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This narrows down whether the issue is isolated to a single database or represents a broader server connectivity problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they can access this same specific database right now
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the unavailability is affecting everyone, or possibly related to this specific user's permissions

troubleshootingSteps.action: Wait a short period and try again, since the database may be temporarily locked by a maintenance task, such as a compact or fixup operation, that will complete shortly
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Server-side maintenance operations often only temporarily restrict access while they run

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for any communication from IT regarding planned maintenance affecting this specific database or its host server
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Scheduled maintenance is a very common and expected cause of temporary database unavailability

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the database was accessible before but suddenly stopped being available, contact the database owner or Notes administrator, since it may have been moved, renamed, or had its access permissions changed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: These types of administrative changes on the server side can directly cause this exact error for standard users

troubleshootingSteps.action: Provide the administrator with the exact database name, the exact error message, and the approximate time the problem started
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Detailed, specific information significantly speeds up the administrator's ability to diagnose the exact cause on the server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once access is restored, confirm the database opens and displays data correctly, checking a few different views if possible
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This confirms the issue is genuinely and fully resolved rather than only partially fixed

possibleSolutions: Wait for a temporary server-side maintenance lock to clear
Wait out scheduled maintenance affecting the database
Have the administrator investigate a moved, renamed, or access-restricted database
Report detailed information to speed up administrator diagnosis
prevention: Stay informed of scheduled maintenance affecting frequently used databases
Report unavailability issues promptly with specific details
Confirm access changes with users in advance when possible

problem: Access denied when trying to open a database or perform an action
description: The user attempts to open a database or perform a specific action, such as editing a document, but receives an error stating they do not have sufficient access rights to do so.
symptoms: Error message such as 'You are not authorized to perform that operation'
Database opens but shows no documents, or only some documents
Cannot edit, create, or delete documents that should be editable
Error may appear consistently, or only for specific actions
possibleCauses: The user's access control list (ACL) entry for this database does not grant sufficient rights
The user is not listed in the ACL at all and is defaulting to a very restricted access level
A recent change to the ACL removed or reduced the user's previous access
The user's group membership, which determines access through role-based ACL entries, was changed
The user is trying to perform an action reserved for a higher access level, such as Manager or Designer
diagnosticQuestions: What exact action were you trying to perform when this error appeared, such as opening, editing, or deleting?
Have you had successful access to this database before, or is this your first time trying?
Do you know if you were recently added to or removed from any relevant security groups?
Are other users with a similar role able to access this database normally?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact action being performed and the exact wording of the error message
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps distinguish between a complete access denial and a more limited restriction on a specific action, like editing versus just reading

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with the database owner or Notes administrator about your current access control list (ACL) entry for this specific database
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The ACL directly controls what each user or group can do within a database, and reviewing it confirms your exact current access level

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether you are individually listed in the ACL, or if your access depends on membership in a specific group
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Group-based access can be affected by changes to group membership that are not always immediately obvious to the end user

troubleshootingSteps.action: If your access level appears lower than expected, or you are missing entirely from the ACL, request that the database owner or administrator add or update your entry appropriately
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly resolves the root cause by granting the correct level of access needed for your role

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm with colleagues in a similar role whether they can access the database normally, to help clarify if this is an individual account issue or a broader change affecting a whole group
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps the administrator prioritize and understand the scope of the access problem more efficiently

troubleshootingSteps.action: If access was recently working and suddenly stopped, ask if any recent ACL changes were made to the database, intentionally or by mistake
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Recent administrative changes are a common and straightforward explanation for a sudden loss of previously working access

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once updated access is granted, close and reopen the database, since ACL changes sometimes require a fresh session to take full effect
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the newly granted permissions are properly recognized and applied

possibleSolutions: Request an updated ACL entry from the database owner or administrator
Confirm and correct group membership affecting access
Have a recent unintended ACL change reverted
Reopen the database after access changes to apply them properly
prevention: Review ACL entries carefully whenever a database is shared with new users
Communicate group membership changes that may affect database access
Document expected access levels for different user roles

problem: Notes workspace is missing or shows no database icons
description: The user opens Notes and expects to see their usual workspace with database icons for mail and other applications, but the workspace appears empty, blank, or missing entirely.
symptoms: Workspace tabs are empty with no database icons visible
Previously bookmarked databases no longer appear
Workspace looks reset to a default, blank state
May happen after a Notes update or reinstall
possibleCauses: The desktop configuration file (desktop8.ndk or similar) has become corrupted
A recent Notes reinstall or update reset the workspace configuration
The user is logged in with a different Notes ID than usual, which has its own separate workspace
The workspace file was accidentally deleted or moved
A new Notes profile is being used for the first time
diagnosticQuestions: Did this happen after a recent Notes update, reinstall, or computer change?
Are you logged in with your usual Notes ID, or possibly a different one?
Do you recall your workspace looking normal recently, or has it always looked empty on this computer?
Do you know if a workspace backup file exists from before this problem started?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm you are logged in with your correct, usual Notes ID by checking File > Security > User Security
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Each ID file has its own separate workspace, and accidentally using a different or new ID would show an empty workspace that is not actually missing, just different

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if this happened right after a Notes client update, reinstall, or migration to a new computer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: These events can sometimes reset the workspace to its default empty state, especially if the previous workspace configuration file was not properly carried over

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if a backup copy of the previous desktop configuration file exists, often named something like desktop8.ndk, in a backup location
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Restoring a backup of this file can bring back the previous workspace layout and database icons directly

troubleshootingSteps.action: If no backup exists, manually re-add the important databases to the workspace using File > Application > Open, browsing to each needed database
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This rebuilds a functional workspace from scratch, ensuring access to needed databases even without the original configuration file

troubleshootingSteps.action: For the mail file specifically, use File > Application > Open and connect to the mail server, then select your mail file to add it back to the workspace
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the most critical database, the user's mail, is restored to the workspace as a priority

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once databases are manually re-added, create bookmarks for frequently used ones for easier future access, since some newer Notes versions favor bookmarks over the traditional workspace tabs
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides a more resilient, easily recreated way to access important databases going forward

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the Notes administrator if you are unsure of the correct server names or paths needed to manually re-add specific company databases
troubleshootingSteps.reason: They can provide the exact information needed to properly reconnect to each required corporate database

possibleSolutions: Confirm the correct Notes ID is being used
Restore a backup copy of the desktop configuration file
Manually re-add important databases using File > Application > Open
Reconnect the mail file specifically as a priority
Recreate bookmarks for frequently used databases
Contact the administrator for correct server and database information
prevention: Keep a backup copy of the desktop configuration file
Document important database server names and paths
Use bookmarks in addition to workspace icons for redundancy
Confirm workspace data is properly migrated during computer changes

description: When trying to log in, the user is informed that their Notes password has expired and must be changed before they can continue accessing Notes.
symptoms: Message specifically stating the password has expired
Prompt to enter a new password appears during login
Login is blocked entirely until the password is changed
May happen suddenly based on a company-wide password expiration policy
possibleCauses: The organization enforces a password expiration policy after a set number of days
The password was not changed proactively before reaching its expiration date
A password change was made on another computer, but this computer has not yet synced the new password information
diagnosticQuestions: Does the message specifically mention that your password has expired, or is it a different error?
Do you know your organization's password expiration policy, such as every 90 days?
Have you changed your Notes password recently on a different computer?
Are you able to proceed with the password change prompt shown on screen?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Read the password expiration prompt carefully and follow the on-screen instructions to set a new password
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Notes typically provides a direct, built-in process for changing an expired password right at the login screen

troubleshootingSteps.action: Choose a new password that meets your organization's password complexity requirements, such as minimum length and character variety
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A new password that does not meet policy requirements will likely be rejected, requiring another attempt

troubleshootingSteps.action: After successfully setting the new password, confirm you can log in normally using it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This verifies the password change was fully successful and properly recognized by the system

troubleshootingSteps.action: If working on multiple computers with the same ID file, update the password on each computer, or ensure the ID file with the updated password is properly synced across them
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Password changes made through Notes update the local ID file, and other computers with a separate copy of the older ID file will still use the old password until updated

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the password change process itself fails or shows an error, contact the Notes or IT administrator for assistance
troubleshootingSteps.reason: In some cases, expired passwords require administrator-level action, especially if the standard self-service change process encounters an error

troubleshootingSteps.action: Going forward, consider setting a personal reminder a few days before your password is expected to expire, based on your organization's policy
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This allows you to change the password proactively and avoid being unexpectedly blocked from logging in during an important task

possibleSolutions: Follow the on-screen prompt to set a new password meeting policy requirements
Update the password consistently across multiple computers if applicable
Contact the Notes/IT administrator if the change process itself fails
Set a personal reminder to change passwords proactively before expiration
prevention: Change passwords proactively before their expiration date
Keep track of your organization's password expiration policy
Ensure the same updated ID file is used across all computers you log in from

problem: Search is not working properly in Lotus Notes
description: The user tries to search for specific emails or documents within a database, but the search returns no results, incorrect results, or an error, even though the content clearly exists.
symptoms: Search returns zero results for content known to exist
Error message when trying to perform a search
Search results seem outdated, missing recently added items
Search works in some databases but not others
possibleCauses: The full-text search index has not been created for this database
The search index exists but has become outdated or corrupted
The search index needs to be updated to include recently added documents
The search is being performed with incorrect search syntax or terms
A very large database causing search performance or reliability issues
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen with just one specific database, or with search across all databases?
Have you ever successfully searched in this database before?
Are you searching for very recently added or received items?
What exact search terms are you using, and does trying simpler terms change the result?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether a full-text search index has been created for this specific database by checking File > Application > Properties > Full Text tab
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Notes requires a search index to be built before full-text searching can work effectively, and this is not always enabled by default

troubleshootingSteps.action: If no index exists, create one using the Create Index option in the same properties dialog
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This builds the necessary search index, enabling full-text search to function correctly for this database going forward

troubleshootingSteps.action: If an index already exists but results seem outdated, manually update the index using the Update Index option
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Indexes do not always update instantly with new content, and a manual update ensures the search reflects the most recent documents

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the search index is scheduled to update automatically, and adjust the schedule to run more frequently if search results often seem outdated
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A more frequent update schedule ensures the search index stays closely aligned with the actual current content of the database

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try simplifying the search terms being used, removing any special characters or overly specific phrases
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Incorrect search syntax can prevent Notes from finding results that would otherwise be located with a simpler search term

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the database is very large, be aware that search performance can be slower, and allow extra time for results to fully return
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Extremely large databases naturally take longer to search thoroughly, which can sometimes appear as a search failure if results seem slow to arrive

troubleshootingSteps.action: If search continues to fail after confirming and updating the index, contact the Notes administrator, since the index itself may require a rebuild at the server level
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Persistent search index problems sometimes require administrator tools to properly rebuild from scratch

possibleSolutions: Create a full-text search index if one does not exist
Manually update an existing but outdated search index
Adjust the index update schedule to run more frequently
Simplify search terms and syntax
Have the administrator rebuild the index at the server level if needed
prevention: Enable full-text indexing for frequently searched databases
Set a reasonable automatic index update schedule
Use simple, clear search terms for best results
Periodically verify search functionality on important databases

description: The user's Notes calendar does not show meetings or appointments correctly, either missing recent invitations, showing outdated information, or not matching what is shown on another device or calendar application.
symptoms: Recent meeting invitations do not appear on the calendar
Calendar entries are missing, duplicated, or show incorrect times
Changes made on a mobile device do not reflect in the desktop Notes calendar
Calendar looks different between the local replica and the server version
possibleCauses: Replication between the local replica and server has not run recently or failed
A time zone mismatch causing meetings to display at incorrect times
Calendar profile settings are misconfigured
A specific calendar entry has become corrupted
Synchronization with an external calendar or mobile device is not properly configured
diagnosticQuestions: Is this calendar issue happening in your local replica, or when connected directly to the server?
Are you comparing this to a calendar on a mobile device or another synced application?
Do you know if replication has run successfully recently for your mail file?
Have you noticed a consistent time difference, such as meetings appearing an hour off?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Manually trigger a replication of your mail file, since the calendar is typically part of the mail database
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the most current calendar data from the server is pulled down to the local replica immediately

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the replication history to confirm the replication completed successfully without errors
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A failed or incomplete replication would directly explain why calendar changes are not appearing as expected

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your Notes calendar profile settings under Preferences > Calendar and To Do, confirming the time zone setting matches your actual current location
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A mismatched time zone setting is a common cause of meetings appearing to be at the wrong time, even though the underlying data is correct

troubleshootingSteps.action: If comparing against a mobile device or another calendar application, check that the synchronization method between Notes and that device is properly configured and currently working
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Mismatches between Notes and external calendars often stem from a broken or misconfigured separate sync process, rather than a problem within Notes itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: For a specific calendar entry that seems corrupted or behaves unexpectedly, try opening it directly and checking its details for anything unusual, such as an incorrect date field
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Individual corrupted entries can sometimes be identified and manually corrected or recreated

troubleshootingSteps.action: If problems persist across the whole calendar, consider rebuilding the calendar view index using the standard Notes view refresh or rebuild options
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A corrupted or outdated calendar view index can cause entries to display incorrectly even when the underlying data is fine

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the Notes administrator if calendar synchronization problems continue, especially if they involve integration with external systems like a company-wide scheduling tool
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Broader calendar synchronization issues, especially involving cross-system integration, often require administrator-level tools to properly diagnose

possibleSolutions: Manually trigger and confirm successful replication
Correct the time zone setting in the calendar profile
Fix or reconfigure synchronization with an external calendar or mobile device
Manually correct a specific corrupted calendar entry
Rebuild the calendar view index
Contact the administrator for broader synchronization issues
prevention: Ensure replication runs regularly and successfully
Confirm time zone settings are correct, especially after travel
Regularly verify external calendar sync connections are working
Report calendar discrepancies to IT promptly

problem: Contacts are missing from the address book
description: The user opens their Notes contacts (address book) expecting to see previously saved entries, but some or all contacts are missing, incomplete, or not appearing as expected.
symptoms: Previously saved contacts no longer appear in the address book
Contacts appear with missing information, such as no email address
Recently added contacts do not show up
Contacts visible on another device are missing in the desktop Notes client
possibleCauses: Replication between the local contacts replica and the server has not run recently or failed
Contacts were accidentally deleted
A corrupted local contacts (names.nsf) database
Contacts were saved to a different, unintended contacts database
Synchronization with a separate corporate directory or external contacts source is not functioning
diagnosticQuestions: Are the missing contacts personal ones you added yourself, or ones from a shared/corporate directory?
Have you checked if replication has run successfully recently?
Do the missing contacts appear on another device or through webmail, if available?
Did you recently do anything that might have affected your contacts, such as an accidental deletion or a computer change?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether the missing contacts are personal entries you added yourself, versus entries that should be coming from a shared corporate directory
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This distinguishes between a personal contacts database issue and a directory synchronization issue, which have very different causes and fixes

troubleshootingSteps.action: Manually trigger a replication of your local contacts (names.nsf) database if it is a replicated database
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the most current contacts data from the server is properly synchronized to the local replica

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the replication history for the contacts database to confirm it completed successfully
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A failed replication would directly explain missing or outdated contact information

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the contacts might have been accidentally deleted by looking in the Trash or Deleted Documents folder within the contacts database, if available
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Accidentally deleted contacts can sometimes be quickly recovered directly from a trash folder before it is permanently emptied

troubleshootingSteps.action: If personal contacts appear to be missing due to potential local database corruption, run a Fixup and Compact operation on the local names.nsf file
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This can repair underlying database corruption that might be causing contacts to not display correctly

troubleshootingSteps.action: For missing corporate directory contacts, confirm with the Notes administrator that the directory synchronization or lookup service is functioning correctly on the server side
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Corporate directory listings depend on a server-side process that is outside of the individual user's local contacts database

troubleshootingSteps.action: As a precaution going forward, periodically export important personal contacts to a backup file
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides an additional safety net in case contacts are lost again due to accidental deletion or database issues

possibleSolutions: Manually trigger and confirm successful contacts replication
Recover accidentally deleted contacts from the trash folder
Repair a corrupted local contacts database using Fixup and Compact
Have the administrator check corporate directory synchronization
Periodically back up personal contacts as a precaution
prevention: Ensure regular, successful replication of the contacts database
Periodically back up personal contacts
Be cautious when performing bulk deletions in the contacts database
Report corporate directory sync issues to IT promptly

problem: Mail archiving fails or does not complete
description: The user tries to archive older emails to reduce the size of their mail file, but the archiving process fails, shows an error, or does not actually move the expected messages to the archive.
symptoms: Error message when trying to run the archive process
Archive process starts but does not complete
Emails remain in the main mail file even after archiving appears to run
Archive database is not created or cannot be found afterward
possibleCauses: Insufficient disk space for creating or updating the archive database
Archive settings are misconfigured, such as an incorrect archive criteria or destination
The archive database itself has become corrupted
Interrupted archiving due to a crash or forced closure during the process
Insufficient permissions to create or write to the archive location
diagnosticQuestions: What exact error message appears when archiving fails, if any?
Do you know how much free disk space is currently available on this computer?
Have you successfully archived mail before, or is this your first attempt?
Where is the archive database supposed to be located, and does that location still exist and is accessible?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available free disk space on the computer, since archiving requires enough room to create or expand the archive database
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient disk space is one of the most common and straightforward reasons an archiving process fails partway through

troubleshootingSteps.action: Free up disk space if it is low, then attempt the archiving process again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly addresses a lack of storage space, which is required for the archive operation to complete successfully

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review your archive settings under File > Preferences > Archive to confirm the criteria and destination location are correctly configured
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Misconfigured settings, such as an invalid destination path, can prevent archiving from working correctly even with sufficient disk space

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the archive database location still exists and that you have write permissions to it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: If the intended archive folder has been moved, deleted, or permissions have changed, archiving will fail to create or update the archive file there

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the archive process was interrupted by a crash or forced closure previously, check the existing archive database for corruption using Fixup and Compact
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An interrupted archiving operation can leave the archive database in a partially corrupted state that needs repair before further archiving can succeed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try running the archive process again, allowing it to complete fully without interruption, ideally when the computer will not need to be restarted or closed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This avoids repeating the same interruption issue that may have caused the original failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: If archiving continues to fail despite these steps, contact the Notes administrator, since some archive configurations are managed at a company policy level and may need administrator adjustment
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Corporate archive policies are sometimes centrally configured, and only an administrator can correct certain settings

possibleSolutions: Free up disk space before archiving
Correct misconfigured archive settings and destination
Restore or recreate access to a missing archive location
Repair a corrupted archive database using Fixup and Compact
Allow the archive process to run uninterrupted
Contact the administrator for centrally managed archive policy issues
prevention: Regularly check and maintain adequate free disk space
Avoid interrupting the archiving process once started
Periodically verify archive settings remain correctly configured
Schedule archiving during times when the computer will not need to restart

description: The user receives an email with an attachment, but when trying to open it, Notes shows an error, the attachment fails to launch, or the associated program does not open the file correctly.
symptoms: Error message when double-clicking the attachment
Attachment icon appears but nothing happens when opened
Associated program opens but shows the file as corrupted or unreadable
Attachment opens correctly for some file types but not others
possibleCauses: The file type of the attachment is blocked by security policy
No program is installed on the computer that can open this specific file type
The attachment itself is corrupted
Antivirus software is blocking or quarantining the attachment
The attachment did not fully download or transfer correctly
diagnosticQuestions: What is the file type of the attachment, such as .pdf, .docx, or .exe?
Does this happen with all attachments, or just this specific one or specific file types?
Is there a specific error message, or does nothing happen at all when trying to open it?
Do you have a program installed that is normally used to open this type of file?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the exact file type (extension) of the attachment to understand what program should normally be used to open it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps confirm whether an appropriate program is even available on the computer to handle this specific file type

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try saving the attachment to the computer first using right-click > Save As, then open the saved file directly rather than opening it straight from within Notes
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Opening a saved local copy sometimes works even when direct opening from within the email fails, and also helps isolate whether the issue is with Notes or the file itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm that a program capable of opening this specific file type is installed on the computer, and install one if needed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Notes relies on other installed programs to actually open most attachment types, and a missing program will cause the attachment to fail to open properly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if certain file types, such as executable (.exe) or script files, are being blocked by a company security policy
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many organizations intentionally block potentially dangerous attachment types as a security measure, which is expected behavior rather than a malfunction

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check antivirus quarantine logs to see if the attachment was automatically flagged and blocked or removed as a security precaution
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Antivirus software sometimes silently blocks or quarantines attachments it considers suspicious, which can appear to the user as the attachment simply failing to open

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the attachment appears corrupted, contact the original sender and ask them to resend it, ideally checking the file opens correctly on their end first
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This confirms whether the problem originated with the file itself before it was even sent, which the sender can verify

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a legitimate business file type is being blocked by company policy and is genuinely needed, contact the Notes or IT administrator to discuss a possible policy exception
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Legitimate business needs for otherwise-blocked file types typically require formal administrator review and approval

possibleSolutions: Save the attachment locally before opening it
Install the appropriate program for the specific file type
Understand and work within company security policies blocking certain file types
Recover a mistakenly quarantined attachment from antivirus logs
Request the sender resend a corrupted attachment
Request a policy exception from IT for legitimate blocked file types
prevention: Keep appropriate programs installed for commonly received file types
Understand your organization's attachment security policies
Confirm large or unusual attachments with the sender before assuming a technical fault
Keep antivirus software properly configured to minimize false positives

problem: Encryption error when opening or sending mail
description: The user tries to open an encrypted email, or send a message using encryption, but receives an error preventing the encryption or decryption process from completing successfully.
symptoms: Error message such as 'You are not able to decrypt this document'
Encrypted email cannot be opened even though it was clearly sent to the correct recipient
Error when trying to send an email using encryption
Encryption-related errors mentioning certificates or public keys
possibleCauses: The recipient's public key is missing from the sender's address book, preventing proper encryption
The local ID file used for decryption is corrupted or outdated
The email was encrypted using a certificate that has since expired or been replaced
The user is trying to open the encrypted email using a different ID file than the one it was originally encrypted for
A mismatch between the sender's and recipient's security certificates
diagnosticQuestions: Are you trying to open an email someone sent you, or trying to send an encrypted email yourself?
What is the exact error message shown?
Have you successfully opened encrypted emails from this same sender before?
Has your Notes ID file been recently reissued, restored, or changed?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact error message and whether the problem is with sending or receiving encrypted mail
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This distinguishes between an issue with your own ID and certificates versus an issue related to the sender's encryption setup

troubleshootingSteps.action: If trying to send an encrypted email, confirm that the recipient's public key (certificate) is present and current in your address book
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Notes requires the recipient's public key to properly encrypt a message specifically for them, and a missing or outdated key will cause the encryption process to fail

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the recipient's key is missing or outdated, request an updated business card or public key from them, or look them up again in the corporate directory if available
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides the current, correct key needed to successfully encrypt future messages to that recipient

troubleshootingSteps.action: If trying to open an encrypted email you received, confirm you are logged in with the correct ID file that the message was originally encrypted for
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An encrypted email can only be decrypted using the specific matching private key from the correct ID file, and using a different or newly issued ID will cause decryption to fail

troubleshootingSteps.action: If your ID file was recently reissued or restored from a backup, be aware that older encrypted emails may only be decryptable with your previous key information, which should typically be included when an ID is properly reissued with key history
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This explains a specific and common cause of being unable to open older encrypted emails after an ID file change

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the Notes or Domino administrator if a decryption failure persists, since they can check your ID file's key history and certificate status
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Certificate and key history issues typically require administrator-level tools to properly diagnose and correct

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the issue is related to an expired certificate, work with the administrator to renew or reissue the necessary certificates
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Expired certificates need to be formally renewed through the organization's certificate authority process, which is managed by the Domino administrator

possibleSolutions: Obtain an updated public key or business card from the recipient before sending encrypted mail
Confirm you are using the correct ID file to decrypt received mail
Have the administrator check your ID's key history after a reissue
Renew expired certificates through the Domino administrator
Contact the administrator for persistent decryption failures
prevention: Regularly update contacts' public keys in your address book
Keep track of certificate expiration dates
Ensure key history is preserved when an ID file is reissued
Coordinate with IT before making major changes to your Notes ID

problem: Database permission denied for a specific action
description: The user can open a database but is denied permission when trying to perform a specific action within it, such as creating a new document, editing an existing one, or deleting content.
symptoms: Error message such as 'You do not have sufficient access to perform this operation'
Certain buttons or menu options appear greyed out or missing
Can view documents but cannot edit or create new ones
Permission works for some documents within the database but not others
possibleCauses: The user's access control list (ACL) role allows reading but not editing or creating documents
Specific documents have additional reader or author field restrictions beyond the general database ACL
The user's role was recently changed to a more restricted level
A form or view has design-level restrictions limiting certain actions to specific roles
diagnosticQuestions: What specific action were you trying to perform when the permission was denied, such as creating, editing, or deleting?
Does this happen with all documents in the database, or just specific ones?
Have you been able to perform this same action successfully before?
Do you know what access level (such as Reader, Author, or Editor) you currently have in this database?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact action being denied and whether it happens with all documents or just specific ones
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps distinguish between a general database-level ACL restriction and a more specific document-level reader/author field restriction

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your current access level for the database, if visible, through File > Application > Access Control, or ask the administrator to confirm
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly shows whether your assigned role, such as Reader or Author, actually supports the action you are trying to perform

troubleshootingSteps.action: If your role is Reader but you need to create or edit documents, request an upgrade to Author or Editor access from the database owner or administrator
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reader access intentionally only allows viewing, and creating or editing requires a higher assigned role

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the restriction happens only with specific documents, check if those documents have special Reader or Author field restrictions applied at the document level, separate from the general database ACL
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Individual documents can have additional field-based access restrictions that override the general database-wide access level for that specific content

troubleshootingSteps.action: If document-level restrictions seem to be the cause, contact the document's creator or the database administrator to request being added to the appropriate reader or author field for that content
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly addresses restrictions that exist beyond the general database ACL and require adjustment at the individual document or form design level

troubleshootingSteps.action: If your access level was recently reduced unexpectedly, ask the administrator if this was an intentional change or possibly an error
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Understanding whether this is intentional helps determine the appropriate next step, whether requesting a policy exception or reporting a mistake

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once updated permissions are granted, close and reopen the database to ensure the new access level is properly recognized
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the change takes full effect within your current Notes session

possibleSolutions: Request an appropriate access level upgrade from the database owner or administrator
Request inclusion in document-level reader/author field restrictions where needed
Confirm whether a reduced access level was intentional or a mistake
Reopen the database after permission changes to apply them
prevention: Confirm the correct access level is assigned when first granted database access
Understand the difference between database-level ACL and document-level field restrictions
Communicate access needs clearly to database owners

problem: A company-specific application will not open within Notes
description: The user tries to open a custom business application built on the Notes platform, such as a timesheet or approval system, but the application fails to open or shows an error specific to that application.
symptoms: Error message specific to the custom application when trying to open it
Application icon exists but clicking it produces no response
Application opens but shows a blank or broken interface
Other standard Notes functions, like mail, continue to work normally
possibleCauses: The custom application database has been moved, renamed, or is temporarily unavailable
The user lacks the correct access permissions specifically for this application
A recent update to the application introduced a bug or compatibility issue
The application relies on a specific Notes client version or configuration that is not currently met
The underlying database for the application has become corrupted
diagnosticQuestions: What is the exact name of the custom application experiencing the problem?
Does this happen only with this specific application, while mail and other standard functions work fine?
Have you used this application successfully before, or is this your first time?
Do other coworkers who use the same application have the same problem right now?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the exact name of the custom application and note the specific error message, if any
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Custom applications can have very specific issues, and precise details are essential for the administrator or application support team to diagnose the problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if other coworkers who use the same application are currently experiencing the same issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is isolated to your account or computer, or represents a broader application-wide issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm your standard Notes functions, such as mail, continue to work normally
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps isolate whether the problem is specific to this one application, or part of a wider Notes client or connectivity issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try opening the application from a bookmark or shortcut rather than a workspace icon, or vice versa, to rule out a broken specific link
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Sometimes only one specific access point to the application is broken, while an alternative path still works correctly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if there has been a recent update or change announced for this specific application by the internal team responsible for it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Custom applications are often maintained by an internal development or business team who may be aware of recent, relevant changes

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the internal team or department responsible for maintaining this specific custom application, since they typically handle its unique support separate from general Notes/IT support
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Custom business applications often have their own dedicated support contacts who understand the application's specific design and common issues

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the responsible team is unavailable or unknown, escalate through the general Notes or IT administrator, who can direct the issue appropriately or investigate underlying database health
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The Notes administrator can at minimum check the general health and accessibility of the underlying database, even if they are not the application's primary business owner

possibleSolutions: Report the specific application and error details to its responsible internal team
Try an alternative access point (bookmark versus workspace icon) to the application
Escalate through the general Notes/IT administrator if the responsible team is unknown
Wait for a known application issue to be resolved by its maintaining team
prevention: Keep a record of who is responsible for supporting each custom Notes application
Report custom application issues promptly with specific error details
Stay informed of planned updates to frequently used custom applications

problem: Lotus Notes is running slowly overall
description: The user finds that Lotus Notes generally feels sluggish, with delays when opening emails, switching folders, or performing everyday tasks, even without a specific error or crash occurring.
symptoms: Noticeable delay when opening emails or switching between folders
Typing or scrolling within Notes feels laggy
Opening the application itself takes longer than usual
Slowness may be constant or worsen over the course of the day
possibleCauses: A very large mail file that has not been archived recently
Outdated or fragmented local view indexes
A slow or degraded network connection to the Domino server
Insufficient system memory or an outdated computer for current Notes requirements
Antivirus software actively scanning Notes data files in real time
Too many databases or replicas configured to sync simultaneously
diagnosticQuestions: How large is your mail file currently, and when was it last archived?
Does the slowness happen with all databases, or mainly with mail specifically?
Are you connected to the office network directly, or working remotely?
Does slowness happen consistently throughout the day, or does it seem to build up over time?

commands.purpose: Check overall CPU, memory, and disk usage to see if Notes or another process is consuming excessive resources
commands.expectedResult: Reasonable resource usage consistent with normal Notes operation
commands.abnormalResult: Notes or a related process shows unusually high, sustained resource usage, pointing to a specific performance bottleneck

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the current size of your mail file and compare it to your organization's recommended size before performance issues typically begin
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An oversized mail file is one of the most common and significant causes of general Notes slowness

troubleshootingSteps.action: Archive older emails to reduce your mail file size if it has grown very large
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reducing the active mail file size directly improves indexing, opening, and general performance

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your network connection quality to the Domino server, especially if working remotely over VPN
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A slow or unstable network connection can make Notes feel sluggish even when the client and databases themselves are healthy

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Task Manager for overall CPU, memory, and disk usage while using Notes to identify if system resources are a limiting factor
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the slowness is related to Notes itself, or a broader resource constraint on the computer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the Notes data directory is properly excluded from real-time antivirus scanning
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Antivirus software actively scanning large Notes database files during normal use is a common but often overlooked cause of ongoing slowness

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review how many databases and replicas are configured to synchronize automatically, and consider reducing unnecessary ones
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Excessive simultaneous replication activity can consume significant system and network resources, slowing down the overall Notes experience

troubleshootingSteps.action: Rebuild view indexes for frequently used, large databases, including your mail file
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Outdated or fragmented view indexes can significantly slow down how quickly Notes can display folder contents and search results

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the computer itself is old or has limited memory, consider whether a hardware upgrade might be needed to meet current Notes client requirements
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Notes client requirements can increase with newer versions, and older hardware may simply struggle to keep up regardless of software optimization

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the Notes administrator if slowness persists despite these steps, since server-side performance or configuration issues may also be contributing
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some performance factors, such as server load or network infrastructure, are outside what an individual user can diagnose or resolve alone

possibleSolutions: Archive older emails to reduce mail file size
Improve network connection quality, especially for remote users
Exclude Notes data files from real-time antivirus scanning
Reduce unnecessary simultaneous database replication
Rebuild view indexes for large, frequently used databases
Upgrade computer hardware if it no longer meets current requirements
Contact the administrator for potential server-side performance factors
prevention: Archive mail regularly to keep file size manageable
Maintain a stable, reasonably fast network connection
Keep antivirus exclusions properly configured for Notes
Periodically review and clean up unnecessary database replicas
Keep computer hardware reasonably current for the Notes client version in use

description: The user is unable to send or receive new mail because their mail file has reached or exceeded the storage quota set by the Domino administrator.
symptoms: Warning message that the mailbox is over quota
New incoming mail is bounced back to senders as undeliverable
User cannot send mail, sometimes with an over-quota error
Mail file size shown in properties is at or above the assigned limit
possibleCauses: Mail file quota set too low for the user's mail volume
Large attachments accumulated in the mail file over time
Old mail not archived or deleted regularly
Quota warning threshold not acted on before hitting the hard limit
diagnosticQuestions: Does the user receive an over-quota warning when opening Notes?
How large is the mail file compared to the assigned quota?
Are there large attachments or old messages that could be archived?
Has the quota been recently lowered by policy, or has usage grown?

commands.purpose: Check current mail file size versus assigned quota and warning threshold
commands.expectedResult: Shows mail file size below the quota and warning threshold
commands.abnormalResult: Size shown at or above the quota limit, confirming the cause of the block

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check mail file size and quota in File > Mail File Properties.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the user is actually at or over the assigned limit.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Archive or delete old emails and large attachments to reduce mail file size.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Frees space so the mail file drops below the quota.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Empty the Trash folder after deleting items.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Deleted documents still count against quota until the Trash is emptied.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If usage is consistently high, request a quota increase from the Domino administrator.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some users legitimately need a higher quota based on job function.

possibleSolutions: Archive old mail to a local or server archive
Delete large attachments and empty Trash
Request a quota increase from the administrator
Set up an automatic archive policy for future mail growth
prevention: Archive mail on a regular schedule
Monitor mail file size periodically
Set realistic quotas based on user role
Educate users to remove large attachments after saving them locally

description: A user's mail file has grown very large over time, causing performance issues, slow replication, and difficulty backing up or maintaining the database, even if it has not yet hit a hard quota.
symptoms: Mail file size significantly larger than typical for the organization
Slow opening, searching, and replication of the mail file
Backups of the mail file take unusually long
User is approaching but has not yet exceeded quota
possibleCauses: Years of accumulated mail without archiving
Large attachments stored directly in the mail file instead of a shared location
Duplicate or unnecessary replicas increasing effective size
No archive policy configured for the user
diagnosticQuestions: When was the mail file last archived, if ever?
Does the user regularly receive or send large attachments?
Is an archive policy currently configured for this user?
How does the file size compare to the organization's typical mail file size?

commands.purpose: View current mail file size and compare to organizational norms
commands.expectedResult: Size within expected range for normal usage
commands.abnormalResult: Size well above typical range, confirming the file needs archiving or cleanup

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review mail file size and identify the largest folders or documents.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Pinpoints where the bulk of the size is coming from before taking action.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Set up or run an archive to move older mail out of the active file.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reduces active file size while preserving historical mail for reference.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Encourage the user to detach and store large attachments outside of Notes.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Attachments are often the largest contributor to mail file bloat.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Compact the mail file after cleanup using administrator tools.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reclaims unused space left behind after documents are deleted or archived.

possibleSolutions: Configure and run a scheduled archive policy
Manually archive and delete old mail
Move large attachments to shared storage
Have the administrator compact the mail file
prevention: Set up automatic archive policies for all users
Educate users on managing large attachments
Periodically review mail file sizes organization-wide
Schedule regular database compaction

description: When the user attempts to open their mail, Notes reports that the mail file cannot be found, or the mail icon/bookmark leads to an error indicating the database does not exist at the expected path.
symptoms: Error stating the database does not exist or cannot be found
Mail bookmark or icon fails to open anything
New Notes installation shows no mail file configured
Mail file exists on server but local replica or path reference is broken
possibleCauses: Mail file was moved, renamed, or deleted on the server
Local replica was deleted or corrupted and bookmark still points to it
Incorrect mail file path configured in the user's Person document
User's Notes client was recently reinstalled without reconfiguring mail
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen only locally, or also when accessing mail via webmail/other devices?
Was the Notes client recently reinstalled or the computer replaced?
Has the user's mail file been moved to a different server recently?
What is the exact error message shown when trying to open mail?

commands.purpose: Manually browse the server for the user's mail file to verify it exists and locate its path
commands.expectedResult: Mail file is found on the expected server and path
commands.abnormalResult: Mail file cannot be located, indicating it was moved, renamed, or deleted

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify the mail file exists on the server by browsing via File > Application > Open.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the issue is a broken local reference or an actual missing server file.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the user's Person document in the Domino Directory for the correct mail server and file path.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect path in the Person document will cause Notes to look in the wrong location.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the local replica is broken, delete it and create a fresh replica from the server copy.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A corrupted local replica reference can be resolved by re-replicating from the authoritative server file.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the server file is genuinely missing, restore it from the most recent backup.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Backup restoration is required when the mail file no longer exists anywhere.

possibleSolutions: Correct the mail file path in the Person document
Recreate the local replica from the server
Restore the mail file from backup if deleted
Reconfigure the Notes client's mail location settings
prevention: Avoid manually moving or renaming mail files without updating the Person document
Maintain regular backups of mail files
Follow proper procedures when reinstalling Notes clients
Document any server migrations affecting mail file locations

description: When provisioning a new user or restoring mail access, the administrator or system fails to create a new mail file, returning an error during the mail file creation process.
symptoms: Error during user registration indicating mail file creation failed
New user has a Person document but no mail file on the server
Administrator receives an access denied or path error when creating the mail file
Mail file creation process hangs or times out
possibleCauses: Insufficient disk space on the target mail server
Administrator lacks sufficient rights on the target server's mail directory
Mail template (mail10.ntf or similar) is missing, corrupted, or wrong version
Naming conflict with an existing file at the target path
diagnosticQuestions: What exact error message appears during mail file creation?
Is there sufficient free disk space on the target mail server?
Does the administrator account have Manager access on the mail directory?
Is the correct, uncorrupted mail template available on the server?

commands.purpose: Refresh or repair a mail file's design against the current mail template from the Domino server console
commands.expectedResult: Mail file design updates successfully against the template
commands.abnormalResult: Errors indicating the template or file could not be accessed, pointing to permissions or corruption

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available disk space on the target mail server.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient space is a common and easily overlooked cause of failed database creation.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the administrator account has Manager access rights on the server's mail directory.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Creating a new database requires sufficient server access rights.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify the mail template file is present and not corrupted on the server.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Mail file creation depends on a valid template to build the initial database structure.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Retry the mail file creation using the Domino Administrator client's registration or file creation tools.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Once the underlying cause is resolved, a fresh attempt should succeed.

possibleSolutions: Free up disk space on the mail server
Grant proper administrator rights on the target directory
Replace or repair a corrupted mail template
Retry mail file creation through Domino Administrator
prevention: Monitor server disk space proactively
Maintain proper administrator access rights documentation
Keep mail templates up to date and verified
Test mail file creation in a staging environment after template updates

problem: Mail File Moved to Another Server
description: A user's mail file was migrated or moved to a different Domino server, but the client, Person document, or bookmarks still point to the old server, causing errors or inability to access mail.
symptoms: Notes attempts to connect to the old mail server and fails
Error indicating the server cannot be contacted or the database is not found there
Mail works from webmail on the new server but not from the desktop client
Local replication fails after the server move
possibleCauses: Person document not updated with the new mail server after migration
Local Notes client location document still references the old server
Local replica stub still points to the old server path
Replication or migration process incomplete
diagnosticQuestions: Was a mail file migration or server consolidation recently performed?
Does the Person document reflect the new mail server name?
Can the user access mail through webmail on the new server?
Is the local replica configured to point to the old server?

commands.purpose: Check which server the current mail replica or bookmark is pointing to
commands.expectedResult: Shows the correct, current mail server
commands.abnormalResult: Shows the old server, confirming the bookmark or replica needs to be updated

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the Person document has been updated with the new mail server name.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the authoritative source Notes uses to locate the user's mail file.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update or recreate the mail bookmark to point to the new server location.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Old bookmarks retain references to the previous server even after the Person document is updated.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Delete the outdated local replica and create a new one from the current server.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures the local copy replicates against the correct, current source database.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Refresh the user's Notes client location document if it manually references the old server.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some configurations hardcode server names in the location document, overriding directory lookups.

possibleSolutions: Update the Person document with the new server
Recreate mail bookmarks and local replicas
Update location document server references
Re-run directory synchronization if changes have not propagated
prevention: Follow a complete migration checklist including Person document updates
Communicate server moves to affected users in advance
Verify client-side access after any server migration
Allow directory replication to fully propagate before considering a migration complete

description: Emails sent from or to Notes users take significantly longer than usual to arrive, ranging from several minutes to hours, without an outright failure.
symptoms: Emails arrive noticeably later than expected
Delay affects internal mail, external mail, or both
Message tracking shows the mail sitting in a queue for an extended period
Delay may be intermittent or consistently affecting all mail
possibleCauses: Router task on the Domino server is overloaded or backed up
Mail.box is congested with a large volume of messages
Network latency or connectivity issues between mail servers
A downstream relay or gateway server is slow or unresponsive
Transfer or routing schedule settings causing batched delivery
diagnosticQuestions: Does the delay affect all mail, or only mail to/from specific servers or domains?
Has message tracking been checked to see where the delay is occurring?
Has mail volume increased significantly recently?
Are there known network issues between the sending and receiving servers?

commands.purpose: Show current mail queues and pending message counts on the Domino server console
commands.expectedResult: Queues are empty or processing normally with low counts
commands.abnormalResult: Large or growing queue counts indicating a routing bottleneck

commands.purpose: Verify the Router task is running on the Domino server console
commands.expectedResult: Router task is listed as active
commands.abnormalResult: Router task is missing or not responding, requiring a restart

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use message tracking to identify where in the routing path the delay is occurring.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Pinpoints whether the bottleneck is local, at a relay, or on the receiving end.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check mail queues on the server console for backlog.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A large backlog indicates the router cannot keep pace with incoming volume.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the Router task is active and responsive.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A stalled or crashed router task will cause mail to back up without being delivered.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check network connectivity and latency between affected mail servers.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Slow or unstable network links directly cause routing delays between servers.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review scheduled transfer and routing intervals for affected mail routes.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some routes may be configured for scheduled rather than immediate delivery, causing apparent delay.

possibleSolutions: Restart the Router task if it is unresponsive
Increase server resources if consistently overloaded
Resolve underlying network connectivity issues
Adjust scheduled routing intervals to more frequent delivery
Escalate to network team if latency is between sites
prevention: Monitor mail queues and router performance proactively
Set up alerts for queue backlog thresholds
Maintain adequate server resources for mail volume
Regularly review routing topology and schedules

description: Mail has completely stopped moving between Domino servers or out to the internet; messages remain queued indefinitely and no mail is being delivered.
symptoms: No mail is being delivered internally or externally
Mail.box shows a growing number of undelivered messages
Users report no new mail arriving for an extended period
Server console shows routing errors or no router activity
possibleCauses: Router task has crashed or was manually stopped
Mail.box database is corrupted and cannot be processed
Connection document misconfiguration between servers
DNS or network failure preventing server-to-server communication

description: A view's underlying index becomes corrupted, causing incorrect document counts, missing documents, errors when opening the view, or repeated failures even after refresh attempts.
symptoms: Error message when attempting to open a specific view

Documents known to exist do not appear despite refreshing

possibleCauses: Improper server or client shutdown while the view index was being updated

diagnosticQuestions: Does the error occur consistently every time this specific view is opened?
Was there a recent server crash or improper shutdown?

commands.purpose: Force a full rebuild of all view indexes to attempt to resolve corruption
commands.expectedResult: Indexes rebuild successfully and the view opens and displays correctly
commands.abnormalResult: Rebuild fails or the view remains broken, indicating underlying database corruption requiring Fixup or Compact

commands.purpose: Repair structural corruption in the database that may be affecting the view index
commands.expectedResult: Fixup completes and reports the database has been repaired
commands.abnormalResult: Fixup reports unresolved corruption, requiring restoration from backup

troubleshootingSteps.action: Attempt to rebuild the view index using load updall -R against the database.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the standard first step to resolve most view index corruption without deeper database repair.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the view still fails, run Fixup against the database to check for and repair structural corruption.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Fixup addresses corruption at the database level that a simple index rebuild cannot fix.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run Compact on the database after Fixup completes successfully.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Compact reclaims space and can resolve additional issues left after structural repair.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If corruption persists, restore the database from the most recent clean backup.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Severe corruption that Fixup cannot resolve typically requires restoring a known-good copy.

possibleSolutions: Rebuild view indexes with updall -R
Run Fixup and Compact on the affected database
Simplify an overly complex view formula if identified as a factor
Restore the database from backup if corruption is unresolved
prevention: Ensure clean server and client shutdowns whenever possible
Schedule regular Fixup and Compact maintenance tasks
Monitor disk health on servers hosting critical databases
Avoid overly complex view selection formulas where simpler alternatives exist

Agent's signer ID has expired or lacks necessary server access
