diagnosticQuestions: Does the agent fail every time, or only under certain conditions?
What does the agent log show when the failure occurs?
Is the agent signed by a user or ID with adequate access rights on the server?
Has the server's agent security list (restricted/unrestricted) been recently modified?

commands.purpose: Display the current agent manager schedule from the server console to confirm the agent is queued to run
commands.expectedResult: Agent appears correctly scheduled
commands.abnormalResult: Agent does not appear in the schedule, indicating a scheduling or security configuration issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the agent log for specific error details from the failed run.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The log typically provides the exact line or reason for failure, focusing troubleshooting efforts.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify the agent's signer has sufficient access rights on the server, particularly for restricted operations.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Agents run with the rights of their signer, and insufficient rights are a common cause of silent or explicit failures.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the server's Security document to confirm the signer is on the appropriate restricted or unrestricted agent list.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Server security settings can block agents from running certain operations even with a valid signer.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the agent's code for runtime errors, such as referencing a document field that may not exist.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Code-level bugs are a frequent cause of agents failing partway through execution.

possibleSolutions: Re-sign the agent with an ID that has sufficient rights
Add the signer to the appropriate server agent security list
Fix the underlying code error causing the runtime failure
Adjust agent trigger settings if scheduling is the root cause
prevention: Test agents thoroughly in a non-production environment before deployment
Maintain proper signer ID management and renewal schedules
Document required server security settings for critical agents
Review agent logs periodically even when agents appear to be working

description: An agent configured to run on a schedule, such as hourly or daily, does not execute at its expected time, leaving its intended automation unperformed.
symptoms: Agent's scheduled actions never occur at the expected time
Agent log shows no recent execution entries
Agent manager statistics show the agent as disabled or not scheduled
Manually running the agent works fine, but the schedule does not trigger it
possibleCauses: Agent Manager task is not running on the server
Agent's schedule setting was disabled or misconfigured
Server's agent execution time window excludes the agent's scheduled time
Database containing the agent is not enabled for scheduled agent execution on this server
diagnosticQuestions: Is the Agent Manager (amgr) task currently running on the server?
What schedule is configured for the agent, and does it match expectations?
Are there server-level restrictions on agent execution time windows?
Is the database's server correctly set to allow scheduled agents to run?

commands.purpose: View the current schedule of agents managed by the Agent Manager task
commands.expectedResult: The agent appears in the schedule with the expected next run time
commands.abnormalResult: The agent is missing from the schedule, indicating a configuration or Agent Manager issue

commands.purpose: Confirm the Agent Manager (AMgr) task is currently running on the server
commands.expectedResult: AMgr is listed as an active task
commands.abnormalResult: AMgr is not listed, meaning no scheduled agents will execute until it is restarted

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the Agent Manager task is running on the server using show tasks.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: No scheduled agents can run at all if the Agent Manager task itself is not active.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the agent's schedule settings in Designer to confirm they match the intended trigger time and frequency.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrectly configured schedule will simply never trigger the agent as expected.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the server document for any agent execution time restrictions that might exclude the scheduled time.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some servers restrict scheduled agent execution to specific windows, which can silently prevent agents from running.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify the database is hosted on a server enabled for running scheduled agents.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some servers are configured to disallow scheduled agent execution entirely for performance or policy reasons.

possibleSolutions: Restart the Agent Manager task if it is not running
Correct the agent's schedule configuration
Adjust server-level agent execution time restrictions
Move the database to a server that supports scheduled agent execution
prevention: Monitor Agent Manager task status with automated alerts
Document expected agent schedules for reference during troubleshooting
Review server agent restrictions periodically
Test scheduled agents after any server migration or reconfiguration

description: A button on a form or view in a Notes application does not perform its intended action when clicked, either doing nothing, throwing an error, or performing the wrong action.
symptoms: Clicking the button produces no visible effect
An error message appears when the button is clicked
Button performs an unexpected or outdated action
Button works for some users but not others
possibleCauses: Button's underlying formula or script contains an error
User lacks sufficient access rights for the action the button performs
Local design cache is outdated, running an old version of the button code
Button relies on a field, agent, or other design element that has since changed or been removed
diagnosticQuestions: Does the button fail for all users or only specific ones?
Is there an error message, and if so, what does it say exactly?
Was the button's code recently modified?
Does the affected user have appropriate ACL access for the intended action?

commands.purpose: Refresh the database design to ensure the button is running its current, intended code
commands.expectedResult: Button behavior matches the current design after refresh
commands.abnormalResult: Button still fails after refresh, pointing to a genuine code or access rights issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact error message, if any, when the button is clicked.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Specific error text often points directly to the failing line of formula or script.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Refresh the local design cache by closing and reopening the database.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves cases where the client is running an outdated cached version of the button's code.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the affected user's ACL access level against what the button's action requires.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient access rights will cause certain button actions, such as document creation or field updates, to silently fail.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Open the button in Designer and review its formula or script for errors or outdated references.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly identifies bugs or broken references to other design elements that may have changed.

possibleSolutions: Fix the underlying formula or script error in the button
Adjust the user's ACL access level appropriately
Refresh local design caches for affected users
Update the button to reference current, valid design elements
prevention: Test button actions across different user access levels before deployment
Use version control and testing for design changes
Document required ACL levels for key application actions
Refresh design caches after significant application updates

description: A user attempts to save a document in a Notes application, but the save fails, either silently, with an error message, or by reverting to the previous state after appearing to save.
symptoms: Error message indicating the document could not be saved
Save appears to complete but changes are not actually persisted
Document reverts to its prior state after closing and reopening
Issue occurs consistently for one user or one specific document
possibleCauses: User does not have sufficient ACL access (at least Author rights) to save the document
A validation formula on the form is silently blocking the save
The document is locked by another user or process
Insufficient disk space on the server hosting the database
diagnosticQuestions: Does the user have at least Author access with Create/Edit rights in the database ACL?
Is there an error message, or does the save simply appear to have no effect?
Could a required field be failing validation without a clear error shown?
Is there sufficient free disk space on the server hosting this database?

commands.command: File > Application > Access Control (Notes client, if administrator)
commands.purpose: Check the user's current access level in the database ACL
commands.expectedResult: User has Author access or higher with appropriate create/edit rights
commands.abnormalResult: User has Reader access or lower, explaining why the save is blocked

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the database ACL to confirm the user has sufficient access to create or edit documents.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient ACL access is one of the most common causes of a document failing to save.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the form for validation formulas that might be silently preventing the save.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A validation formula failing without a clear message can appear as if the save simply is not working.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check whether the document is currently locked by another user or session.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Document locking, if enabled, will prevent saves from other users while the lock is active.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify sufficient free disk space on the server hosting the database.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A server with no free disk space cannot write new or updated documents to the database.

possibleSolutions: Adjust the user's ACL access level appropriately
Fix or clarify the validation formula blocking the save
Release the document lock held by another user or session
Free up disk space on the hosting server
prevention: Set ACL access levels appropriately based on user roles
Provide clear error messages for validation formula failures
Monitor server disk space proactively
Educate users on document locking behavior where enabled

description: A user attempts to open or edit a document but is informed it is currently locked by another user, preventing edits even though the other user may no longer actually be working on it.
symptoms: Error message stating the document is locked by another user
User can view but not edit the document
Lock persists even after the other user has closed the document or logged off
Multiple users report being unable to edit the same document over time
possibleCauses: Document locking is enabled and another user genuinely has the document open for editing
A stale lock remains after the other user's session crashed or disconnected improperly
Document locking settings are misconfigured, causing locks to persist longer than intended
Replication conflict created an unexpected lock state
diagnosticQuestions: Is document locking intentionally enabled for this application?
Is the user who allegedly holds the lock currently active, or did their session end abnormally?
How long has the lock been in place?
Does this happen with one specific document or across many documents in the database?

commands.purpose: Refresh the database design in case a locking-related design element needs updating (used alongside manual lock review)
commands.expectedResult: No direct effect on locks, but confirms design is current before further troubleshooting
commands.abnormalResult: N/A - this step is primarily precautionary before manual lock investigation

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether the user holding the lock is still actively working on the document.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: If they are genuinely editing, the lock is functioning as intended and should not be forcibly removed.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check how long the lock has been active and whether the locking user's session ended abnormally.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A stale lock from a crashed session is the most common cause of a lock persisting incorrectly.

troubleshootingSteps.action: As an administrator, manually clear the document lock using administration tools if confirmed stale.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Removing a confirmed stale lock restores normal editing access without waiting for automatic expiration.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the database's document locking configuration if this occurs frequently.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Frequent stale locks may indicate a configuration issue, such as too long a lock timeout setting.

possibleSolutions: Wait for the legitimate lock holder to finish and release it
Manually clear a confirmed stale lock as an administrator
Adjust document locking timeout settings if stale locks recur often
Disable document locking for the application if it is not actually needed
prevention: Set reasonable lock timeout values for locking-enabled applications
Encourage users to close documents properly rather than force-closing sessions
Only enable document locking where genuinely necessary
Monitor for recurring stale lock patterns
keywords: document locked by another user notes

description: A computed field on a form shows an incorrect, outdated, or unexpected value rather than the result its formula should logically produce based on current document data.
symptoms: Computed field shows a value that does not match its formula logic
Field value does not update when related fields change
Field shows blank or an error indicator instead of a computed value
Issue appears only on certain documents, not all
possibleCauses: Field is set to compute only on document creation rather than recalculate on edit
Formula references a field that has been renamed, removed, or is empty
Local design cache is outdated, using a previous version of the formula
Circular or conflicting formula logic between multiple computed fields
diagnosticQuestions: Is the field set to 'Computed', 'Computed for display', or 'Computed when composed'?
Does the formula reference any fields that might be missing or renamed?
Does refreshing the document or design resolve the incorrect value?
Are there other computed fields whose formulas might interact with this one unexpectedly?

commands.purpose: Refresh the database design to ensure the computed field is using its current formula
commands.expectedResult: Field displays the correct computed value after refresh
commands.abnormalResult: Field still shows an incorrect value, pointing to a genuine formula logic issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the field's compute type, such as Computed, Computed for display, or Computed when composed.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The compute type determines when the formula runs, and a mismatch with expectations explains many apparent bugs.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the field's formula for references to other fields that may be missing, renamed, or blank.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A formula referencing an invalid or empty field will often produce blank or incorrect results.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Refresh the local design cache and reopen the affected document.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves cases where the client is displaying results based on an outdated cached formula.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test the formula in isolation using Designer's formula debugging tools if available.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps pinpoint exactly where the formula logic diverges from the expected result.

possibleSolutions: Change the field's compute type to match the intended behavior
Fix formula references to renamed or missing fields
Refresh design caches for affected users
Resolve conflicting logic between interacting computed fields
prevention: Document field compute types and dependencies during design
Test formulas thoroughly after renaming or removing fields
Use consistent naming conventions to avoid broken references
Review computed field logic when making related design changes

description: A document fails to save because a validation formula on the form determines that required conditions are not met, but the resulting error message is unclear or the condition itself may be incorrectly configured.
symptoms: Error message referencing a validation failure when attempting to save
User cannot identify which field or condition is causing the validation to fail
Validation blocks save even though the document appears correctly filled out
Issue occurs consistently for specific documents or field combinations
possibleCauses: Validation formula logic contains an error causing it to fail incorrectly
Required field referenced by the validation formula is blank or improperly formatted
Validation formula was recently changed and is stricter than intended
Hidden or computed fields involved in validation are not populating as expected
diagnosticQuestions: What exact validation error message is displayed?
Which field or fields does the validation formula check?
Was the validation formula recently added or modified?
Does the issue occur only with certain data entered, or in all cases?

commands.purpose: Refresh the database design to ensure the form is using its current validation formula
commands.expectedResult: Validation behaves as expected after refresh if the issue was cache-related
commands.abnormalResult: Validation still incorrectly blocks the save, indicating a genuine formula logic issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact validation error message and which field it references.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Pinpoints exactly which condition in the formula is failing, focusing further investigation.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Open the form in Designer and review the validation formula logic for the referenced field.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Allows direct inspection of whether the logic itself is correct or overly strict.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test saving the document with different sample data to isolate the exact triggering condition.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps confirm whether the validation is working as intended but simply needs correct data, or is genuinely broken.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct the validation formula logic if it is found to be inaccurate or overly restrictive.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly resolves the issue by aligning the validation with its intended business rule.

possibleSolutions: Correct the underlying validation formula logic
Ensure referenced fields are properly populated before save
Improve the validation error message for clarity
Refresh design caches if the issue was due to an outdated formula version
prevention: Write clear, specific error messages for validation formulas
Test validation formulas thoroughly with various data scenarios
Document the business rules behind each validation condition
Review validation logic when related fields are changed

description: The Domino server service or process is not running on the host machine, making all databases, mail routing, and directory services on that server completely unavailable.
symptoms: Users cannot connect to the server at all
Server does not respond to console commands or remote administration
Operating system service manager shows the Domino service as stopped
No server activity visible in logs since the stop occurred
possibleCauses: Service was manually stopped for maintenance and not restarted
Server crashed due to an unhandled error or resource exhaustion
Operating system-level issue prevented the service from continuing to run
Scheduled maintenance or patching process stopped the service unexpectedly
diagnosticQuestions: Was any planned maintenance or patching scheduled around the time the service stopped?
Does the operating system event log show any errors related to the Domino service?
Can the server be reached at the operating system level, such as via remote desktop or SSH?
Has this happened before, suggesting a recurring stability issue?

commands.purpose: Attempt to manually start the Domino server service on Windows
commands.expectedResult: Service starts successfully and the server becomes reachable
commands.abnormalResult: Service fails to start, requiring review of the operating system and Domino logs for the underlying cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm at the operating system level whether the Domino service is stopped or crashed.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes the exact current state before attempting any restart.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review operating system and Domino server logs for errors around the time the service stopped.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Log entries often reveal the specific cause, such as a crash, resource exhaustion, or manual stop.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Attempt to manually start the Domino service.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines whether the service can start cleanly now that the immediate cause may have passed.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the service fails to start, investigate underlying operating system issues such as disk space, memory, or corrupted files.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A failure to start often points to a deeper system-level problem that must be resolved first.

possibleSolutions: Manually restart the Domino server service
Resolve underlying operating system issues preventing startup
Free up system resources if exhaustion caused the crash
Escalate to the server or infrastructure team for persistent instability
prevention: Set up service monitoring and automated alerts for the Domino service
Schedule and communicate planned maintenance clearly
Maintain adequate system resources on the server
Configure automatic service restart on failure where appropriate

description: An attempt to start the Domino server fails, with the process terminating shortly after launch or reporting a startup error before reaching a normal operating state.
symptoms: Server process starts and then immediately terminates
Startup error message referencing a specific database, port, or configuration issue
Server console shows startup halting partway through initialization
Service remains in a stopped or failed state after each startup attempt
possibleCauses: Corrupted or locked system database, such as names.nsf or log.nsf, preventing startup
Port conflict with another process using the same network port
Server ID file is missing, corrupted, or password-protected without the password available
NOTES.INI misconfiguration introduced by a recent manual edit
diagnosticQuestions: What specific error message or log entry appears at the point startup fails?
Was any change made to NOTES.INI or system databases recently?
Is another process potentially using the same network port as Domino?
Is the server ID file present, accessible, and does its password (if any) match what is expected?

commands.purpose: Attempt to repair a corrupted log.nsf that may be preventing server startup
commands.expectedResult: Fixup completes and the server can subsequently start normally
commands.abnormalResult: Fixup fails or the server still cannot start, pointing to a different underlying cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the exact startup error message or console output at the point of failure.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Startup failures typically report a specific reason, which directs the rest of the troubleshooting.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for recent changes to NOTES.INI and review them for errors.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Manual configuration changes are a common and easily overlooked cause of startup failures.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify no other process is using the same network ports required by Domino.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Port conflicts will prevent the server from binding and completing startup.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the server ID file is present, valid, and its password is correctly configured if required.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A missing, corrupted, or inaccessible server ID will halt startup very early in the process.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run Fixup against critical system databases such as log.nsf if corruption is suspected.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Corrupted system databases required during initialization can prevent successful startup.

possibleSolutions: Correct NOTES.INI misconfiguration
Resolve port conflicts with other processes
Restore or reconfigure a valid server ID file
Repair corrupted system databases with Fixup
prevention: Back up NOTES.INI before making manual changes
Document and test configuration changes in a non-production environment first
Maintain secure, accessible backups of server ID files
Monitor for port conflicts when deploying new services on the same host

description: The Domino server consistently shows very high CPU utilization, causing slow response times for users and potentially triggering performance alerts, without a clear single cause immediately apparent.
symptoms: Server CPU usage consistently at or near 100%
Users experience slow response times across mail and applications
Specific server tasks show unusually high processing activity
High CPU usage may be constant or occur in recurring spikes
possibleCauses: A runaway or inefficient agent consuming excessive CPU
Full-text indexing or a large view rebuild running during peak hours
Excessive replication activity from too many concurrent replicas
A stuck or looping server task consuming CPU without completing
diagnosticQuestions: Which specific server task or process is consuming the most CPU?
Does high usage correlate with a specific time of day or recurring scheduled task?
Have any new agents or applications been deployed recently?
Is the high usage constant, or does it spike and then subside?

commands.purpose: List currently running server tasks to identify which one may be consuming excessive CPU
commands.expectedResult: Tasks are shown with normal, expected activity levels
commands.abnormalResult: A specific task shows unusually long-running or repeated activity, pointing to the source of high CPU usage

commands.purpose: Display current CPU utilization statistics from the server console
commands.expectedResult: CPU usage within normal operating range
commands.abnormalResult: CPU usage consistently very high, confirming the reported performance issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use show tasks to identify which server task is most active during the high CPU period.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Isolates the specific process responsible rather than treating the server as a whole black box.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if high CPU correlates with scheduled agents, indexing, or replication activity.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many high CPU incidents are tied to identifiable scheduled processes rather than random spikes.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review recently deployed agents or applications for inefficient loops or excessive processing.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: New or modified code is a common source of unexpected CPU consumption.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Adjust scheduling of resource-intensive tasks, such as indexing or large agents, to off-peak hours.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Redistributing load away from peak usage times reduces user-facing impact even if total CPU work is unchanged.

possibleSolutions: Fix or disable an inefficient runaway agent
Reschedule resource-intensive tasks to off-peak hours
Reduce unnecessary concurrent replication activity
Add server resources if sustained legitimate load has grown
prevention: Monitor CPU usage trends and set proactive alerts
Review new agents for performance impact before production deployment
Schedule maintenance-heavy tasks during low-usage windows
Periodically review and optimize high-traffic applications

description: The Domino server consumes an unusually high or steadily increasing amount of system memory, potentially leading to slowdowns, swapping, or eventual crashes if left unaddressed.

System begins swapping to disk, causing broader performance degradation
Server or specific tasks crash with out-of-memory related errors
Memory usage remains high even during periods of low user activity
possibleCauses: A memory leak in a specific server task, add-in, or agent
Excessive number of concurrent user sessions or open databases
NSD (Notes Shared Database) or cache settings configured too large for available hardware
A stuck process failing to release memory after completing its work
diagnosticQuestions: Does memory usage climb steadily over time, or spike suddenly?
Is the increase tied to a specific task, add-in, or time of day?
How does current memory usage compare to the server's total available memory?
Have any third-party add-ins been recently installed or updated?

commands.purpose: Check current free memory statistics from the Domino server console
commands.expectedResult: Adequate free memory remains available for normal operation
commands.abnormalResult: Free memory is critically low, confirming the reported high usage issue

commands.purpose: Identify which server tasks are currently running and potentially consuming excessive memory
commands.expectedResult: Tasks show normal, expected memory footprints
commands.abnormalResult: A specific task appears to be consuming disproportionate resources, warranting further investigation

troubleshootingSteps.action: Monitor memory usage over time to determine if it climbs steadily or spikes suddenly.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A steady climb suggests a memory leak, while sudden spikes suggest a specific triggering event or task.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Identify any recently installed or updated add-ins or agents that coincide with the memory increase.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Third-party or custom code is a common source of memory leaks not present in the base Domino server.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the specific task or add-in suspected of leaking memory, if it can be isolated.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A targeted restart can free leaked memory without requiring a full server restart, minimizing disruption.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the cause cannot be isolated, schedule a full server restart to clear accumulated memory usage.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A full restart provides immediate relief while further root-cause investigation continues.

possibleSolutions: Restart the specific leaking task, add-in, or agent
Update or remove a problematic third-party add-in
Schedule regular server restarts if a root cause cannot be immediately resolved
Increase server memory if legitimate load has genuinely grown
prevention: Monitor memory usage trends with proactive alerting
Test third-party add-ins for memory stability before production use
Schedule periodic preventive server restarts for known leak-prone environments
Keep server software and add-ins updated to current stable versions

description: The disk volume hosting the Domino server's data directory has run out of free space, preventing databases from growing, mail from routing, and potentially causing the server to become unstable.

Mail routing halts and databases fail to accept new documents
Server console shows warnings about low or no free disk space
Server may become unresponsive or crash if the condition is severe

Large mail files or databases have not been archived or cleaned up
Log.nsf or other system databases have grown unusually large
Backup or temporary files were not cleaned up after a previous maintenance operation
diagnosticQuestions: How much free space remains on the affected volume?
Are transaction logs configured to archive or purge automatically?
Are there any unusually large databases or log files that could be cleaned up or moved?
Was a backup or maintenance operation recently run that may have left temporary files behind?

commands.purpose: Display current disk space usage for volumes used by the Domino server
commands.expectedResult: Adequate free space remains on all relevant volumes
commands.abnormalResult: One or more volumes show critically low or zero free space, confirming the disk full condition

troubleshootingSteps.action: Move or delete unnecessary large files, backups, or temporary data no longer needed.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly frees space to restore normal server operation.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once space is freed, verify mail routing and database operations have resumed normally.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the underlying disk space issue was indeed the root cause of the reported symptoms.

possibleSolutions: Archive or purge old transaction logs
Remove unnecessary temporary or backup files
Archive large mail files and databases
Add additional disk capacity if space needs have genuinely grown
prevention: Monitor disk space with proactive alerts at multiple thresholds
Configure automatic transaction log archiving and purging
Schedule regular archiving of large mail files and databases
Clean up temporary and backup files as part of routine maintenance
keywords: notes server out of disk space

Transaction logging configuration was changed or disabled unintentionally
Underlying disk or file system issue affecting the log volume

Rebuild or reset a corrupted transaction log following Domino's documented process
Restore correct transaction logging configuration settings
Address underlying disk or file system issues affecting the log volume

Ensure clean server shutdowns whenever possible
Review transaction logging configuration after any major server change
Maintain healthy disk infrastructure for log volumes

description: The Domino server console, used by administrators to enter commands and monitor server activity, becomes unresponsive, failing to accept new commands or display current output.

No new log output appears in the console despite ongoing server activity
Remote console access also fails to respond
Server may still be processing user requests despite the console being unresponsive
possibleCauses: A specific server task has hung and is blocking console processing
Server is under extremely high load, delaying console responsiveness
Console log file has grown extremely large, slowing display and input processing
Underlying operating system resource exhaustion affecting the console process
diagnosticQuestions: Are users still able to access mail and applications despite the console being unresponsive?
Has any specific administrative command been entered just before the console became unresponsive?
How large has the console log file grown, and when was it last cleared or rotated?
Are there signs of high CPU or memory usage on the server at the operating system level?

commands.purpose: Attempt to list running tasks, which may still succeed even if other console commands appear unresponsive
commands.expectedResult: Task list displays normally, indicating the console can still process some commands
commands.abnormalResult: No response at all, confirming a more severe console or server hang

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether users can still access mail and applications despite the console appearing unresponsive.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines whether this is purely a console display issue or indicates a broader server hang.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Attempt a simple command such as show tasks to see if the console responds at all.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Distinguishes between a fully hung console and one that is simply slow or partially responsive.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check operating system-level resource usage (CPU, memory) on the server.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Severe resource exhaustion at the OS level can make the console appear frozen even if the server process is technically alive.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the console remains fully unresponsive and users are also affected, plan a controlled server restart.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A restart is often necessary to recover from a genuinely hung server process when other remedies fail.

possibleSolutions: Wait for a temporary high-load condition to subside if users are unaffected
Clear or rotate an oversized console log file
Restart the specific hung task if it can be identified and safely stopped
Perform a controlled server restart if the hang is severe and widespread
prevention: Monitor console responsiveness alongside other server health metrics
Configure console log rotation to prevent excessive file growth
Investigate recurring console hangs for a specific root cause task
Maintain adequate server resources to avoid load-related console delays

description: A specific Domino server task, such as the Router, Agent Manager, or a database task, crashes unexpectedly, terminating its activity and potentially generating a crash report (NSD) on the server.
symptoms: A specific task is missing from the active task list after previously running normally
Server generates a crash diagnostic file (NSD) around the time of the failure
Functionality dependent on the crashed task stops working, such as mail routing or agent execution
Server console log shows a panic or termination message referencing the specific task
possibleCauses: A bug in the specific task triggered by unusual data or a rare edge case
Resource exhaustion causing the task to crash under load
Corruption in a database the task was actively processing
Incompatibility introduced by a recent server patch or third-party add-in
diagnosticQuestions: Which specific task crashed, and was an NSD crash file generated?
Was the task processing any unusual or particularly large data at the time of the crash?
Has this specific task crashed before, suggesting a recurring issue?
Was any patch, update, or add-in recently installed before the crash occurred?

commands.purpose: Manually restart the specific crashed task from the server console
commands.expectedResult: Task restarts successfully and resumes normal operation
commands.abnormalResult: Task fails to restart or crashes again immediately, indicating a persistent underlying issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Identify the specific task that crashed and check whether an NSD crash file was generated.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The NSD file contains detailed diagnostic information useful for identifying the root cause.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the server console log around the time of the crash for related error messages.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Log context often reveals what the task was doing immediately before it failed.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Attempt to manually restart the crashed task.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Restores functionality quickly while further root-cause investigation continues in parallel.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the task crashes repeatedly, review recent patches or add-ins for known compatibility issues.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Recurring crashes often point to a specific software change rather than a one-time random event.

possibleSolutions: Restart the crashed task manually
Apply a vendor patch if a known bug is identified via the NSD report
Remove or update an incompatible add-in causing repeated crashes
Escalate to support with the NSD file if the cause cannot be determined internally
prevention: Monitor for and promptly review any NSD crash files generated
Test patches and add-ins in a staging environment before production deployment
Keep the server appropriately resourced to avoid load-related crashes
Maintain a record of recurring task crashes for pattern identification

description: The Domino server's ID file has passed its expiration date, causing the server to fail authentication, refuse connections, or be unable to start or communicate with other servers.
symptoms: Error message referencing an expired ID during server startup or connection attempts
Server-to-server communication, such as replication or mail routing, fails with authentication errors
Administrators cannot authenticate to the server using the expired ID
Client connections to the server are rejected
possibleCauses: The server ID's certificate expiration date was reached without renewal
Certificate renewal process was not completed or scheduled in advance
ID recertification was attempted but not properly applied to the running server
Clock or date misconfiguration on the server causing a false expiration reading
diagnosticQuestions: What is the exact expiration date shown for the server ID, and does it match the current date?
Was a certificate renewal process previously scheduled or attempted for this server?
Is the server's system clock and date set correctly?
Does this affect only this server, or multiple servers under the same certifier?

commands.purpose: Launch the certificate tool on the server to review and manage ID expiration and recertification
commands.expectedResult: Tool displays current certificate status and allows recertification
commands.abnormalResult: Tool confirms the ID has expired and requires immediate recertification

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the server's system date and time are set correctly.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect system clock can cause a valid ID to appear expired incorrectly.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify the actual expiration date of the server ID using administration tools.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the ID has genuinely expired or the issue lies elsewhere.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Recertify the server ID using the appropriate certifier ID or Certificate Authority process.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Recertification extends the ID's validity and is the standard resolution for an expired server ID.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the Domino server after recertification to ensure the updated ID is fully in effect.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some authentication states are only refreshed after a server restart following recertification.

possibleSolutions: Recertify the server ID using the organization's certifier
Correct the server's system date if it was the cause of a false expiration reading
Restart the server after applying the renewed certificate
Review and fix the certificate renewal process to prevent recurrence
prevention: Set up alerts well in advance of ID and certificate expiration dates
Maintain a documented schedule for periodic ID recertification
Automate certificate renewal processes where supported
Regularly audit expiration dates for all server and user IDs

description: The certificate used by the Domino server for secure communications, such as SSL/TLS for web or internet protocols, has expired, causing secure connections to fail or display warnings.
symptoms: Browsers or clients show a certificate expired warning when connecting securely
Secure protocols such as HTTPS or secure LDAP fail to establish connections
Internal applications relying on server certificates report trust or validation errors
Certificate details show an expiration date in the past when reviewed
possibleCauses: The SSL/TLS certificate's validity period simply expired without renewal
Certificate renewal was completed but not properly installed or activated on the server
Certificate Authority chain issue causing validation failure alongside expiration
Server was not monitored for upcoming certificate expiration
diagnosticQuestions: What is the exact expiration date of the certificate currently in use?
Was a renewed certificate already obtained but perhaps not yet installed?
Which specific services or protocols are affected by this expired certificate?
Is there a documented process for certificate renewal that was missed?

commands.purpose: Launch the Domino certificate tool to review current certificate status and manage renewal
commands.expectedResult: Tool displays certificate details and allows import of a renewed certificate
commands.abnormalResult: Tool confirms the certificate has expired and requires immediate replacement

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the exact expiration date and which services are affected by the expired certificate.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes the scope and urgency of the issue before proceeding with renewal.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Obtain or locate a renewed certificate from the appropriate Certificate Authority.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A valid renewed certificate is required to replace the expired one and restore secure connections.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Install and activate the renewed certificate on the Domino server using the certificate tool.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Properly installing the new certificate resolves the expiration and restores trusted secure connections.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart affected services, such as the HTTP task, to ensure the new certificate is fully in use.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some services cache certificate information and require a restart to recognize the update.

possibleSolutions: Renew and install a new SSL/TLS certificate
Restart affected server tasks after certificate installation
Correct the Certificate Authority chain if validation issues persist
Implement expiration monitoring to prevent recurrence
prevention: Set up automated alerts well before certificate expiration dates
Maintain a documented certificate renewal schedule and process
Use certificate management tools that support automatic renewal where possible
Regularly audit all server certificates across the environment

description: When addressing mail or looking up a name, Notes reports that the name is ambiguous, presenting multiple matching entries and preventing automatic resolution to a single recipient.
symptoms: Error or prompt indicating the name is ambiguous when addressing mail
Multiple similar entries appear in a name resolution dialog
Mail fails to send until the correct specific recipient is manually selected
Issue occurs consistently for names shared by multiple users
possibleCauses: Multiple users share the same or very similar display name
Duplicate Person documents exist for the same individual
Directory contains both an internal user and an external contact with matching names
Multiple directories (via Directory Assistance) return overlapping name matches
diagnosticQuestions: How many matching entries appear when the ambiguous name prompt is shown?
Are the matches genuinely different people, or duplicate entries for the same person?
Is the ambiguity occurring within a single directory or across multiple directories via Directory Assistance?
Has this name always been ambiguous, or did it start recently after a directory change?

commands.purpose: Search the Domino Directory directly for all entries matching the ambiguous name to review details
commands.expectedResult: Search reveals distinct, legitimate entries or duplicate entries needing cleanup
commands.abnormalResult: Search reveals unexpected duplicate Person documents for the same individual

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review all matching entries shown in the ambiguous name dialog for their distinguishing details, such as department or email address.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines whether the matches are legitimately different people or accidental duplicates.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Search the Domino Directory directly for the name to confirm how many Person documents exist.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides a clearer view than the abbreviated ambiguous name prompt, confirming duplicate entries if present.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If duplicate Person documents are found for the same individual, remove or merge the incorrect one.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Eliminates the root cause of the ambiguity going forward.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the matches are legitimately different people, advise users to select the correct one carefully or use unique identifiers like email address when addressing mail.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides a practical workaround when the ambiguity reflects a genuine naming coincidence rather than an error.

possibleSolutions: Remove or merge duplicate Person documents
Advise users to select the correct match carefully when genuinely ambiguous
Encourage use of full email addresses for addressing when names conflict
Review Directory Assistance configuration if cross-directory duplicates are the cause
prevention: Establish a process to check for duplicate names before creating new Person documents
Periodically audit the directory for duplicate or near-duplicate entries
Use unique display name conventions where naming conflicts are common
Review Directory Assistance configuration for unintended overlaps

description: When addressing mail, Notes cannot find a match for the intended recipient's name, showing an error or leaving the name unresolved (typically underlined in red) instead of resolving it to a valid address.
symptoms: Recipient name remains underlined in red after addressing an email
Error message stating the recipient could not be found when sending
Type-ahead does not suggest the expected recipient while typing
Recipient exists but under a different name format than expected
possibleCauses: Recipient's Person document does not exist or has not replicated to this server yet
User is searching only the local address book, which is out of date
Recipient's actual name differs from what is being typed, such as a nickname or alternate name
Directory Assistance is not properly configured to search a secondary directory containing the recipient
diagnosticQuestions: Is the recipient definitely a valid user, and do they exist in the Domino Directory?
Has the local address book (names.nsf) been recently refreshed or replicated?
Could the recipient's actual name differ from what is being entered?
Is Directory Assistance configured if the recipient is expected to come from another directory?

commands.purpose: Manually replicate the local address book to pick up any recent directory changes
commands.expectedResult: Local address book updates and the recipient becomes resolvable
commands.abnormalResult: Recipient still cannot be found after replication, indicating a deeper directory or configuration issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the recipient exists as a valid entry in the Domino Directory.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes whether the issue is a lookup problem or the recipient genuinely does not have an account.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Replicate the user's local address book to ensure it has the latest directory data.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An outdated local address book is a common and easily resolved cause of failed name resolution.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try searching for the recipient using an alternate name format, such as first name only or email address.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps rule out simple naming mismatches rather than a genuine directory issue.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Directory Assistance configuration if the recipient is expected to come from a secondary directory.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Misconfigured Directory Assistance will prevent valid recipients in another directory from being found.

possibleSolutions: Replicate the local address book to get current directory data
Use an alternate name format or the recipient's email address directly
Correct Directory Assistance configuration for secondary directories
Create the missing Person document if the recipient genuinely lacks one
prevention: Schedule regular local address book replication
Train users to use type-ahead and verify recipients before sending
Maintain accurate and complete Directory Assistance configuration
Ensure new users are fully registered before expecting others to mail them
keywords: type ahead not finding user notes

description: Mail addressed to an external internet email address fails to resolve or send correctly, with Notes either failing to recognize it as a valid address or the message bouncing after sending.
symptoms: Internet email address is not recognized as valid when addressing mail
Message bounces back with a delivery failure notice after sending
Address shows correctly formatted but is still flagged as unresolved
Issue affects only certain domains or address formats
possibleCauses: Typo or invalid formatting in the internet address itself
Server's DNS configuration cannot resolve the recipient's domain
Outbound internet mail routing is misconfigured on the Domino server
Recipient's mail server is rejecting messages due to spam filtering or blacklisting
diagnosticQuestions: Is the internet address correctly formatted with no typos?
Does the bounce message, if any, indicate a specific reason for failure?
Can the Domino server successfully resolve DNS for the recipient's domain?
Does this affect all internet addresses, or only specific domains?

commands.purpose: Verify that the Domino server can resolve DNS for the recipient's email domain
commands.expectedResult: DNS resolves successfully to valid mail server records
commands.abnormalResult: DNS resolution fails, indicating a DNS configuration issue affecting outbound mail

troubleshootingSteps.action: Double-check the internet address for typos or formatting errors.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Simple address errors are a common and easily overlooked cause of resolution failures.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review any bounce-back message for a specific delivery failure reason.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Bounce messages often clearly state whether the issue is DNS, routing, or recipient-side rejection.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test DNS resolution for the recipient's domain from the Domino server.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the server can locate the recipient's mail servers at all.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the Domino server's outbound internet mail routing (SMTP) configuration.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Misconfigured outbound routing can prevent otherwise valid internet addresses from being processed correctly.

possibleSolutions: Correct typos or formatting in the internet address
Resolve DNS configuration issues on the server
Fix outbound SMTP routing configuration
Work with the recipient's mail administrator if their server is rejecting messages
prevention: Encourage careful address verification before sending
Monitor DNS health for outbound mail servers
Regularly test outbound internet mail routing
Maintain good sender reputation to avoid recipient-side rejections

problem: Local Address Book Out of Date
description: A user's local replica of the address book (names.nsf) has not synchronized recent changes from the server, causing outdated names, missing new users, or incorrect information when addressing mail.
symptoms: Recently added users do not appear in local lookups
Recently updated information, such as a changed mail server, does not reflect locally
Users no longer with the organization still appear as valid recipients locally
Type-ahead suggests outdated or incorrect information
possibleCauses: Local replication schedule has not run recently or has failed silently
Replication is disabled or misconfigured for the local address book
User has been working offline or disconnected for an extended period
Local replica has a stuck or failed replication conflict
diagnosticQuestions: When was the local address book last successfully replicated?
Is the user's Notes client configured for scheduled replication, and is it functioning?
Has the user been working offline or away from the network for an extended time?
Are there any replication error messages in the user's client replication history?

commands.purpose: Manually force replication of the local address book with the server
commands.expectedResult: Replication completes and the local address book reflects current server data
commands.abnormalResult: Replication fails or reports errors, indicating a deeper connectivity or configuration issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the replication history for the local address book to see when it last succeeded.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes how far out of date the local copy actually is and whether replication has been failing.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Manually trigger replication using File > Replication > Replicate Now.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides an immediate update and reveals any errors preventing normal scheduled replication.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the client's scheduled replication settings to confirm the address book is included and enabled.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A misconfigured or disabled replication schedule will cause the local copy to fall permanently behind.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Resolve any reported replication errors, such as connectivity or access issues, found during manual replication.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Addressing the underlying error ensures future scheduled replications succeed as well.

possibleSolutions: Manually replicate the local address book
Correct scheduled replication settings to include the address book
Resolve underlying connectivity issues preventing replication
Recreate the local replica if persistent replication errors cannot be resolved
prevention: Ensure scheduled replication is properly configured for all users
Encourage regular network connectivity for laptop and remote users
Monitor for replication failures across the user base
Educate users on manually replicating before extended offline periods
keywords: local address book out of date notes

description: The Domino Directory (names.nsf) on the server cannot be accessed at all, either by administrators or the server itself, preventing lookups, authentication, and mail routing.
symptoms: Error message stating names.nsf cannot be opened or accessed
All directory-dependent functions fail, including authentication and mail routing
Server console shows errors related to accessing the Domino Directory
Administrator cannot open the directory even locally on the server console
possibleCauses: Corruption in the names.nsf database file
File-level lock or permissions issue preventing access
Disk or file system error affecting the volume hosting names.nsf
ACL misconfiguration inadvertently blocking all access, including administrators
diagnosticQuestions: What exact error appears when attempting to access the Domino Directory?
Can any user or administrator, even locally on the server, open names.nsf?
Are there signs of disk or file system errors on the volume hosting the directory?
Was any recent change made to the directory's ACL or file permissions?

commands.purpose: Attempt to repair structural corruption in the Domino Directory database
commands.expectedResult: Fixup completes and the directory becomes accessible again
commands.abnormalResult: Fixup fails or the directory remains inaccessible, requiring restoration from backup

troubleshootingSteps.action: Attempt to access names.nsf directly from the server console.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the issue is server-wide or specific to certain users or access methods.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the file system permissions and any file locks on names.nsf at the operating system level.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A file-level permissions or lock issue outside of Domino's own ACL can block all access.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run Fixup against names.nsf to check for and repair database corruption.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Corruption is a common cause of a database becoming completely inaccessible.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If Fixup cannot resolve the issue, restore names.nsf from the most recent clean backup.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Severe corruption preventing all access typically requires restoring a known-good copy to restore service quickly.

possibleSolutions: Repair corruption in names.nsf using Fixup and Compact
Correct file system-level permissions or locks
Restore names.nsf from a recent backup if repair is unsuccessful
Review and correct any ACL misconfiguration once access is restored
prevention: Maintain regular, verified backups of the Domino Directory
Monitor disk health on servers hosting critical system databases
Restrict and audit changes to the Domino Directory ACL
Ensure clean server shutdowns to reduce corruption risk

description: The Directory Catalog, used to provide a lightweight, fast-searching combined view of directory entries for client type-ahead, is out of date and does not reflect recently added or changed users.
symptoms: Recently added users do not appear in client type-ahead lookups
Directory Catalog entries reflect outdated names, titles, or mail server information
Full Domino Directory search finds users that the catalog does not
Users report inconsistent lookup results between type-ahead and full directory search
possibleCauses: Directory Catalog generation agent has not run recently or has failed
Scheduled Directory Catalog update interval is too infrequent for the rate of directory changes
The catalog's source directories are not fully included in its configuration
Replication of the catalog to client machines has not occurred recently
diagnosticQuestions: When was the Directory Catalog last regenerated or updated?
Is the catalog generation agent running successfully on its configured schedule?
Does the catalog configuration include all relevant source Domino Directories?
Has the updated catalog replicated out to affected client machines?

commands.purpose: Confirm the Directory Catalog generation agent is scheduled and running as expected
commands.expectedResult: Agent appears scheduled and has recent successful run history
commands.abnormalResult: Agent is missing from the schedule or shows failed run history, explaining the outdated catalog

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check when the Directory Catalog was last successfully regenerated.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes how outdated the catalog actually is and whether generation has stopped entirely.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify the catalog generation agent is running successfully on its configured schedule.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A failed or disabled generation agent is the most direct cause of an outdated catalog.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the catalog's configuration to confirm all relevant source directories are included.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Missing source directories will cause certain users to never appear, even with regular regeneration.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the updated catalog has replicated to affected client machines.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A correctly regenerated server-side catalog will not help users whose local replicas have not synced.

possibleSolutions: Restart or reschedule the catalog generation agent
Adjust the catalog's source directory configuration
Increase the frequency of catalog regeneration if changes occur often
Force replication of the updated catalog to affected clients
prevention: Monitor Directory Catalog generation agent success regularly
Set an appropriate regeneration frequency based on organizational change rate
Review catalog configuration whenever new directories are added
Include catalog replication in standard client synchronization schedules

description: More than one Person document exists in the Domino Directory for the same individual, causing ambiguous name resolution, inconsistent access rights, or confusion during administration.
symptoms: Ambiguous name prompts appear when addressing mail to the affected user
Different Person documents show conflicting information, such as different mail servers
Group memberships or ACL entries reference the wrong duplicate document
Administrator finds two or more entries for what should be a single user
possibleCauses: User was registered more than once, possibly on different servers
A rename or migration process created a new document without removing the old one
Manual directory entry errors introduced a duplicate
Import or bulk update process created duplicates due to mismatched matching criteria
diagnosticQuestions: How many Person documents exist for this individual, and what are the differences between them?
Which document is the current, authoritative one that should be retained?
Are any groups, ACLs, or mail-in databases referencing the incorrect duplicate?
Was this user recently renamed, migrated, or re-registered?

commands.purpose: Search the Domino Directory to locate and compare all duplicate Person documents for the individual
commands.expectedResult: Search clearly shows the duplicate entries and their differing details
commands.abnormalResult: N/A - this is a diagnostic search rather than a pass/fail check

troubleshootingSteps.action: Search the Domino Directory to locate all Person documents for the individual and compare their details.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes exactly how many duplicates exist and which one is the correct, current record.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Determine which document is authoritative based on current mail server, department, and other accurate details.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures the correct document is retained while the incorrect one is removed.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update any groups, ACLs, or mail-in database references pointing to the incorrect duplicate.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Prevents access or mail issues after the duplicate document is removed.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Delete the incorrect duplicate Person document and force directory replication.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Removes the source of ambiguity and ensures the correction propagates to all servers.

possibleSolutions: Identify and retain the correct, authoritative Person document
Update group and ACL references to the correct document
Delete the duplicate Person document
Force directory replication after cleanup
prevention: Check for existing Person documents before registering a user
Follow proper rename and migration procedures that avoid creating duplicates
Use matching criteria carefully during bulk directory imports
Periodically audit the directory for duplicate entries

description: A user's canonical name in the Domino Directory is malformed or incorrect, such as having the wrong organizational unit, misspelled components, or an improperly formatted hierarchy, causing authentication or addressing issues.
symptoms: Authentication failures referencing the user's distinguished name
Mail addressing or ACL entries fail to match the user correctly
Canonical name displayed in Person document does not match expected organizational hierarchy
Errors referencing name normalization or hierarchy mismatches
possibleCauses: Data entry error when the Person document was originally created
User was registered under an incorrect organizational unit certifier
A directory import process introduced malformed canonical name data
Organizational restructuring was not properly reflected in the user's registration
diagnosticQuestions: What is the current canonical name shown in the Person document, and how does it differ from what is expected?
Was the user registered under the correct organizational unit certifier?
Does the issue affect authentication, addressing, or both?
Has the organization's naming hierarchy changed since this user was registered?

commands.purpose: Open the user's Person document to review the exact current canonical name value
commands.expectedResult: Canonical name matches the expected, correct organizational hierarchy
commands.abnormalResult: Canonical name shows an incorrect or malformed hierarchy, confirming the reported issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the user's current canonical name in their Person document.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes the exact incorrect value that needs to be corrected.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Determine the correct canonical name based on the user's actual organizational unit and certifier.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides the accurate target value needed to properly fix the record.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the correction requires a change in certifier or organizational unit, use the appropriate Domino Administrator rename or move process rather than a manual edit.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Manual edits to canonical name fields can cause further inconsistencies; the proper administrative process ensures related certificates and IDs stay in sync.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify the user's Notes ID file also reflects the corrected canonical name after the change.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A mismatch between the directory entry and the ID file will continue to cause authentication problems.

possibleSolutions: Use Domino Administrator's proper rename/move process to correct the canonical name
Update the user's Notes ID file to match the corrected name
Re-certify the user under the correct organizational unit if needed
Force directory replication after correction
prevention: Use standardized registration procedures with correct organizational unit selection
Validate canonical name data during any bulk import process
Review naming hierarchy consistency during organizational changes
Train administrators on proper rename/move procedures rather than manual edits

description: Notes fails to resolve an entered name or address to a valid recipient during addressing, despite the recipient appearing to be a legitimate, existing user or contact.
symptoms: Generic address resolution failure error when sending mail
Name appears correctly typed but is still flagged as unresolved
Issue occurs intermittently rather than consistently for the same recipient
Resolution works from one client or location but not another for the same user
possibleCauses: Temporary directory replication delay between servers
Client's local address book or Directory Catalog is out of sync
Network connectivity issue preventing the lookup from completing
Multiple directory sources (via Directory Assistance) returning inconsistent results
diagnosticQuestions: Does the resolution failure happen consistently, or only sometimes for this recipient?
Does it happen from all client locations, or only specific ones?
Has directory replication completed recently across all relevant servers?
Is Directory Assistance involved, and could it be returning conflicting results?

commands.purpose: Force replication of the local address book to rule out a synchronization delay as the cause
commands.expectedResult: Address resolves successfully after replication
commands.abnormalResult: Resolution still fails after replication, pointing to a network or directory configuration issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Determine whether the failure is consistent or intermittent, and whether it is isolated to specific clients or locations.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps distinguish between a systemic directory issue and a localized client or network problem.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Force replication of the local address book and Directory Catalog if used.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves cases where the failure is simply due to outdated local directory data.

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check network connectivity from the affected client to the directory server.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Intermittent network issues can cause lookups to fail even when the underlying directory data is correct.

troubleshootingSteps.action: If Directory Assistance is involved, review its configuration for consistency across the servers being used.
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Conflicting or misconfigured secondary directory sources can cause inconsistent resolution results.

possibleSolutions: Replicate local directory data to resolve synchronization delays
Resolve underlying network connectivity issues
Correct Directory Assistance configuration inconsistencies
Escalate to the directory replication topology for a systemic fix if widespread
prevention: Maintain healthy, regular directory replication schedules
Monitor network stability between clients and directory servers
Keep Directory Assistance configuration consistent across all servers
Periodically audit address resolution behavior organization-wide

problem: Cannot Download ID from ID Vault
description: A user attempting to retrieve their Notes ID file from the ID Vault, such as when setting up a new device or recovering from a lost ID, is unable to successfully download it.
symptoms: Error message when attempting to download the ID from the vault
Download process appears to start but never completes
User is prompted for credentials that are then rejected
ID download works for some users but not others on the same vault
possibleCauses: User's ID is not actually stored in the configured ID Vault
Vault policy does not grant the user download or reset rights
Network connectivity issue between the client and the vault server
ID Vault database itself has a corruption or access issue
diagnosticQuestions: Is the user's ID confirmed to be stored in the ID Vault according to administration tools?
Does the user's security/ID Vault policy grant them rights to download their own ID?
Can the client reach the vault server over the network without issues?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for a circular reference warning at the bottom of the screen, which can prevent proper calculation of related formulas

troubleshootingSteps.action: Carefully review the formula syntax for typing mistakes, such as missing parentheses or incorrect cell references
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A syntax error can cause Excel to treat the entry as plain text rather than a working formula

Force recalculation using F9
Change cell formatting from Text to General or Number and re-enter the formula
Fix a circular reference causing calculation issues
Correct formula syntax errors

Watch for circular reference warnings and address them promptly

troubleshootingSteps.reason: External links break if the source file has been deleted, renamed, or moved to a different folder

troubleshootingSteps.action: Going forward, before deleting rows or columns, check if any formulas depend on that data using Excel's 'Trace Dependents' feature
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps prevent future #REF! errors by showing what formulas rely on the data before it is removed

possibleSolutions: Undo the recent deletion that caused the error
Manually correct the formula with valid cell references
Fix a broken worksheet name reference
Update a broken external workbook link
Use Trace Dependents before deleting data in the future
prevention: Check Trace Dependents before deleting rows, columns, or cells
Avoid deleting cells that other formulas rely on without checking first
