description: A formula cell displays '#DIV/0!', indicating that the formula is trying to divide a number by zero or by an empty cell, which is not mathematically possible.
symptoms: Cell displays '#DIV/0!' instead of a calculated result
Error appears in calculations involving division, such as averages or percentages
Error may appear only for certain rows while others calculate correctly
Related formulas that depend on this cell may also show errors
possibleCauses: The formula is dividing by a cell that contains a zero
The formula is dividing by a cell that is currently empty
A function like AVERAGE is being used on a range that is completely empty for that specific row
Data has not yet been entered for a calculation intended to be completed later
diagnosticQuestions: Which specific cell is being used as the divisor (the number being divided by) in this formula?
Is that cell currently empty, or does it contain a zero?
Is this error expected until more data is entered, such as in an ongoing report?
Does this happen in one row only, or across many rows in the same column?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Click on the cell showing the #DIV/0! error and identify which part of the formula is the divisor
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This pinpoints exactly which cell is currently zero or empty, causing the division error

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if that divisor cell is genuinely supposed to have a value, and if data is simply missing, enter the correct value
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly resolves the error by providing valid data for the calculation

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the divisor being zero or empty is expected in certain situations, such as a report where data has not yet been entered for that row, wrap the formula in an IFERROR function
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This allows the formula to show a blank cell, zero, or a custom message instead of the error, keeping the report visually clean while the error is expected and harmless

troubleshootingSteps.action: For example, change a formula like '=A1/B1' to '=IFERROR(A1/B1,0)' or '=IFERROR(A1/B1,"")' depending on what should display instead of the error
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the standard, recommended way to gracefully handle expected division errors in Excel

troubleshootingSteps.action: If using an AVERAGE function on a range that might be empty, consider using AVERAGEIF or checking with an IF statement first to avoid dividing by zero when no data exists
troubleshootingSteps.reason: AVERAGE internally divides by the count of numbers, and an entirely empty or non-numeric range causes this same type of error

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the error appears unexpectedly in a formula that previously worked, check if a value in the divisor cell was recently changed to zero or accidentally deleted
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps identify a recent change that introduced the error where it did not exist before

possibleSolutions: Enter the correct, non-zero value in the divisor cell
Wrap the formula in IFERROR to handle expected division by zero gracefully
Use AVERAGEIF or an IF check to avoid averaging empty ranges
Correct a recently changed value that introduced the error
prevention: Use IFERROR proactively in formulas involving division where empty data is expected
Double check source data before performing division-based calculations
Use data validation to prevent accidental zero entries where not appropriate

problem: Macros are disabled and will not run
description: The user opens a workbook that contains macros, but sees a security warning saying macros have been disabled, and any buttons or automated features relying on macros do not work.
symptoms: Yellow security warning bar saying 'Macros have been disabled'
Buttons or automated tools in the workbook do nothing when clicked
Error message when trying to run a macro manually
Macro-enabled features work on some computers but not others
possibleCauses: Excel's macro security settings are set to disable all macros by default
The file was downloaded from the internet and is marked as untrusted
The macro itself contains an error preventing it from running
The workbook is saved with a .xlsx extension instead of .xlsm, which does not support macros
Company security policies block macros entirely on managed computers
diagnosticQuestions: Do you see a yellow security warning bar when opening the file, and if so, what does it say?
Where did this file come from, such as downloaded from the internet, received by email, or created locally?
Is this a personal computer, or a company-managed computer with possible security restrictions?
Do you trust the source of this file and its macros?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for a yellow security warning bar at the top of the workbook when it opens, and read exactly what it says
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the most common and direct explanation, showing that Excel intentionally blocked the macros as a security precaution

troubleshootingSteps.action: If you trust the source of the file completely, click 'Enable Content' on the security warning bar
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the standard, safe way to allow macros to run for a specific trusted file

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the file was downloaded from the internet, right-click the file in File Explorer, select Properties, and check the 'Unblock' checkbox at the bottom if present
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Windows marks internet-downloaded files as potentially unsafe, and unblocking removes this flag, allowing macros to run more smoothly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Excel's Trust Center settings under File > Options > Trust Center > Trust Center Settings > Macro Settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This shows the current overall macro security level, which may be set to block all macros without any warning

troubleshootingSteps.action: Adjust the macro setting to 'Disable all macros with notification' if it is currently set to block them entirely, so you at least get the option to enable trusted macros going forward
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides a balance between security and functionality, showing a warning rather than silently blocking everything

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the file is saved with a .xlsm extension if it is genuinely meant to contain macros
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Standard .xlsx files do not support macros at all, and a file mistakenly saved in this format will lose any macro functionality

troubleshootingSteps.action: On a company-managed computer, contact the IT department if macros are needed for legitimate work purposes but are blocked by policy
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Company-wide macro restrictions are often intentional security measures that require IT approval to adjust

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a macro is enabled but still does not run correctly, check the macro's code in the Visual Basic Editor for errors, if you have the necessary permissions and knowledge
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The macro being allowed to run does not guarantee it is written correctly, and errors within its code can also prevent it from working

possibleSolutions: Click 'Enable Content' on the security warning bar for trusted files
Unblock the file in its Properties if downloaded from the internet
Adjust Trust Center macro settings appropriately
Save the file with the correct .xlsm extension
Request IT approval for macros on a managed company computer
Fix errors within the macro's code if it still fails after being enabled
prevention: Only enable macros from trusted, known sources
Keep macro security settings at a reasonable, notification-based level
Save macro-containing workbooks with the correct .xlsm extension
Be cautious with macros in files received from unknown senders

problem: Pivot Table is not refreshing with updated data
description: The user updates the source data for a Pivot Table, expecting the Pivot Table to reflect the new numbers, but it continues to show old, outdated values until manually refreshed, or does not update even after refreshing.
symptoms: Pivot Table shows old data even after the source data has been changed
New rows added to the source data do not appear in the Pivot Table
Manually refreshing does not update the values
Pivot Table field list may be missing new columns added to the source data
possibleCauses: The Pivot Table has simply not been manually refreshed yet, since this does not happen automatically by default
The Pivot Table's source data range does not include newly added rows or columns
The data source is set to a fixed range rather than a dynamic table
The Pivot Table is connected to an external data source that needs a separate refresh action
Filters applied to the Pivot Table are hiding the new data
diagnosticQuestions: Have you tried right-clicking the Pivot Table and selecting Refresh?
Was new data added as new rows below the original data range, or within the existing range?
Is the source data a regular cell range, or was it converted into an official Excel Table?
Are there any filters currently applied to the Pivot Table that might be hiding the new data?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Right-click anywhere inside the Pivot Table and select Refresh, or use the Refresh button on the PivotTable Analyze tab
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Pivot Tables do not automatically update when source data changes, and a manual refresh is the first and simplest step

troubleshootingSteps.action: If refreshing does not show new rows that were added below the original data, check the Pivot Table's source data range under PivotTable Analyze > Change Data Source
troubleshootingSteps.reason: If new rows were added outside the originally defined range, the Pivot Table will not include them even after refreshing

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the data source range to include the new rows and columns if the current range is too small
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly expands what the Pivot Table considers as its source data going forward

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider converting the source data range into an official Excel Table using Ctrl+T before creating or updating the Pivot Table
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Excel Tables automatically expand to include new data added directly below or beside them, which then flows into the Pivot Table without manually adjusting the range each time

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if any filters are currently applied within the Pivot Table that might be hiding the new or updated data
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Data that does not match an active filter will not display, even though it is technically included in the underlying source

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the Pivot Table is connected to an external data source, such as another workbook or a database, use the specific 'Refresh All' option and confirm the connection settings are correct
troubleshootingSteps.reason: External data connections sometimes require a different refresh process than a simple internal data range

troubleshootingSteps.action: For workbooks where this happens frequently, consider enabling 'Refresh data when opening the file' under PivotTable options
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the Pivot Table automatically refreshes every time the workbook is opened, reducing the chance of viewing outdated data

possibleSolutions: Manually refresh the Pivot Table
Expand the Pivot Table's source data range to include new data
Convert the source data into an Excel Table for automatic range expansion
Remove or adjust filters hiding new data
Refresh external data connections properly
Enable automatic refresh when opening the file
prevention: Use Excel Tables as the source data for Pivot Tables
Refresh Pivot Tables as a habit after updating source data
Enable automatic refresh on file open for frequently updated reports
Regularly review applied filters on Pivot Tables

New rows or columns of data do not appear in the chart
Chart appears frozen even after significant changes to the source data
Deleted data may still appear as an empty category or zero value on the chart
possibleCauses: The chart's data range is fixed and does not include newly added rows or columns
The source data is a regular cell range rather than an Excel Table with automatic expansion
Manual calculation mode is preventing the chart from reflecting recalculated values
The chart was copied or is linked to a different, unintended data range
Hidden rows or columns are excluded from the chart by a specific chart setting
diagnosticQuestions: Was the new data added within the original chart's data range, or added as new rows or columns outside of it?
Is the source data a regular range, or has it been converted into an Excel Table?
Is Excel's calculation mode set to Automatic or Manual?
Are there any hidden rows or columns in the data that the chart might be excluding intentionally?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Click on the chart and check the highlighted data range shown around the source cells to see exactly what the chart currently includes
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This visually confirms whether new data falls inside or outside the range the chart is currently using

troubleshootingSteps.action: If new data falls outside the current range, click the chart, go to Chart Design > Select Data, and expand the data range to include the new rows or columns
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly updates what data the chart is set to display

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider converting the source data into an official Excel Table using Ctrl+T if this problem happens frequently
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Excel Tables automatically expand to include new data, and charts based on them will automatically update as new rows or columns are added

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check that Excel's Calculation mode is set to Automatic under the Formulas tab
troubleshootingSteps.reason: If set to Manual, values feeding the chart may not be recalculating, causing the chart to appear outdated even with correct data ranges

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if any rows or columns involved are hidden, and review the chart's settings under Chart Design > Select Data > Hidden and Empty Cells to see how hidden data is being handled
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Charts can be configured to intentionally exclude hidden rows or columns, which may explain missing data that the user expects to see

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the chart seems linked to unexpected data, right-click the chart, choose Select Data, and carefully verify the exact cell references being used
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A chart can sometimes be accidentally linked to the wrong range, especially after copying and pasting charts between worksheets

troubleshootingSteps.action: As a final step, try deleting and recreating the chart from the current, correct data range if none of the above resolves the issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This guarantees a chart built fresh from the intended current data, removing any lingering reference issues from the original chart

possibleSolutions: Expand the chart's data range to include new data
Convert source data into an Excel Table for automatic range updates
Switch Calculation mode to Automatic
Adjust hidden and empty cell settings for the chart
Correct an unintended data range link
Recreate the chart from the correct current data range
prevention: Use Excel Tables as chart source data whenever possible
Keep Calculation mode set to Automatic
Regularly verify chart data ranges after major spreadsheet changes
Be cautious when copying charts between worksheets

problem: Excel freezes while working with a spreadsheet
description: While the user is entering data, applying formulas, or scrolling through a spreadsheet, Excel stops responding entirely, with the window showing 'Not Responding' and no input having any effect.
symptoms: Window title shows 'Excel (Not Responding)'
Cannot click, type, or scroll within the workbook
May happen with large workbooks, heavy formulas, or many open files
Freeze may resolve after a long wait, or require force closing
possibleCauses: A very large workbook with thousands of rows, complex formulas, or many worksheets
Excel is set to Automatic calculation, causing heavy recalculation with every change in a large file
A problematic add-in causing instability
Not enough system memory (RAM) to handle the workbook's size
A specific formula or function causing a long, intensive calculation
Multiple large workbooks open simultaneously
diagnosticQuestions: How large is the workbook, in terms of rows, worksheets, and complexity of formulas?
Does this happen with all workbooks, or just one particularly large or complex one?
Does the freeze happen right after entering data, or while performing another action like sorting or filtering?
How much RAM does the computer have, and how many programs are typically open at the same time?

commands.purpose: Check Excel's CPU and memory usage while it appears frozen, to see if it is truly stuck or just working intensively
commands.expectedResult: High CPU usage suggests Excel is actively calculating, while 0% usage over a long period suggests it is truly stuck
commands.abnormalResult: Excel is stuck at 0% CPU usage for many minutes with no progress, indicating a true freeze rather than heavy processing

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Task Manager to see if Excel is using high CPU, suggesting it is still actively calculating rather than truly frozen
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps decide whether to keep waiting or to consider force closing the program

troubleshootingSteps.action: If CPU usage is high, allow more time for a very large or complex workbook to finish processing before assuming it is stuck
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Extremely large or formula-heavy workbooks can genuinely take a long time to complete calculations, especially on older hardware

troubleshootingSteps.action: If Excel does recover, immediately save the workbook using Save As to create a fresh, safe copy
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This protects the user's work in case Excel freezes again or shows early signs of instability

troubleshootingSteps.action: Change Calculation mode to Manual for very large workbooks under the Formulas tab, then manually recalculate using F9 when ready
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This prevents Excel from recalculating the entire workbook automatically after every small change, which can significantly reduce freezing during data entry

troubleshootingSteps.action: Close other open programs and unnecessary browser tabs to free up system memory for Excel
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Large workbooks require significant memory, and freeing up resources elsewhere can improve Excel's performance

troubleshootingSteps.action: Disable unnecessary add-ins through File > Options > Add-ins
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Add-ins can add overhead that contributes to freezing, especially in already resource-intensive workbooks

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider splitting a very large workbook into smaller, separate files if it has grown excessively large over time
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reducing the overall size and complexity directly reduces the processing load that can cause freezing

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the computer has limited RAM and frequently works with large workbooks, consider upgrading the amount of installed RAM
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This addresses the underlying hardware limitation causing frequent freezing with demanding files

possibleSolutions: Wait for a large workbook to finish genuine processing
Save work using Save As once recovered
Switch Calculation mode to Manual for large workbooks
Close other programs to free up memory
Disable unnecessary add-ins
Split an overly large workbook into smaller files
Upgrade system RAM for frequent work with large files
prevention: Save workbooks frequently while working
Use Manual calculation mode for very large or complex workbooks
Keep workbook size and complexity reasonable when possible
Only use necessary, trusted add-ins
Ensure adequate system RAM for typical workbook sizes

description: The user tries to save an Excel workbook, but receives an error message, the save appears to do nothing, or the file will not save to the intended location.
symptoms: Error message when trying to save, such as a permissions or naming conflict error
Save appears to complete but changes are not actually saved
Error mentioning the file is locked or in use by another user
Saving to a specific location fails while saving elsewhere works
possibleCauses: The file is set to read-only
Insufficient permissions to save to the chosen folder or network location
The destination drive or folder is full or disconnected
The file name contains characters not allowed in file names
A network connection was lost while saving to a network location
The workbook is open and locked by another user in a shared environment
The workbook is extremely large and hitting a size or row limit issue
diagnosticQuestions: What exact error message appears when trying to save?
Where are you trying to save the file, such as locally, on a USB drive, or a network/shared location?
Does saving with a different file name or in a different location work?
Is this file shared with or currently open by another person?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Read the exact error message shown when the save fails
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The specific wording often points directly to the cause, such as a permissions or naming issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try saving the workbook with File > Save As to a different location, such as the Desktop
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is with the specific destination or the workbook itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the file is marked as read-only by right-clicking the file in File Explorer, checking Properties, and unchecking Read-only if selected
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A read-only file cannot be saved over until this attribute is removed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available storage space on the destination drive
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A completely full drive will prevent any new save operations from completing

troubleshootingSteps.action: If saving to a network or shared drive, confirm the network connection is currently working
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A dropped network connection during saving is a common cause of save failures in shared environments

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the file name contains special characters that are not allowed, such as / \ : * ? " < > |
troubleshootingSteps.reason: These characters are restricted in file names and will cause save errors if used

troubleshootingSteps.action: If working in a shared environment, check if someone else has the workbook open, which can lock it from being saved by others
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Simultaneous access without proper co-authoring features can cause save conflicts

troubleshootingSteps.action: As a safety measure, copy all worksheets into a new blank workbook and save that instead if the original file consistently fails to save
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This preserves the user's work using a completely fresh file, bypassing whatever specific issue affects the original

possibleSolutions: Remove the read-only attribute from the file
Save to a different location to confirm the file works
Free up space on the destination drive
Fix or wait for the network connection to a shared drive
Rename the file to remove invalid characters
Save content into a new workbook if the original remains broken
prevention: Regularly check available storage space
Avoid special characters in file names
Use a stable network connection when saving to shared drives
Coordinate with others when working on shared workbooks

Run Office Quick Repair or Online Repair

Keep antivirus software properly configured to avoid false blocks

Disable a problematic add-in

description: The user has applied animations or transitions to slide elements, but when running the actual slide show, the animations either do not play at all or play incorrectly compared to how they appeared while editing.

Animation order is different than intended
Transitions between slides do not play smoothly or at all
Animations work in edit view but not during Presenter View or full slide show

Slide show settings have animations disabled
Outdated graphics drivers affecting animation rendering
The presentation was opened in a different, older version of PowerPoint that does not support certain animation types
Performance settings reducing animation quality on less powerful computers

Have any slide show settings been changed recently, intentionally or accidentally?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Click the Preview button on the Animations tab while editing to confirm the animations are still correctly applied to the intended elements
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This verifies whether the animations exist and function correctly outside of the full slide show environment

troubleshootingSteps.reason: This specific setting can be intentionally or accidentally enabled, disabling all animations during playback while leaving them intact in the file

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the animation order in the Animation Pane matches what is intended, checking for elements that may have been duplicated or reordered accidentally
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Animations play in the exact order listed in the Animation Pane, and unintended changes here directly affect playback

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the computer's graphics driver, since animation rendering relies on it, especially for more complex or 3D-style animations
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Outdated graphics drivers are a common and often overlooked cause of animations not displaying correctly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check what version of PowerPoint the presentation was originally created in versus the version currently being used to present it

troubleshootingSteps.action: If presenting on an older or less powerful computer, consider simplifying complex animations, since performance-limited systems sometimes skip or shorten animations to maintain smooth playback
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures more consistent animation playback across different hardware capabilities

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test the full slide show, not just the edit view preview, well before an important presentation to confirm animations behave as expected in the actual presenting environment
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Edit view previews do not always perfectly represent full slide show behavior, especially with Presenter View or dual monitor setups

possibleSolutions: Turn off 'Show Without Animation' if accidentally enabled
Correct the animation order in the Animation Pane
Update the graphics driver
Use a consistent, current PowerPoint version for creating and presenting
Simplify complex animations for less powerful presenting computers
Test the full slide show in advance of important presentations
prevention: Test animations in full Slide Show mode, not just edit view, before presenting
Keep graphics drivers updated
Use a consistent PowerPoint version between creation and presentation computers
Avoid overly complex animations for presentations on unknown or older hardware

problem: Fonts are missing or displaying incorrectly in a presentation
description: A presentation opens, but the text appears in a different, substitute font than intended, changing the overall look and sometimes causing text to overflow or misalign on slides.
symptoms: Text appears in an unexpected substitute font
Slide layout looks different from how it was originally designed, with text overflowing text boxes
PowerPoint may show a message that fonts used in the presentation are not installed
Presentation looks correct on the original computer but wrong on another computer
possibleCauses: The font used in the original presentation is not installed on the current computer
The presentation was created on a different computer with different available fonts
Fonts were not embedded when the presentation was saved
A font file has become corrupted or was uninstalled
diagnosticQuestions: Was this presentation created on this computer, or received from someone else or another computer?
Do you know the specific name of the font that should be used?
Does the presentation display correctly when opened on the original computer it was created on?
Was the option to embed fonts used when the presentation was originally saved?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Select the affected text and check the font name shown in the font box to see what font the presentation expects to use
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This confirms the exact font name being called for, even though it is currently being substituted with something else

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the Windows Fonts folder to see if the required font is installed on this specific computer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This confirms whether the font genuinely needs to be installed on this machine

troubleshootingSteps.action: If missing, obtain and install the correct font from a legitimate, licensed source
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Installing the correct font is the most direct way to restore the presentation's intended appearance

troubleshootingSteps.action: Close and reopen the presentation after installing the font to confirm it displays correctly
troubleshootingSteps.reason: PowerPoint needs to reload the file to properly apply a newly installed font

troubleshootingSteps.action: For presentations you create yourself that will be shown on other computers, use File > Options > Save > Embed fonts in the file before saving
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the presentation displays correctly on any computer, even without the fonts separately installed, which is especially important for presentations

troubleshootingSteps.action: If embedding fonts, choose the option to embed all characters rather than just the characters currently used, if the presentation might be edited further on another computer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures any new text typed later on a different computer will still display using the correct embedded font

troubleshootingSteps.action: As a more universal option, consider using widely available standard fonts for important presentations that will be shown on unknown computers, especially where embedding is not possible or reliable
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This avoids missing font problems entirely by relying only on fonts virtually guaranteed to be available

possibleSolutions: Install the missing font from a legitimate source
Embed fonts when saving the presentation
Use widely available standard fonts for shared presentations
Reapply the correct font manually if it becomes available
prevention: Embed fonts in important presentations before sharing or presenting elsewhere
Use widely available standard fonts when possible
Test presentations on the target computer in advance of important events

description: The user tries to save a PowerPoint presentation, but receives an error message, the save appears to do nothing, or the file will not save to the intended location.
symptoms: Error message when trying to save, such as a permissions or naming conflict error
Save appears to complete but changes are not actually saved
Error mentioning the file is locked or in use by another user
Saving to a specific location fails while saving elsewhere works
possibleCauses: The file is set to read-only
Insufficient permissions to save to the chosen folder or network location
The destination drive or folder is full or disconnected
The file name contains characters not allowed in file names
A network connection was lost while saving to a network location
The presentation is open and locked by another user in a shared environment
The presentation is very large due to embedded videos or images, causing save timeouts
diagnosticQuestions: What exact error message appears when trying to save?
Where are you trying to save the file, such as locally, on a USB drive, or a network/shared location?
Does saving with a different file name or in a different location work?
Is the presentation unusually large, especially with embedded videos or many high-resolution images?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Read the exact error message shown when the save fails
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The specific wording often points directly to the cause, such as a permissions or naming issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try saving the presentation with File > Save As to a different location, such as the Desktop
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is with the specific destination or the presentation itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the file is marked as read-only by right-clicking the file in File Explorer, checking Properties, and unchecking Read-only if selected
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A read-only file cannot be saved over until this attribute is removed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available storage space on the destination drive, especially if the presentation contains large embedded videos
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Media-heavy presentations can be very large, and a nearly full drive can prevent a successful save

troubleshootingSteps.action: If saving to a network or shared drive, confirm the network connection is currently stable, since large file saves are especially vulnerable to interruptions
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A dropped network connection during a large save is a common cause of save failures for media-heavy presentations

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the file name contains special characters that are not allowed, such as / \ : * ? " < > |
troubleshootingSteps.reason: These characters are restricted in file names and will cause save errors if used

troubleshootingSteps.action: If working in a shared environment, check if someone else has the presentation open, which can lock it from being saved by others
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Simultaneous access without proper co-authoring features can cause save conflicts

troubleshootingSteps.action: Compress media within the presentation using File > Compress Media before saving, if the file is very large due to videos or images
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This reduces the overall file size, which can resolve save failures related to size or timeout issues, especially on slower drives or network locations

possibleSolutions: Remove the read-only attribute from the file
Save to a different location to confirm the file works
Free up space on the destination drive
Fix or wait for the network connection to a shared drive
Rename the file to remove invalid characters
Compress media to reduce file size before saving
prevention: Regularly check available storage space
Avoid special characters in file names
Use a stable network connection when saving to shared drives
Compress media in presentations regularly to keep file size manageable

description: The user clicks to start the slide show, either from the beginning or the current slide, but nothing happens, an error appears, or the presentation freezes before displaying the first slide.

Error message appears when trying to start the slide show
Screen goes black or shows a loading indicator that never completes

A corrupted or problematic embedded object on the first slide causing a failure
Outdated graphics drivers affecting slide show rendering

Incorrect monitor selection settings when using an external display or projector
diagnosticQuestions: Are you presenting using a single monitor, or with an additional monitor or projector connected?
Does any error message appear, or does the slide show simply not start at all?
Have you tried starting from a different slide, rather than always the first one?
Does this happen with all presentations, or just this specific one?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if an external monitor or projector is connected and confirm the display settings are correctly configured in Windows
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Incorrect display configuration is a very common cause of slide shows failing to start properly, especially in presentation settings with a projector

troubleshootingSteps.action: In PowerPoint, go to Slide Show > Set Up Slide Show and confirm the correct monitor is selected if using multiple displays
troubleshootingSteps.reason: PowerPoint needs to know which screen to use for the full slide show versus Presenter View, and an incorrect setting can prevent the show from starting as expected

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try starting the slide show from a slide other than the first one, to see if the issue is specific to the first slide's content
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps identify if a specific object or element on the first slide is causing the failure to start

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a specific slide seems to be the trigger, check that slide for a potentially corrupted embedded video, image, or object
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A single corrupted embedded object can sometimes prevent the entire slide show from starting or cause it to crash immediately

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the computer's graphics driver, since slide show rendering, especially with multiple monitors, relies heavily on it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Outdated graphics drivers are a common cause of display-related failures when starting a slide show

troubleshootingSteps.action: Turn off Presenter View temporarily under Slide Show settings and try starting the show again with just the basic full-screen mode

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run Office Quick Repair if the problem happens consistently across multiple different presentations
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This addresses potential underlying installation issues affecting the slide show engine specifically

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test the presentation and its slide show functionality well in advance of any important live presentation
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This allows time to resolve display and slide show startup issues before they become a problem in front of an audience

possibleSolutions: Correct display and monitor selection settings
Fix or remove a corrupted embedded object on the problematic slide
Update the graphics driver
Temporarily disable Presenter View to isolate the issue
Run Office Quick Repair for persistent, cross-presentation issues
Test slide show functionality well before important presentations
prevention: Test slide shows with the actual presenting equipment in advance
Keep graphics drivers updated
Avoid embedding unnecessarily large or complex objects when simpler options exist
Confirm monitor and display settings before important presentations

problem: Images are not displaying in a presentation
description: The user opens a presentation and finds that images which should appear on the slides are showing as blank boxes, red X icons, or are simply missing entirely.
symptoms: Blank white or grey boxes where images should be
A small red X icon in the corner of an empty image placeholder
Images that displayed correctly before are now missing
Problem appears only on certain computers, not the one where the presentation was created
possibleCauses: Images were linked rather than embedded, and the linked image files have been moved or deleted
The presentation was transferred to a different computer without also transferring the linked image files
The image files themselves have become corrupted
A graphics driver issue affecting image rendering
Antivirus or security software blocking certain image file types from loading
diagnosticQuestions: Were the images inserted using 'Insert Picture' and embedded directly, or linked from an external file location?
Is this presentation being viewed on the same computer where it was originally created, or a different one?
Did the images display correctly before, and if so, what changed recently?
Do all images show as missing, or just some specific ones?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if all images are missing, or just specific ones, to help narrow down whether this is a widespread or isolated problem
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A pattern affecting only certain images often points to those specific files being linked and broken, rather than a general presentation-wide issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Click on an empty image placeholder to see if any information appears about a missing linked file path
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This can directly reveal if the image was linked to an external file rather than embedded, and show where PowerPoint expects to find it

troubleshootingSteps.action: If images were linked, locate the original image files and either move them back to their expected location, or reinsert them directly into the presentation
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This restores the connection between the presentation and its image content, or permanently embeds the images to avoid the issue in the future

troubleshootingSteps.action: For future presentations that need to be shared or moved, always insert images so they are embedded directly, which is PowerPoint's default and standard behavior when using the normal Insert Picture option
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This prevents the entire class of problems related to broken links when a presentation is moved to a different computer or folder

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the computer's graphics driver, since some display or rendering issues can prevent images from showing correctly even when the files themselves are intact
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This addresses a less common but still possible cause related to graphics rendering rather than missing files

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if antivirus or security software might be blocking or quarantining certain image file types, especially if the presentation was recently downloaded from the internet or an email attachment
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some security software can interfere with embedded or linked media in ways that cause images to fail to load

troubleshootingSteps.action: If specific image files appear corrupted, try replacing them with a fresh copy of the original image if available
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A corrupted individual image file cannot be repaired within PowerPoint and needs to be replaced with a working version

possibleSolutions: Locate and restore missing linked image files
Re-embed images directly into the presentation
Update the graphics driver
Check antivirus settings for interference with media files
Replace corrupted individual image files with fresh copies
prevention: Always embed images rather than linking them when possible
Keep presentations and their linked files together if linking is used
Test presentations on the target computer before important events
Keep graphics drivers updated

description: The computer cannot reach the internet at all. This may show as 'No Internet' next to the network icon, and no websites or online apps work.
symptoms: Network icon shows a red X or 'No Internet' warning
Browser shows 'This site can't be reached' for all websites
No apps that need internet will load or sync
possibleCauses: Modem or router is powered off or malfunctioning
ISP outage in the area
Cable (Ethernet) unplugged or WiFi disconnected
Wrong network settings (IP, DNS, gateway)
Network adapter driver problem
Firewall or antivirus blocking all traffic
diagnosticQuestions: Is only this computer affected, or all devices on the network?
Are the modem and router powered on with normal-looking lights?
Is this a wired or wireless connection?
Did this start suddenly or after any recent change, like a storm, move, or software install?

commands.purpose: Check the computer's current IP address, gateway, and DNS settings
commands.expectedResult: Valid IP address, subnet, gateway, and DNS shown for the active adapter
commands.abnormalResult: No IP address, or an address starting with 169.254.x.x, meaning no valid network config was received

commands.purpose: Test raw internet connectivity to a known reliable IP address, bypassing DNS
commands.expectedResult: Replies received
commands.abnormalResult: Request timed out, meaning there is no path to the internet at all

commands.purpose: Test internet connectivity including DNS name resolution
commands.expectedResult: Replies received with google.com resolved to an IP
commands.abnormalResult: 'Ping request could not find host' means a DNS problem rather than a raw connectivity problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if other devices on the same network (phone, another computer) also have no internet
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines if the problem is with this computer specifically or the whole network/ISP

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the modem and router for normal status lights, especially the internet/WAN light
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An abnormal or off WAN light usually points to an ISP-side or modem problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run ipconfig /all to check if the computer has a valid IP address
troubleshootingSteps.reason: No valid IP means the computer never properly joined the local network

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping 8.8.8.8 to test raw connectivity, then ping google.com to test DNS
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Separates a pure connectivity problem from a DNS-only problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the modem and router by powering them off for 30 seconds, then back on
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves the majority of temporary ISP and router connection issues

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the ISP if the WAN light stays off or red after a restart
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Indicates an outage or line problem outside the local network

possibleSolutions: Restart modem and router
Check and reseat all cables
Renew the IP address with ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew
Contact ISP if the outage is confirmed on their end
Update or reinstall the network adapter driver
prevention: Use a surge protector for modem and router
Keep router firmware updated
Avoid unplugging networking equipment during active updates

description: The network icon shows a normal connected status, but web pages will not load in the browser.
symptoms: Network status shows connected with no warning icon
Browser shows 'This site can't be reached' or keeps loading forever
Other network apps like games or file sync may still work
possibleCauses: DNS server not resolving website names
Browser-specific issue like cache, extensions, or proxy settings
Firewall blocking the browser specifically
ISP DNS server down
Malware redirecting or blocking browser traffic
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen in all browsers or just one?
Can you browse using a mobile data connection to compare?
Have you tried visiting a website by typing its raw IP address?
Were any new browser extensions or antivirus programs installed recently?

commands.purpose: Check if raw internet connectivity works even though browsing fails
commands.expectedResult: Replies received, confirming the internet connection itself is fine
commands.abnormalResult: Timeout would mean this is not just a browser issue but a deeper connectivity problem

commands.purpose: Test whether DNS name resolution is working
commands.expectedResult: Returns an IP address for google.com
commands.abnormalResult: 'DNS request timed out' or no answer means DNS resolution is failing

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping 8.8.8.8 to confirm the raw internet connection works
troubleshootingSteps.reason: If this succeeds, the problem is isolated to DNS or the browser, not the network connection itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run nslookup on a well-known domain to test DNS resolution
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether DNS is the specific point of failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different browser to see if the problem is browser-specific
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Narrows the cause to one application versus the whole system

troubleshootingSteps.action: Change the DNS server to a public one like 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1 in network adapter settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Bypasses a malfunctioning ISP DNS server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Clear the browser cache and disable extensions one by one
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Corrupted cache or a bad extension can block or break page loading

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run a malware scan if the problem persists across all browsers and DNS changes
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some malware intercepts or redirects browser traffic silently

possibleSolutions: Change DNS server to a public DNS like 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1
Clear browser cache and cookies
Disable browser extensions one at a time to find the culprit
Run a malware/antivirus scan
Reset the browser to default settings
prevention: Keep browser and extensions updated
Avoid installing browser extensions from unknown sources
Periodically clear browser cache

description: Windows shows 'Limited' next to the network connection, meaning the device is connected to the local network but cannot reach the internet properly.
symptoms: Network icon shows a yellow warning triangle or 'Limited' status
Local network devices may be reachable, but internet is not
Sometimes intermittently works then drops back to limited
possibleCauses: Router failed to provide internet access even though local connection is fine
APIPA address (169.254.x.x) assigned instead of a real DHCP address
Router's WAN connection to the ISP is down
Network adapter driver issue

Is the router's internet/WAN light on and normal?
Can you access other devices on the local network, like a printer or another computer?
Does restarting the adapter or router fix it temporarily?

commands.purpose: Check the current IP address type and range
commands.expectedResult: A normal private IP like 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x
commands.abnormalResult: An address starting with 169.254.x.x (APIPA) confirms no valid DHCP address was received

commands.purpose: Release the current IP address configuration
commands.expectedResult: Adapter releases its IP with no error
commands.abnormalResult: Error releasing may indicate a deeper adapter or driver issue

commands.purpose: Request a new IP address from the DHCP server
commands.expectedResult: A valid new IP address is assigned
commands.abnormalResult: Renewal fails or still returns a 169.254.x.x address, pointing to a DHCP or router problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the IP address with ipconfig to see if it is an APIPA (169.254.x.x) address

troubleshootingSteps.action: Release and renew the IP address using ipconfig /release then ipconfig /renew

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router if renewal fails or the same APIPA address returns

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router's WAN status to confirm it has internet from the ISP
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A router without WAN internet can still hand out local IPs but with limited access

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the network adapter driver if the problem is isolated to one computer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An outdated or corrupted driver can prevent proper DHCP negotiation

possibleSolutions: Release and renew the IP address
Restart the router
Update the network adapter driver
Manually set a static IP as a temporary workaround
Check ISP status if the router's WAN connection is down
prevention: Keep router firmware updated
Ensure the router's DHCP pool is large enough for all connected devices
Restart the router periodically if it is older hardware

description: The internet connection works but is much slower than expected, with pages loading slowly and downloads taking longer than normal.

Download and upload speeds are far below the subscribed plan
Speed test results are consistently low

ISP throttling or an outage affecting speed
Malware or background applications using bandwidth
Outdated router hardware or firmware

How many devices are actively using the internet right now?
Have you run a speed test, and how does it compare to your subscribed plan?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check how many devices are connected and actively using bandwidth, such as downloads or streaming

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the modem and router

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for background applications or updates consuming bandwidth on the affected computer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Compare the speed test result to the plan speed from the ISP

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the ISP if wired speeds are consistently far below the subscribed plan
troubleshootingSteps.reason: May indicate a line problem or an area-wide issue on their end

possibleSolutions: Connect via Ethernet cable to rule out WiFi issues
Limit the number of simultaneous heavy-bandwidth devices
Restart modem and router
Close bandwidth-heavy background applications
Contact ISP if wired speed remains consistently low
prevention: Regularly restart networking equipment
Keep router firmware updated for best performance
Position the router centrally to improve WiFi speed for all devices

description: The internet connection drops and reconnects repeatedly throughout the day instead of staying stable.
symptoms: Internet works, then disconnects briefly, then reconnects on its own

Network icon flickers between connected and disconnected

WiFi interference from other devices or networks
Overheating router or modem
ISP-side intermittent line issue

IP address conflict causing intermittent drops

Does the router or modem feel warm or hot to the touch?

commands.purpose: Continuously ping to observe exactly when and how often the connection drops

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run a continuous ping test while using the computer normally to capture the exact drop pattern

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check and reseat all physical cable connections, or try a different cable

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the router or modem feels excessively warm and ensure it has proper ventilation

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the network adapter driver on the affected computer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the ISP to check the line if the issue affects all devices and persists after equipment checks
troubleshootingSteps.reason: May indicate an external line quality issue

possibleSolutions: Replace damaged or loose cables
Improve router ventilation and placement
Reduce WiFi interference sources
Update network adapter drivers
Contact ISP to check line quality if the problem is network-wide
prevention: Use quality cables and connectors
Keep networking equipment in a cool, ventilated location
Regularly update router firmware and device drivers

description: The internet connection disconnects completely and requires manual reconnection or a router restart multiple times per day.

Manual reconnect or router restart is needed each time

ISP modem/router experiencing hardware failure

Power supply issues to the router or modem
diagnosticQuestions: How many times per day does this happen, roughly?
Does restarting the router fix it every time, or does it sometimes need longer to recover?
How old is the router/modem, and has firmware ever been updated?
How many devices are typically connected to this network?

commands.purpose: Check for a valid IP address after a disconnect to see how the computer's network state looks
commands.expectedResult: A valid, current IP address and gateway
commands.abnormalResult: Missing or APIPA address suggests the router itself dropped and did not properly hand out addresses

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router's firmware version and update to the latest available version
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many frequent-disconnect issues are fixed by manufacturers in firmware updates

troubleshootingSteps.action: Count and review all connected devices for one that might be overloading the router, such as a device downloading heavily
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An overloaded router can crash or drop connections under heavy load

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the power supply and cable to the router/modem for looseness or damage
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Power interruptions can cause the equipment to reset unexpectedly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Perform a factory reset on the router if firmware updates do not help
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears any corrupted configuration causing instability

troubleshootingSteps.action: Replace the router if it is old and resets continue after a factory reset and firmware update
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Aging hardware often becomes unstable over time

possibleSolutions: Update router firmware
Reduce the number of connected devices or upgrade to router hardware that supports more devices
Check and secure the power connection to the router
Factory reset the router if problems continue
Replace aging router hardware
prevention: Keep firmware updated on a regular schedule
Avoid overloading a single router with excessive devices
Use a UPS to protect against power fluctuations

description: Network responses take longer than normal, causing lag in video calls, online games, or any real-time application, even though the connection is otherwise working.
symptoms: Video calls have noticeable delay or lag
Online games show high ping numbers
Ping tests return high response times, for example over 100-150ms for a normally low-latency connection
possibleCauses: Network congestion from other devices
WiFi instead of wired connection adding latency
ISP routing issue or distant server location
Router processing overload
Background applications consuming bandwidth
diagnosticQuestions: What ping time are you seeing, and what would you normally expect?
Is this happening on WiFi or a wired connection?
Does the high latency happen with everything, or only specific applications or servers?
Are other devices on the network actively using a lot of bandwidth right now?

commands.purpose: Measure average latency over multiple pings to a general destination
commands.expectedResult: Consistent, low response times appropriate for the connection type
commands.abnormalResult: Consistently high or highly variable response times confirm a latency problem

commands.purpose: Identify at which hop along the route latency increases significantly
commands.expectedResult: Latency increases gradually and reasonably at each hop
commands.abnormalResult: A large latency jump at a specific hop points to where the delay is being introduced, such as the ISP or a specific server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run a ping test to a well-known server to measure current latency
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes a baseline number to work with

troubleshootingSteps.action: Switch from WiFi to a wired Ethernet connection if possible and re-test
troubleshootingSteps.reason: WiFi commonly adds extra latency compared to a wired connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for other devices or applications using heavy bandwidth at the same time
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Congestion from other traffic increases queuing delay

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run tracert to see where along the path latency increases sharply
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps determine if the delay is local, at the ISP, or further along the internet route

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router to clear any processing overload
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves temporary router performance issues contributing to latency

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the ISP if tracert shows the delay starting outside the local network
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The issue may be in their network or peering routes, outside local control

possibleSolutions: Switch to a wired connection to reduce latency
Reduce simultaneous bandwidth usage from other devices
Restart the router
Contact the ISP if the delay is confirmed to originate outside the local network
prevention: Use wired connections for latency-sensitive activities like gaming or video calls
Avoid heavy downloads during important real-time sessions
Choose servers geographically closer when possible for online applications

description: Some data packets sent over the network never arrive at their destination, causing choppy calls, game rubber-banding, or incomplete data transfers.
symptoms: Video or voice calls sound choppy or cut out briefly
Online games show rubber-banding or missed hits
Ping tests show some requests timing out while others succeed
possibleCauses: Weak or interfered WiFi signal
Damaged network cable or faulty port
Network congestion overloading equipment
Faulty router, switch, or modem hardware
ISP-side network issue
diagnosticQuestions: Is this happening on WiFi or a wired connection?
What percentage of packet loss are you seeing in a ping test?
Does packet loss happen constantly or only at certain times of day?
Have you tried testing from a different device or location to compare?

commands.purpose: Send many pings to calculate a percentage of lost packets
commands.expectedResult: 0% packet loss, or very close to it
commands.abnormalResult: Noticeable packet loss percentage (for example, above 1-2%) confirms a real problem

commands.purpose: Identify which hop in the network path is dropping packets
commands.expectedResult: All hops respond consistently
commands.abnormalResult: A specific hop showing repeated timeouts or high loss indicates where the problem is occurring

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run an extended ping test and check the packet loss percentage in the summary
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Quantifies the severity of the problem with concrete numbers

troubleshootingSteps.action: Switch to a wired connection if currently on WiFi and re-test
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Wireless interference is a very common cause of packet loss

troubleshootingSteps.action: Inspect and replace network cables between the computer, switch, and router
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A damaged cable can cause consistent packet loss

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run tracert to identify which specific hop is dropping packets
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps determine if the loss is local, at the router, or somewhere in the ISP's network

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart networking equipment (router, switch, modem) to rule out a temporary hardware glitch
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears buffer overflows or temporary faults causing packet drops

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the ISP if packet loss is confirmed beyond the local network in the tracert results
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The issue lies outside what can be fixed locally

possibleSolutions: Switch from WiFi to a wired connection
Replace damaged network cables
Restart routers, switches, and modems
Contact the ISP if loss is confirmed on their network segment
prevention: Use quality, undamaged cables
Position WiFi routers to minimize interference and obstruction
Monitor network equipment for early signs of hardware failure

description: The internet works normally for most sites, but one or a few specific websites will not load, while everything else works fine.
symptoms: Most websites load normally
One or a few specific sites time out, show an error, or never load
Other devices may or may not have the same problem with those sites
possibleCauses: The specific website itself is down or having issues
DNS cache holding outdated or incorrect information for that site
ISP or regional block/throttling of that specific site
Firewall or security software blocking that particular domain
Browser-specific cache or cookie issue for that site
diagnosticQuestions: Which specific website or websites are affected?
Does the site fail on all your devices, or just this one?
Have you tried accessing the site from a different network, like mobile data?
Have you tried clearing your browser cache or using a private/incognito window for that site?

commands.purpose: Check basic reachability to the specific website's server
commands.expectedResult: Replies received (though some sites block ping deliberately)
commands.abnormalResult: Timeout may indicate a routing or blocking issue, though it is not conclusive since many sites disable ping responses

commands.purpose: Confirm the domain resolves to a valid IP address
commands.expectedResult: Returns a valid IP address for the domain
commands.abnormalResult: No response or an unexpected IP may indicate a DNS caching or resolution problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the website is down for everyone using a third-party outage checking site or by testing from another network
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out a problem on your end if the site itself is having issues

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try opening the site in a private/incognito browser window
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Bypasses cached cookies and data that might be causing the specific site to fail

troubleshootingSteps.action: Flush the DNS cache using ipconfig /flushdns
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears any outdated or corrupted cached DNS entry for that specific domain

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try accessing the site using a different DNS server, such as 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some ISP DNS servers have issues resolving specific domains correctly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check firewall or security software logs for the domain being specifically blocked
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Security software or parental controls sometimes block specific sites intentionally

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test the site from mobile data to determine if the block is specific to this network
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the restriction is local (ISP/router/firewall) or on the site's end

possibleSolutions: Flush the DNS cache
Try a different public DNS server
Clear browser cache/cookies or use a private window
Check and adjust firewall or security software rules for that domain
Wait if the site itself is confirmed down
prevention: Keep a note of frequently used sites' normal behavior to quickly spot anomalies
Keep DNS and security software configurations well documented
Regularly clear browser cache to avoid stale site data

problem: Internet Works on Other Devices Only
description: Every device on the network has internet access except one specific computer, which shows no connection or limited access.
symptoms: Phones, tablets, and other computers connect fine
One specific computer has no internet or limited access
Problem persists even after restarting the router
possibleCauses: Network adapter driver issue on the affected computer
IP address conflict specific to that device
Incorrect network settings (static IP, DNS, proxy) on that computer only
Firewall or security software on that computer blocking traffic
Faulty network adapter hardware or cable specific to that device
diagnosticQuestions: Is this a wired or wireless connection on the affected computer?
Have any network settings been manually changed on this computer, like a static IP or proxy?
Does the problem happen only on this network, or also elsewhere?
Was any new security software or VPN installed recently on this computer?

commands.purpose: Check the affected computer's specific network configuration for problems
commands.expectedResult: Valid IP, subnet, gateway, and DNS matching the rest of the network
commands.abnormalResult: APIPA address, wrong subnet, incorrect static IP, or missing gateway explains why only this device fails

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run ipconfig /all on the affected computer and compare its settings to a working device on the same network
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Quickly reveals if the configuration is different or invalid on the problem computer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for a manually configured static IP, DNS, or proxy setting that may be incorrect
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Manual settings are a common cause of a single device failing while others work fine

troubleshootingSteps.action: Set the network adapter back to automatic (DHCP) IP and DNS settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Removes any incorrect manual configuration as the cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Temporarily disable firewall or security software to test if it is blocking the connection
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Overly aggressive security software can block all internet traffic on just one machine

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different network cable or, for WiFi, try a different WiFi adapter if available, to test for a hardware fault
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Isolates whether the issue is a failing physical network component

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update or reinstall the network adapter driver
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A corrupted or outdated driver can cause connectivity to fail on just this device

possibleSolutions: Reset network adapter settings to automatic (DHCP)
Disable conflicting security software temporarily to test
Update or reinstall the network adapter driver
Replace a faulty cable or adapter
prevention: Avoid manually changing network settings unless necessary and well documented
Keep network drivers updated
Review security software rules after installation to ensure they don't block normal traffic
keywords: other devices work fine but not this one

description: Windows or the network status shows the Ethernet cable as unplugged, even though a cable appears to be connected.
symptoms: Notification or icon says 'Network cable unplugged'
No network connection through the wired port
Cable appears physically connected
possibleCauses: Cable not fully seated in the port
Damaged cable or connector
Faulty Ethernet port on the computer or router/switch
Cable plugged into the wrong port
Network adapter disabled
diagnosticQuestions: Have you tried unplugging and firmly replugging the cable at both ends?
Have you tried a different, known-working cable?
Does the port's link light turn on when the cable is plugged in?
Have you tried plugging the cable into a different port on the router or switch?

commands.purpose: Check the Ethernet adapter's current status
commands.expectedResult: Adapter shows 'Media State: Media disconnected' only if truly unplugged; otherwise a valid IP appears
commands.abnormalResult: Persistent 'Media disconnected' despite a plugged-in cable confirms a physical link problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Unplug the Ethernet cable and firmly reinsert it at both the computer and router/switch ends until it clicks
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A cable not fully seated is the most common and simplest cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the small link/activity light near the Ethernet port lights up when connected
troubleshootingSteps.reason: No light at all usually confirms a physical connection or port problem rather than a software issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different, known-working Ethernet cable
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out a damaged cable as the cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try plugging into a different port on the router or switch
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Isolates whether the router/switch port itself has failed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Device Manager to confirm the network adapter is enabled and not disabled or missing
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A disabled adapter can sometimes show a similar 'unplugged' style message

possibleSolutions: Firmly reseat the cable at both ends
Replace a damaged Ethernet cable
Use a different port on the router or switch
Enable the network adapter if it was disabled
prevention: Use good quality cables and avoid excessive bending or pulling
Label and route cables neatly to avoid accidental disconnection
Periodically inspect cable connectors for wear

description: The Ethernet connection shows as 'Not connected' in network settings, with no active link to the router or switch.
symptoms: Ethernet adapter listed but shows 'Not connected' status
No internet or local network access via the wired connection
May happen consistently or only sometimes
possibleCauses: Cable, port, or adapter hardware fault
Adapter disabled in Windows or Device Manager
Driver issue preventing the adapter from establishing a link
Switch or router port not active or misconfigured
Duplex/speed mismatch between adapter and switch
diagnosticQuestions: Does the port's link light turn on with the cable connected?
Is the network adapter enabled in Device Manager and network settings?
Has this connection worked before on this exact cable and port?
Have any recent driver or Windows updates been installed?

commands.purpose: View detailed adapter state including media connection status
commands.expectedResult: Shows a connected state with a valid IP address
commands.abnormalResult: Shows 'Media disconnected' or the adapter missing entirely

commands.purpose: View the status of all network adapters from PowerShell
commands.expectedResult: Ethernet adapter status shows 'Up'
commands.abnormalResult: Status shows 'Disabled', 'Disconnected', or the adapter is missing from the list

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the cable is properly connected and check for a link light on both ends
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out a basic physical connection issue first

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Device Manager to ensure the Ethernet adapter is enabled and has no warning icons
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A disabled or malfunctioning adapter will never show as connected

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run Get-NetAdapter in PowerShell to check the adapter's detailed status
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Gives clear technical confirmation of whether the adapter itself is up or down

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update or reinstall the Ethernet adapter driver
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A corrupted or incompatible driver can prevent the adapter from establishing a link

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test the same cable and port with another device if possible
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the fault is with this specific computer or the network side

possibleSolutions: Reseat or replace the cable
Enable the adapter in Device Manager if disabled
Update or reinstall the Ethernet driver
Test the port/cable with another device to isolate the fault
prevention: Keep network adapter drivers updated
Avoid disabling network adapters unless necessary
Regularly inspect physical connections on frequently moved equipment

description: The Ethernet connection shows as connected with a valid IP address, but there is still no internet access.
symptoms: Ethernet status shows 'Connected' with no warning
Local network devices may be reachable
Websites and online services do not load
possibleCauses: Router has no internet from the ISP (WAN down)
DNS server not resolving correctly
Incorrect gateway configuration
Firewall blocking internet traffic despite local connectivity
ISP outage
diagnosticQuestions: Does the network icon show fully connected with no warning triangle?
Can you access other devices on the local network, like a shared printer or file server?
Can you ping the router's IP address successfully?
Does the router's WAN/internet light look normal?

commands.purpose: Confirm the computer has a valid local IP, gateway, and DNS
commands.expectedResult: Valid private IP address with a correct gateway matching the router
commands.abnormalResult: Missing or incorrect gateway/DNS entries explain the lack of internet despite local connection

commands.purpose: Test connectivity to the router itself
commands.expectedResult: Replies received, confirming the local network segment works
commands.abnormalResult: Timeout means even the local connection to the router has an issue

commands.purpose: Test connectivity beyond the local router to the wider internet
commands.expectedResult: Replies received
commands.abnormalResult: Timeout while the gateway ping succeeds confirms the router itself has no internet (WAN down)

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the router's gateway IP address to confirm the local connection is healthy
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Separates a local network problem from an internet (WAN) problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping a known public IP address like 8.8.8.8 to test beyond the router
troubleshootingSteps.reason: If the gateway responds but this fails, the problem is the router's internet connection, not the computer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router's WAN/internet status light and admin page for a connected status
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the router itself has lost its ISP connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the modem and router
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves many temporary WAN connectivity issues

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check firewall settings on the computer if other devices on the same network do have internet
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A local firewall issue can block internet while allowing local network access

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the ISP if the router confirms no WAN connection after a restart
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Indicates an outage or line issue outside local control

possibleSolutions: Restart modem and router to restore WAN connection
Check and correct DNS/gateway settings
Adjust firewall rules if only this device is affected
Contact ISP if WAN remains down after restart
prevention: Monitor router WAN status periodically
Keep modem and router firmware updated
Use a UPS to prevent power-related WAN drops

description: Windows shows the network as 'Unidentified Network' after connecting an Ethernet cable, often with limited or no internet access.
symptoms: Network name shows as 'Unidentified Network' in Windows
Network may be categorized as public even on a trusted network
Internet access may be limited or missing
possibleCauses: Windows could not properly detect the network's identity or gateway
Router or switch not responding correctly to network discovery
IP configuration incomplete or incorrect
Faulty cable or port causing an unstable connection
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen every time you connect, or only occasionally?
Is this a new router, network, or cable setup?
Does ipconfig show a complete IP configuration including a gateway?
Have you tried a different cable or port?

commands.purpose: Check whether the adapter received a complete network configuration
commands.expectedResult: Full configuration including IP, subnet, gateway, and DNS
commands.abnormalResult: Missing gateway or an APIPA address explains why Windows cannot identify the network

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run ipconfig /all to check if a complete network configuration, including a gateway, was received
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incomplete configuration is the most common reason Windows cannot identify the network

troubleshootingSteps.action: Release and renew the IP address using ipconfig /release and ipconfig /renew
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Forces a fresh, hopefully complete, configuration request

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different cable and port to rule out a physical fault causing an unstable connection
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An unstable link can prevent Windows from fully completing network detection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the computer and the router/switch
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears temporary state issues on both ends that may prevent proper identification

troubleshootingSteps.action: Manually set the network profile to Private if identification issues persist but connectivity is otherwise fine
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Allows normal local network features to work even if auto-identification is imperfect

possibleSolutions: Release and renew the IP configuration
