Try a different cable or port
Restart the computer and networking equipment
Manually set the network profile if needed
prevention: Ensure the router's DHCP service is functioning properly for all clients
Use quality cables to maintain a stable link
Keep network adapter drivers updated

description: The Ethernet network adapter has been disabled in Windows, so the wired connection cannot be used at all.
symptoms: Ethernet adapter shows greyed out in Network Connections
No Ethernet option appears active in network settings
Right-click menu shows an option to 'Enable' rather than 'Disable'
possibleCauses: Adapter was accidentally disabled by a user
Group Policy or IT management disabled the adapter
A driver or Windows update disabled the adapter
Power management settings turned off the adapter
diagnosticQuestions: Was the adapter intentionally disabled by anyone recently, such as during troubleshooting?
Is this a personal computer or a managed work/school computer?
Did this happen after a Windows update?
Are other adapters, like WiFi, working normally?

commands.purpose: List all network adapters and their enabled/disabled status
commands.expectedResult: Ethernet adapter status shows 'Up' or at least 'Disconnected' rather than 'Disabled'
commands.abnormalResult: Status shows 'Disabled', confirming the adapter itself is turned off

commands.purpose: Enable a disabled Ethernet adapter from PowerShell
commands.expectedResult: Adapter status changes to enabled/connected
commands.abnormalResult: Access denied error means PowerShell needs to be run as Administrator, or Group Policy is preventing the change

troubleshootingSteps.action: Open Network Connections (ncpa.cpl) and check if the Ethernet adapter icon appears greyed out
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms visually whether the adapter is disabled

troubleshootingSteps.action: Right-click the adapter and select 'Enable'
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the direct and simplest fix if the adapter was just turned off

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the option is greyed out or reverts back to disabled, check with IT if this is a managed/work computer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Group Policy on managed computers can intentionally keep certain adapters disabled

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check adapter power management settings under Device Manager to ensure 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' is unchecked
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Aggressive power saving can effectively disable the adapter under certain conditions

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the computer after enabling the adapter
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures the change takes full effect

possibleSolutions: Enable the adapter through Network Connections or Device Manager
Check and adjust power management settings for the adapter
Check with IT/administrator if Group Policy is disabling the adapter on a managed device
prevention: Avoid disabling network adapters unless necessary for troubleshooting
Document any intentional Group Policy restrictions for managed devices
Regularly review power management settings after Windows updates

description: The Ethernet adapter does not appear at all in Network Connections or Device Manager, as if the hardware does not exist.
symptoms: No Ethernet adapter listed in Network Connections
Device Manager does not show the Ethernet controller, or shows it as unknown
Wired connection cannot be configured or used at all
possibleCauses: Network adapter driver not installed
Motherboard's onboard network hardware failure
Adapter disabled at the BIOS/UEFI level
Recent Windows update removed or corrupted the driver
Physical hardware fault, especially on desktop motherboards
diagnosticQuestions: Is this a laptop or desktop, and is the Ethernet port built-in or a separate USB adapter?
Did this start after a Windows update, reinstall, or hardware change?
Have you checked Device Manager under 'Other devices' or 'Network adapters' for anything with a warning icon?
Have you checked the BIOS/UEFI settings to confirm onboard LAN is enabled?

commands.purpose: List all network-related devices Windows can detect, including ones without working drivers
commands.expectedResult: Ethernet controller listed with status 'OK'
commands.abnormalResult: Ethernet controller missing entirely, or listed with an error/unknown status

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Device Manager under 'Network adapters' and also 'Other devices' for anything unrecognized
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A missing driver often shows the hardware as an unknown device rather than disappearing completely

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the computer's BIOS/UEFI settings to confirm onboard LAN/Ethernet is enabled
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some systems allow disabling onboard network hardware at the firmware level

troubleshootingSteps.action: Download and install the correct network adapter driver directly from the motherboard or laptop manufacturer's website
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures Windows has the correct driver to recognize and use the hardware

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a USB-to-Ethernet adapter as a test if the built-in port is suspected to have failed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps determine if this is a hardware failure versus a software/driver issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider professional repair or a USB Ethernet adapter as a permanent workaround if onboard hardware has failed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A confirmed hardware failure on a motherboard's LAN chip typically cannot be fixed through software

possibleSolutions: Install the correct network adapter driver from the manufacturer
Enable onboard LAN in BIOS/UEFI if disabled
Use a USB-to-Ethernet adapter as a workaround for failed hardware
Seek professional repair for confirmed hardware failure
prevention: Keep chipset and network drivers updated
Avoid unnecessary BIOS/UEFI changes to hardware settings
Keep a USB Ethernet adapter on hand as a backup for critical systems

description: The Ethernet adapter hardware is recognized by Windows, but no driver is installed, so it cannot be used to connect to a network.
symptoms: Device Manager shows the Ethernet controller with a yellow warning icon
Error message: 'The drivers for this device are not installed'
No Ethernet option available in network settings
possibleCauses: Fresh Windows installation without network drivers
Driver was uninstalled or corrupted
Windows Update did not provide a compatible driver automatically
diagnosticQuestions: Was this a fresh Windows installation or reset?
Do you have another way to get online, such as WiFi or a USB drive with the driver on another computer?
What is the exact motherboard or laptop model, to find the correct driver?

commands.purpose: Confirm the adapter is detected as hardware even without a working driver
commands.expectedResult: Device listed with a status indicating a driver problem
commands.abnormalResult: Status explicitly shows 'Error' or 'Unknown', confirming the driver is missing or not functioning

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Device Manager for the Ethernet controller under 'Other devices' with a warning icon
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the hardware is detected but lacks a working driver

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use another internet-connected device to download the correct driver from the motherboard or laptop manufacturer's website
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Without a network driver, this computer cannot download it itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: Transfer the driver installer to the affected computer using a USB drive
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides the only way to install the driver without existing network access

troubleshootingSteps.action: Install the driver and restart the computer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Completes the installation and applies the changes

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the Ethernet adapter now appears normally in Device Manager and Network Connections
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Verifies the driver installed correctly and the adapter is usable

possibleSolutions: Download and install the correct driver from the manufacturer using another device, then transfer via USB
Use Windows Update to search for a compatible driver if any other network connection is available
Run the manufacturer's full driver support package if available
prevention: Keep a copy of network drivers saved externally for quick recovery after OS reinstalls
Check manufacturer support pages for driver downloads before reinstalling Windows
Use a USB WiFi adapter as an alternative internet source during recovery

description: The Ethernet driver is installed but not functioning correctly, causing connection failures, errors, or inconsistent behavior.
symptoms: Adapter shows in Device Manager but with a warning icon or error code
Connection frequently drops or fails to establish
Error codes like 'Code 10' or 'Code 31' appear in Device Manager
possibleCauses: Driver files corrupted due to an incomplete update or crash
Conflict with another recently installed driver or software
Malware damage to system driver files
Incompatible driver version for the current Windows build
diagnosticQuestions: What exact error code, if any, shows in Device Manager for this adapter?
Did this start after a Windows update or new software installation?
Have you tried updating or reinstalling the driver already?
Does the problem happen consistently or only intermittently?

commands.purpose: List network devices currently reporting an error status
commands.expectedResult: No devices returned (no errors)
commands.abnormalResult: Ethernet adapter listed, confirming a driver-level error

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the exact error code shown in Device Manager for the adapter
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Specific error codes point to specific documented causes and fixes from Microsoft

troubleshootingSteps.action: Uninstall the driver completely through Device Manager, including deleting the driver software if prompted
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures no corrupted files remain before reinstalling

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the computer to let Windows attempt to reinstall a basic driver automatically
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Windows often reinstalls a default driver on restart after removal

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the basic driver does not resolve it, manually install the latest driver from the manufacturer's website
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides a clean, up-to-date, and compatible driver

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run a malware scan if driver corruption happens repeatedly without a clear cause
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out malicious software damaging system files

possibleSolutions: Uninstall and reinstall the Ethernet driver completely
Install the latest driver from the manufacturer's website
Run System File Checker (sfc /scannow) to repair corrupted system files
Run a malware scan if corruption recurs
prevention: Keep drivers updated through official manufacturer channels
Avoid interrupting driver installations or Windows updates
Run regular malware scans to protect system files

description: The network connection works but is limited to 100 Mbps instead of the expected higher gigabit speed, even though the hardware supports it.
symptoms: Network adapter properties show link speed as 100 Mbps instead of 1.0 Gbps
File transfers between local devices are slower than expected
Internet speed itself may be fine if the plan is under 100 Mbps, but local transfers suffer
possibleCauses: Damaged or low-category cable (Cat5 instead of Cat5e/Cat6)
Faulty port on the switch, router, or computer negotiating at a lower speed
Auto-negotiation failure between devices
Outdated network driver limiting speed
diagnosticQuestions: What category of Ethernet cable is being used, if known (Cat5, Cat5e, Cat6)?
Are both the computer's network adapter and the switch/router port gigabit-capable?
Has this always been 100 Mbps, or did it recently drop from a higher speed?
Have you tried a different cable or port?

commands.purpose: Check the currently negotiated link speed of the network adapter
commands.expectedResult: Shows 1 Gbps or higher on capable hardware
commands.abnormalResult: Shows 100 Mbps despite gigabit-capable hardware, confirming a negotiation or cable issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the network adapter's reported link speed using Get-NetAdapter or adapter properties
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the actual negotiated speed versus the expected capability

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the Ethernet cable is at least Cat5e, ideally Cat6, since older Cat5 cables cannot support gigabit speeds reliably
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Cable category is a very common and simple cause of this limitation

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different cable and a different port on the switch or router
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out a damaged cable or a switch/router port stuck at a lower negotiated speed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the adapter's advanced settings for a manually forced speed setting instead of auto-negotiation
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A manually forced 100 Mbps setting will override the hardware's true capability

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the network adapter driver to the latest version
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Driver bugs can sometimes cause incorrect speed negotiation

possibleSolutions: Replace the cable with a Cat5e or Cat6 cable
Try a different switch/router port
Set the adapter speed/duplex setting to 'Auto Negotiation' instead of a fixed value
Update the network adapter driver
prevention: Use Cat5e or better cabling for all new installations
Label cable categories during installation for future reference
Keep adapter settings on auto-negotiation unless there is a specific reason to force a setting

description: The small link/activity light next to the Ethernet port is completely off or stays solid without ever blinking, suggesting no active data connection.
symptoms: Link light is off or does not blink during normal use
No network connectivity through the wired port
May be accompanied by a 'cable unplugged' message
possibleCauses: Cable not properly connected or damaged
Faulty port on the computer, switch, or router
Adapter disabled or driver not functioning
No power to the switch or router the cable connects to
diagnosticQuestions: Is the light completely off, or on but never blinking during activity?
Have you confirmed both ends of the cable are firmly connected?
Is the switch or router the cable connects to powered on?
Have you tested this exact cable and port combination with another device?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the switch or router on the other end of the cable is powered on
troubleshootingSteps.reason: No power on the far end means there will never be a link, regardless of the local port

troubleshootingSteps.action: Firmly reseat the cable at both ends
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A loose connection can prevent the link light from activating even if it looks plugged in

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different, known-working cable
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out a damaged cable preventing link establishment

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different port on the switch or router
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Isolates whether the specific port on the networking equipment has failed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Device Manager to confirm the network adapter is enabled and has no driver errors
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A disabled or malfunctioning adapter will not establish a link even with a good cable

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test the cable and port with a different computer if the problem persists
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the issue is with this specific computer's port/adapter or the networking equipment

possibleSolutions: Reseat or replace the cable
Use a different port on the switch/router
Confirm power to the switch/router
Enable or repair the network adapter on the computer
prevention: Regularly inspect physical connections on critical systems
Label and test spare cables periodically
Keep networking equipment powered by a UPS to avoid unexpected outages

description: Neither the Ethernet nor WiFi adapter (or a specific one) is detected by the operating system at all, leaving no way to configure networking.
symptoms: No network adapters appear in Network Connections
Device Manager shows no network adapters, or an unknown device
No way to connect to any network, wired or wireless, depending on which adapter is affected
possibleCauses: Driver not installed for the adapter
Hardware failure of the network adapter
Adapter disabled in BIOS/UEFI
Physical damage to the adapter, especially for add-in cards or USB adapters
diagnosticQuestions: Is this affecting the Ethernet adapter, WiFi adapter, or both?
Is this a built-in adapter or an external USB/PCIe adapter?
Did this happen after a Windows reinstall, update, or hardware change?
Have you checked BIOS/UEFI to confirm the adapter is enabled?

commands.purpose: List all network devices Windows can detect, even with driver problems
commands.expectedResult: All expected adapters listed with 'OK' status
commands.abnormalResult: Adapters missing entirely, indicating either a disabled, failed, or undetected hardware component

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Device Manager thoroughly, including 'Other devices' and hidden devices, for any trace of the adapter
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An adapter without a driver often appears as an unknown device rather than disappearing completely

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check BIOS/UEFI settings to confirm the relevant onboard adapter is enabled
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some systems allow network adapters to be disabled at the firmware level

troubleshootingSteps.action: For external adapters, try a different USB port or PCIe slot
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out a faulty port or slot rather than the adapter itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: Install the correct driver from the manufacturer using another computer with internet access if needed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides the correct driver when Windows cannot detect or auto-install one

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider the adapter hardware failed if it still is not detected after driver installation and BIOS checks, and plan for replacement
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms a hardware fault that software troubleshooting cannot resolve

possibleSolutions: Enable the adapter in BIOS/UEFI if disabled
Install the correct manufacturer driver
Try a different port/slot for external adapters
Replace the adapter if hardware failure is confirmed
prevention: Keep BIOS/UEFI settings documented after any changes
Handle add-in cards and USB adapters carefully to avoid physical damage
Keep driver installers backed up externally

description: The desired WiFi network name (SSID) does not appear in the list of available networks, even though the router is on and other devices can see it.
symptoms: Target WiFi network missing from the available networks list
Other WiFi networks nearby are visible
Other devices can see and connect to the same network
possibleCauses: Router broadcasting on a WiFi band or channel the device does not support
Network is hidden (SSID broadcast disabled)
WiFi adapter disabled or malfunctioning on the affected device
Device is out of range or blocked by interference
Router's WiFi radio has crashed or is disabled
diagnosticQuestions: Can other devices see and connect to this exact network name?
Is your device far from the router, or are there many walls/obstructions?
Do you know if the router uses 5GHz, 2.4GHz, or both, and does your device support that band?
Is the network hidden, or should it normally be visible?

commands.purpose: List all WiFi networks the adapter can currently detect
commands.expectedResult: Target network appears in the list with a signal strength value
commands.abnormalResult: Target network missing from the list even though other networks are shown, confirming a detection or compatibility issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm on another device that the network is broadcasting normally and visible
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes whether the problem is with the router or just this one device

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the router is using a WiFi band, like 5GHz, that this specific device may not support
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Older devices sometimes cannot see or connect to 5GHz-only networks

troubleshootingSteps.action: Move closer to the router and retry scanning for networks
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out range or interference as the cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Toggle WiFi off and on, or restart the WiFi adapter through Device Manager
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves a stuck or crashed WiFi radio state on the device

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check router settings to confirm SSID broadcast is enabled if the network should not be hidden
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A hidden network requires manual entry rather than appearing in the scan list

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router if its WiFi radio may have crashed while other functions still work
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A router-side radio crash will make the network invisible to all devices

possibleSolutions: Restart the WiFi adapter or toggle WiFi off and on
Move closer to the router to rule out range issues
Enable SSID broadcast on the router if unintentionally hidden
Restart the router to reset its WiFi radio
Manually add the network if it is intentionally hidden
prevention: Choose WiFi bands and channels supported by all household/office devices
Keep router firmware updated
Avoid placing the router in an isolated or obstructed location

description: The WiFi network is visible in the list, but the device fails to connect, either hanging on 'Connecting' or returning an error.
symptoms: Connection attempt hangs on 'Connecting...' indefinitely
Error message appears such as 'Can't connect to this network'
Other devices connect to the same network without issue
possibleCauses: Incorrect WiFi password entered
Router's maximum connected device limit reached
MAC address filtering blocking this specific device
Corrupted saved network profile on this device
WiFi driver issue
diagnosticQuestions: Are you certain the WiFi password being entered is correct and current?
How many devices are currently connected to this network?
Does this device connect fine to other WiFi networks?
Have you tried forgetting this network and reconnecting from scratch?

commands.command: netsh wlan show profile name="<network_name>" key=clear
commands.purpose: View the saved WiFi password Windows has stored for this network profile
commands.expectedResult: Shows the correct, current WiFi password
commands.abnormalResult: Shows an outdated or incorrect password, explaining the connection failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Double-check the WiFi password being used matches the current router password exactly, watching for case sensitivity
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect password is by far the most common cause of connection failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Forget the network on the device and reconnect from scratch, entering the password fresh
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears any corrupted or outdated saved profile causing silent failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router admin page for the number of currently connected devices versus its maximum supported limit
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some routers silently refuse new connections once a device limit is reached

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router's MAC address filtering settings, if enabled, to confirm this device is allowed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: MAC filtering can block a legitimate device that was never added to the allow list

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart both the router and the device's WiFi adapter
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears temporary state issues on both ends that can prevent a successful handshake

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the WiFi adapter driver if the device fails to connect to this network specifically but not others
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Driver bugs can cause compatibility issues with specific router models or security settings

possibleSolutions: Forget and reconnect to the network with the correct password
Check and adjust MAC address filtering on the router
Restart the router and the device's WiFi adapter
Update the WiFi driver
Reduce connected devices if the router's limit is reached
prevention: Keep WiFi passwords documented securely for authorized users
Regularly review MAC filtering lists if used
Choose router hardware rated for the expected number of connected devices

description: The device rejects the WiFi password as incorrect, even though the user believes they are entering the correct one.
symptoms: Error message specifically indicates an incorrect network security key or password
Connection fails immediately after entering the password
Other devices connect successfully with the same password
possibleCauses: Password was mistyped, including case sensitivity errors
Router's WiFi password was recently changed
Saved/cached password on the device is outdated
Confusion between similar network names, such as 2.4GHz and 5GHz versions with different passwords
diagnosticQuestions: Are you sure of the exact current WiFi password, including uppercase and lowercase letters?
Has the WiFi password been changed recently by anyone with router access?
Are there multiple networks with similar names, like 'HomeWiFi' and 'HomeWiFi_5G', that might use different passwords?
Does this device have a previously saved profile for this network that might be outdated?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Carefully re-type the WiFi password, double-checking uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Simple typos are the most frequent cause of this exact error

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router's admin page or a label on the router itself for the correct current password
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the actual current password rather than relying on memory

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm you are connecting to the correct network name if multiple similar SSIDs exist
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Prevents accidentally trying a 5GHz password on the 2.4GHz network or vice versa

troubleshootingSteps.action: Forget the saved network profile on the device and reconnect fresh with the correct password
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Removes any outdated cached password causing repeated rejection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Change the WiFi password on the router if it may have been changed unexpectedly by someone else, then reconnect all devices
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves confusion when the password was changed without the user's knowledge

possibleSolutions: Re-enter the password carefully, checking case sensitivity
Confirm the correct password from the router directly
Forget and reconnect to the network with the correct password
Change the router's WiFi password if needed and update all devices
prevention: Use a password manager to store WiFi credentials accurately
Label the router with its current WiFi credentials in a secure location
Communicate password changes to all users of the network

description: The device connects partway to the WiFi network but then shows an 'Authentication failed' or similar error, disconnecting shortly after.
symptoms: Device briefly shows connected, then disconnects with an authentication error
Repeated connection attempts fail the same way
Other devices may or may not be affected
possibleCauses: Incorrect or outdated WiFi password/security key
Mismatched security protocol between device and router, such as WPA2 vs WPA3
Router's authentication server or radio malfunctioning
Corrupted network profile on the device
MAC address filtering rejecting the device after initial handshake
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen with a fresh password entry, or does it happen even though the password is correct?
What WiFi security type does the router use, such as WPA2-Personal or WPA3?
Is this a new or recently updated device that may not support the router's security protocol?
Does restarting the router or the device change anything?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the exact WiFi password is correct by checking it directly from the router
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Even with authentication-specific errors, an incorrect password remains a common root cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check what WiFi security protocol the router is using and whether the device supports it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Older devices may not support newer protocols like WPA3, causing authentication failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: Forget the network profile on the device and reconnect from scratch
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears potentially corrupted authentication data cached from a previous connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router to reset its wireless authentication process
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves temporary glitches in the router's handling of client authentication

troubleshootingSteps.action: Temporarily switch the router's security mode to a more widely compatible setting like WPA2-Personal (AES) to test compatibility
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether a security protocol mismatch is the root cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the WiFi adapter driver on the device if the issue is isolated to one device
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Driver-level bugs can cause authentication handshakes to fail with certain routers

possibleSolutions: Forget and reconnect using the correct password
Switch router security mode to a more compatible setting if needed
Restart the router
Update the WiFi adapter driver on the affected device
prevention: Use a widely compatible security protocol like WPA2/WPA3 mixed mode if older devices are in use
Keep router firmware updated for authentication stability
Keep device WiFi drivers updated

description: The device shows as connected to WiFi with full or good signal, but there is no actual internet access.
symptoms: WiFi icon shows connected, sometimes with a warning symbol
Local network devices may be reachable, like a shared printer
Websites and online services fail to load
possibleCauses: Router has no internet from the ISP (WAN down)
DNS resolution failure
Too many devices causing the router to struggle assigning proper internet routing
Firewall or router misconfiguration blocking internet traffic
ISP outage
diagnosticQuestions: Do other devices on the same WiFi network also have no internet, or just this one?
Does the router's internet/WAN light look normal?
Can you access local network devices even though internet fails?
Have you tried connecting via Ethernet cable to see if internet works when wired?

commands.purpose: Test connectivity to the router itself over WiFi
commands.expectedResult: Replies received, confirming the local WiFi connection is healthy
commands.abnormalResult: Timeout means even the local connection to the router is failing

commands.purpose: Test connectivity beyond the router to the internet
commands.expectedResult: Replies received
commands.abnormalResult: Timeout while the gateway ping succeeds confirms the router has no internet (WAN down), not a WiFi problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if other devices on the same WiFi also lack internet
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines whether this is a router/ISP-wide issue or specific to one device

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the router's gateway IP, then ping a public IP like 8.8.8.8
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Separates a local WiFi connectivity issue from a router-to-internet (WAN) issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router's WAN/internet status light or admin page
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms if the router itself has lost its connection to the ISP

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the modem and router
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves the majority of temporary WAN or routing issues

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try connecting via Ethernet cable directly to the router to isolate whether this is WiFi-specific or a broader internet issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: If wired also fails, the problem is the router/ISP, not WiFi itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the ISP if the WAN remains down after a restart and wired connections also fail
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Indicates an outage or line issue outside local control

possibleSolutions: Restart modem and router
Change DNS settings if resolution is the issue
Test with a wired connection to isolate the WiFi from the WAN problem
Contact ISP if WAN stays down after restart
prevention: Monitor router WAN status periodically
Keep firmware updated
Avoid overloading the router with too many simultaneously active devices
keywords: wifi says connected but no internet access

description: The WiFi connection drops repeatedly throughout the day and needs to reconnect, similar to intermittent wired issues but specific to wireless.
symptoms: WiFi disconnects and reconnects on its own multiple times a day
Video calls, streaming, or downloads interrupted periodically
May affect one device or multiple devices on the same network
possibleCauses: Weak signal due to distance or obstructions
Interference from other WiFi networks or electronic devices
Router firmware bug or overheating
Power-saving settings on the device turning off the WiFi adapter periodically
Outdated WiFi driver
diagnosticQuestions: How far is the device from the router, and are there walls or floors in between?
Does this happen on multiple devices or just one?
Are there many other WiFi networks nearby that might be causing channel interference?
Does the device have WiFi power-saving mode enabled?

commands.purpose: Check current WiFi signal strength and connection details
commands.expectedResult: Good signal strength (generally above 60-70%) and a stable connection
commands.abnormalResult: Low signal strength or frequent state changes suggest a range or interference problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the WiFi signal strength using netsh wlan show interfaces or the device's WiFi settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Weak signal is one of the most common causes of frequent disconnects

troubleshootingSteps.action: Move closer to the router or reduce obstructions to test if signal improves and disconnects stop
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether distance/obstruction is the root cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Disable WiFi adapter power-saving mode in Device Manager's adapter properties
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Aggressive power saving can cause the adapter to briefly disconnect to save power

troubleshootingSteps.action: Change the router's WiFi channel to a less congested one, especially on 2.4GHz
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reduces interference from neighboring networks using the same channel

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the WiFi adapter driver and the router's firmware
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves known bugs that can cause periodic disconnections

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider a WiFi extender or mesh system if the affected area is consistently far from the router
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Physically extends good signal coverage to problem areas

possibleSolutions: Disable WiFi power-saving mode on the device
Change the router's WiFi channel
Move closer to the router or add a WiFi extender/mesh node
Update WiFi driver and router firmware
prevention: Position the router centrally and elevated for best coverage
Regularly update router firmware and device drivers
Consider mesh WiFi systems for larger homes or offices

description: The WiFi signal strength is consistently low in certain areas, resulting in slow speeds, disconnects, or an inability to connect at all in those spots.
symptoms: Signal strength indicator shows only 1-2 bars in certain rooms or areas
Connection is slow or unstable in these low-signal spots
Signal is strong closer to the router
possibleCauses: Physical distance from the router
Obstructions like thick walls, floors, metal objects, or large appliances
Interference from other electronics or neighboring WiFi networks
Router antenna orientation or placement
Older or lower-powered router hardware
diagnosticQuestions: In which specific areas is the signal weak, and how far are they from the router?
What kind of walls or materials are between the device and the router, such as concrete or brick?
Is the router placed in a central, open location or tucked away in a corner or cabinet?
How old is the router, and does it support modern WiFi standards?

commands.purpose: Check the exact signal strength percentage in the affected area
commands.expectedResult: Signal strength appropriate for reliable use, generally 60% or higher
commands.abnormalResult: Consistently low signal strength, such as under 30-40%, in the affected area confirming a coverage problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the signal strength percentage in the affected area using the device's WiFi settings or netsh wlan show interfaces
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Quantifies exactly how weak the signal really is

troubleshootingSteps.action: Relocate the router to a more central, open, and elevated location if possible
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Router placement has a major impact on overall coverage

troubleshootingSteps.action: Adjust router antenna angles if external antennas are present
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Proper antenna orientation can noticeably improve coverage in certain directions

troubleshootingSteps.action: Identify and reduce sources of interference, such as moving the router away from microwaves or cordless phone bases
troubleshootingSteps.reason: These devices can interfere with WiFi signals, especially on the 2.4GHz band

troubleshootingSteps.action: Add a WiFi extender, access point, or mesh system to cover consistently weak areas
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Physically extends reliable coverage beyond the main router's range

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider upgrading to a newer router if the current one is old and has limited range or power
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Newer hardware often has significantly better range and performance

possibleSolutions: Reposition the router to a more central and elevated location
Adjust antenna orientation
Reduce interference from nearby electronics
Add a WiFi extender, additional access point, or mesh system
Upgrade to newer router hardware if needed
prevention: Plan router placement during setup to minimize obstructions
Consider mesh systems for larger or multi-floor spaces from the start
Regularly reassess coverage as the space or furniture layout changes

description: WiFi connects normally with good signal strength, but internet and local network speeds are noticeably slower than expected.
symptoms: Speed test results on WiFi are much lower than the subscribed plan or wired speed
Streaming buffers or drops quality
File transfers over WiFi to local devices are slow
possibleCauses: Too many devices sharing the same WiFi band
Outdated WiFi standard on the router or device (e.g., WiFi 4 instead of WiFi 5/6)
Channel congestion from neighboring networks
Router placed far from the device despite decent signal bars
Background bandwidth usage from other devices or applications
diagnosticQuestions: How does WiFi speed compare to a wired Ethernet speed test on the same network?
How many devices are actively connected and using bandwidth right now?
What WiFi standard does the router support, and what does the device support (2.4GHz vs 5GHz, WiFi 5, WiFi 6)?
Have you tried switching to the 5GHz band if available?

commands.purpose: Check the current negotiated WiFi connection speed (PHY rate) versus signal strength
commands.expectedResult: A connection speed appropriate for the router and device's supported standard
commands.abnormalResult: A surprisingly low negotiated speed despite good signal strength suggests a band, channel, or compatibility issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run a speed test over WiFi, then repeat over a wired connection on the same network for comparison
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines whether the slowness is specific to WiFi or affects the whole connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check whether the device is connected to the 2.4GHz or 5GHz band and switch to 5GHz if available and within range
troubleshootingSteps.reason: 5GHz typically offers significantly faster speeds at closer range compared to 2.4GHz

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for channel congestion using a WiFi analyzer app and change the router's channel if heavily congested
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reduces interference from neighboring networks competing for the same channel

troubleshootingSteps.action: Reduce the number of actively connected and bandwidth-heavy devices during testing
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether shared bandwidth usage is contributing to the slowness

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update router firmware and the device's WiFi driver
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Performance improvements and bug fixes are often included in updates

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider upgrading router hardware if it uses an older WiFi standard that limits maximum possible speed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Older WiFi 4 routers cannot deliver speeds that newer WiFi 5/6 hardware can achieve

possibleSolutions: Switch to the 5GHz band if available
Change the router's WiFi channel to reduce congestion
Limit simultaneous heavy bandwidth usage during important tasks
Update router firmware and device WiFi drivers
Upgrade to a newer WiFi standard router if needed
prevention: Choose router hardware matching current WiFi standards
Regularly review and adjust WiFi channel selection
Position router to minimize obstructions for best speed, not just signal bars

description: The user needs to connect to a WiFi network that has its name (SSID) intentionally hidden and does not appear in the normal network list.
symptoms: Network does not appear in the available WiFi list
Connecting requires manually entering the network name
Router administrator has confirmed SSID broadcast is disabled
possibleCauses: This is intentional router configuration for privacy/security, not a fault
User does not know the exact SSID or security settings needed to connect manually
Case sensitivity or typo in the manually entered network name
diagnosticQuestions: Do you know the exact SSID (network name), including correct capitalization?
Do you know the security type used, such as WPA2-Personal, and the password?
Is SSID hiding intentional, done by an administrator for security reasons?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Obtain the exact SSID name, security type, and password from the network administrator or router settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A hidden network cannot be discovered automatically and requires exact manual entry

troubleshootingSteps.action: On the device, choose the option to manually add a network rather than selecting from the visible list
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the correct method for connecting to networks that do not broadcast their name

troubleshootingSteps.action: Enter the SSID exactly as configured, matching uppercase and lowercase letters precisely
troubleshootingSteps.reason: SSIDs are case-sensitive, and even small typos will prevent a successful connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Select the correct security type and enter the password
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect security type selection will cause the connection to fail even with the right password

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm successful connection and consider whether hiding the SSID provides meaningful benefit, since it is a weak security measure on its own
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Hidden SSIDs offer minimal real security while adding inconvenience, which is worth discussing with the administrator

possibleSolutions: Manually add the network using the exact SSID, security type, and password
Confirm exact capitalization and spelling of the hidden SSID
Ask the administrator to temporarily unhide the SSID to simplify onboarding, if appropriate
prevention: Document hidden SSID names and passwords securely for authorized users
Consider that SSID hiding provides minimal actual security benefit compared to strong WPA2/WPA3 passwords
Use a consistent process for onboarding new devices to hidden networks

description: The device connects to the WiFi network (correct password accepted) but then fails to receive a valid IP address, resulting in no network access.
symptoms: Status shows 'Connecting...' then 'Cannot obtain IP address' or similar error
WiFi password is accepted, but connection stalls after that point
May show an APIPA (169.254.x.x) address instead of a proper one
possibleCauses: Router's DHCP service is full, disabled, or malfunctioning
IP address conflict on the network
Device's network adapter or driver issue preventing proper DHCP negotiation
Too many devices connected, exceeding the DHCP pool size
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen on this one device only, or on any new device trying to join the network?
How many devices are currently connected to this WiFi network?
Have you tried restarting the router?
Does ipconfig show an APIPA address (169.254.x.x)?

commands.purpose: Check what IP address, if any, was assigned to the WiFi adapter
commands.expectedResult: A valid private IP address matching the router's network range
commands.abnormalResult: An APIPA address (169.254.x.x) or no address at all confirms the DHCP request failed

commands.purpose: Manually release and request a new IP address from the router
commands.expectedResult: A new, valid IP address is successfully assigned
commands.abnormalResult: The renewal fails or still returns an APIPA address, pointing to a router-side DHCP problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run ipconfig /all to confirm whether an APIPA address was assigned
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the device failed to receive a proper address from the router's DHCP service

troubleshootingSteps.action: Release and renew the IP address manually
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Forces a fresh DHCP request that may succeed if the first attempt simply failed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router's admin page for the number of connected devices versus the DHCP pool size
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A full DHCP pool will refuse to assign new addresses to additional devices

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router to reset its DHCP service
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves a stuck or crashed DHCP service on the router

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the affected device and try reconnecting fresh
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears any stuck network stack state on the device itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: Increase the router's DHCP pool size in its settings if it is being exhausted regularly by many devices
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Prevents future devices from being unable to obtain an address

possibleSolutions: Release and renew the IP address
Restart the router to reset DHCP
Increase the DHCP pool size if it is full
Restart the affected device's network adapter
prevention: Monitor the number of connected devices relative to the DHCP pool size
Keep router firmware updated for DHCP stability
Consider a larger DHCP range for busy networks

description: The WiFi adapter has been disabled, either through a physical switch, a function key, or in Windows settings, so no wireless networks can be found or used.
symptoms: No WiFi networks are listed at all, as if no adapter exists
WiFi toggle in settings is off, or the adapter shows disabled in Device Manager
A physical WiFi switch or indicator light on a laptop may be off
possibleCauses: Physical WiFi switch or airplane mode turned on
WiFi disabled through a function key (Fn+F-key) combination
Adapter disabled in Windows Network Connections or Device Manager
Power management or Group Policy disabling the adapter
diagnosticQuestions: Does the laptop have a physical WiFi switch or indicator light, and what state is it in?
Is Airplane Mode turned on in Windows settings?
Have you checked Device Manager to see if the WiFi adapter is disabled?
Was WiFi working before, and did anything change recently, like a key press or software install?

commands.purpose: Check the current status of the WiFi adapter
commands.expectedResult: Adapter status shows 'Up' or at least present, not 'Disabled'
commands.abnormalResult: Status shows 'Disabled', confirming the adapter itself has been turned off

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if Airplane Mode is turned on in Windows quick settings and turn it off if so
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Airplane Mode disables all wireless radios, including WiFi, with one simple toggle

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for a physical WiFi switch on the laptop, often on the side or front edge, and ensure it is in the 'on' position
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many laptops have a hardware switch that overrides all software settings

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try the WiFi function key combination, usually Fn plus a key showing a wireless icon
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Accidental key presses are a common and simple cause of WiFi being toggled off

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Device Manager and Network Connections to confirm the WiFi adapter is enabled
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms and fixes the issue if it was disabled at the software/driver level

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Group Policy settings if this is a managed work or school computer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Administrators sometimes intentionally disable WiFi on managed devices for security reasons

possibleSolutions: Turn off Airplane Mode
Check and enable the physical WiFi switch if present
Use the WiFi function key to re-enable wireless
Enable the adapter in Device Manager or Network Connections
Check with IT if Group Policy is disabling WiFi on a managed device
prevention: Be mindful of function key combinations that toggle WiFi
Avoid disabling network adapters unless necessary for troubleshooting
Document Group Policy restrictions on managed devices for user reference
keywords: no wifi networks found at all

description: The network adapter shows no IP address at all, whether wired or wireless, preventing any network communication.
symptoms: ipconfig shows no IPv4 address for the adapter, or shows 'Media disconnected'
No local network or internet access
Network icon typically shows a warning or disconnected state
possibleCauses: No physical or wireless connection established
DHCP server (router) not responding
Adapter driver issue preventing address negotiation
Static IP was removed or misconfigured without a valid replacement
diagnosticQuestions: Is this a wired or wireless connection?
Is the physical link (cable connected, or WiFi connected) actually established before checking for an IP?
Have you tried releasing and renewing the IP address?
Is this affecting just this device or the whole network?

commands.purpose: Check the current IP configuration status for all adapters
commands.expectedResult: A valid IPv4 address listed for the active adapter
commands.abnormalResult: No IPv4 address at all, or 'Media disconnected', confirming no address was received

commands.purpose: Release any current IP address configuration
commands.expectedResult: Releases without error
commands.abnormalResult: Error releasing may indicate an adapter or driver problem

commands.purpose: Request a new IP address from the DHCP server
commands.expectedResult: A valid new IP address is assigned
commands.abnormalResult: Renewal fails entirely or returns no address, pointing to a DHCP/router issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the physical connection (cable plugged in or WiFi connected) is actually established first
troubleshootingSteps.reason: No IP address is expected and normal if there is no underlying connection at all

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run ipconfig /release followed by ipconfig /renew
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Forces a fresh request for a valid IP address from the network's DHCP server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router to reset its DHCP service if renewal fails
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A stuck or crashed DHCP service on the router will not respond to any client requests

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if a static IP was previously configured and is now invalid or missing required fields
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incomplete static configuration can prevent any address from being properly applied

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update or reinstall the network adapter driver if release/renew consistently fails on this device only
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A driver-level fault can prevent the adapter from properly requesting or accepting an address

possibleSolutions: Release and renew the IP address
Restart the router to reset DHCP service
Correct or remove an invalid static IP configuration
Update or reinstall the network adapter driver
prevention: Keep DHCP services on routers/servers properly maintained
Avoid leaving incomplete static IP configurations on devices
Regularly test and monitor network adapter health on critical systems

description: The device has assigned itself an Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) address starting with 169.254, meaning it failed to get a real address from DHCP.
symptoms: ipconfig shows an IP address starting with 169.254
No internet or local network access, or only very limited local access
May show a 'Limited' network status in Windows
possibleCauses: DHCP server (router) not responding or unreachable
Physical or wireless connection unstable during the address request
Router's DHCP service disabled or its address pool exhausted
Firewall or driver issue blocking the DHCP request/response
diagnosticQuestions: Have you tried releasing and renewing the IP address?
Is the router's DHCP service enabled, and is its address pool full?
Does this happen on this device only, or on multiple devices joining the network?
Is the physical or WiFi connection to the router stable?

commands.purpose: Confirm the exact IP address currently assigned
commands.expectedResult: A valid private IP in the router's normal range, such as 192.168.x.x
commands.abnormalResult: An address starting with 169.254.x.x confirms an APIPA self-assigned address was used because DHCP failed

commands.purpose: Force the device to request a new address from the DHCP server
commands.expectedResult: A valid address in the correct range is received
commands.abnormalResult: The device falls back to another 169.254.x.x address, confirming DHCP is still not responding

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the APIPA address with ipconfig /all
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes clearly that this is a failed DHCP request rather than another type of network issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Release and renew the IP address
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Gives the device another chance to successfully reach the DHCP server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router to reset its DHCP service
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A crashed or overloaded DHCP service is a very common cause of repeated APIPA assignment

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router's DHCP pool size and current usage in its admin page
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A full address pool will cause new or renewing devices to fail and fall back to APIPA

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check cable/WiFi stability during the renewal process, since a dropped connection mid-request can cause failure
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An unstable connection at the exact moment of the DHCP request can cause it to fail

troubleshootingSteps.action: Temporarily assign a manual static IP as a workaround while investigating the DHCP issue further
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Restores network access immediately while the underlying DHCP problem is resolved

possibleSolutions: Release and renew the IP address
Restart the router to reset DHCP
Increase the DHCP pool size if exhausted
Temporarily assign a static IP as a workaround
prevention: Monitor DHCP pool utilization on busy networks
Keep router firmware updated for DHCP reliability
Use a stable, quality connection during initial network setup

description: Windows shows a warning that another device on the network is using the same IP address as this computer, causing connectivity conflicts.
symptoms: Warning message: 'Another device on the network has the same IP address'
Intermittent or complete loss of network connectivity
May affect one or both devices sharing the same address
possibleCauses: Two devices manually configured with the same static IP
A device with a static IP falls within the router's dynamic DHCP pool range, causing a clash
DHCP server assigning a duplicate address due to a lease table error
diagnosticQuestions: Is this device using a static (manually set) IP address, or automatic (DHCP)?
Do you know of any other device that might be using the same static IP?
Was a new device recently added to the network with a manually configured address?
Does restarting the router or renewing the IP resolve the conflict temporarily?

commands.purpose: Check whether this device is using a static or DHCP-assigned address
commands.expectedResult: Clarifies the current configuration type and address in use
commands.abnormalResult: A static IP that happens to fall within the router's DHCP range is a likely source of the conflict

commands.purpose: View the ARP table to see which MAC addresses are associated with which IPs on the local network
commands.expectedResult: Each IP address maps to only one MAC address
commands.abnormalResult: Inconsistent or conflicting entries can sometimes reveal duplicate address activity, though this may need to be checked from another device

troubleshootingSteps.action: Identify whether the device in question uses a static IP or receives one automatically via DHCP
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines the right fix path, since static IP conflicts are resolved differently than DHCP conflicts

troubleshootingSteps.action: If static, change the device to use an IP address outside the router's DHCP pool range, or switch it to automatic (DHCP)
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Prevents future clashes with dynamically assigned addresses

troubleshootingSteps.action: If using DHCP, release and renew the IP address to request a fresh, hopefully non-conflicting address
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Often resolves temporary DHCP lease table errors causing the duplicate assignment

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check other devices on the network for any manually configured static IPs that might conflict
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Identifies and corrects the actual source of the duplicate address

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router to clear and rebuild its DHCP lease table if conflicts persist
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves internal DHCP server errors that may be causing repeated duplicate assignments

possibleSolutions: Change conflicting static IP to one outside the DHCP range, or switch to automatic
Release and renew the IP address
Identify and correct other devices with conflicting static IPs
Restart the router to rebuild the DHCP lease table
prevention: Reserve a specific range outside the DHCP pool for static IP devices
Use DHCP reservations instead of manual static IPs where possible
Document all statically assigned IP addresses on the network

description: A device configured with a manual (static) IP address cannot connect properly due to incorrect settings in that configuration.
symptoms: Device cannot reach the local network or internet despite appearing 'connected'
ipconfig shows a static IP that does not match the network's actual range
Other devices using DHCP work fine on the same network
possibleCauses: Wrong IP address entered, not matching the network's subnet
Incorrect subnet mask
Incorrect default gateway or DNS server entered
IP address conflicts with another device or falls within the DHCP pool
diagnosticQuestions: What static IP, subnet mask, gateway, and DNS values were manually entered?
What is the correct network range used by the router, for example 192.168.1.x?
Was this configuration copied from another device or documentation that might be outdated?
Does switching this device to automatic (DHCP) restore connectivity?

commands.purpose: Review the exact static configuration currently applied
commands.expectedResult: IP address, subnet mask, gateway, and DNS all correctly matching the network
commands.abnormalResult: Any mismatched value, such as a wrong subnet or gateway on a different network segment, explains the failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Compare the manually configured IP, subnet mask, gateway, and DNS against a known-working device on the same network using DHCP
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Quickly reveals which specific value is incorrect

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct the IP address to be within the correct network range and outside the router's DHCP pool
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures the address is valid for this network and will not conflict with dynamically assigned devices

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct the subnet mask to match the rest of the network, typically 255.255.255.0 for most home/small office networks
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect subnet mask can prevent the device from communicating even within the same physical network

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct the default gateway to match the router's actual IP address
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect gateway prevents any traffic from leaving the local network

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct or update the DNS server entries, or set them to a reliable public DNS like 8.8.8.8
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures website names can be properly resolved even with the correct IP configuration otherwise

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test connectivity after each correction, or consider switching to automatic (DHCP) if manual configuration is not required
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the fix and simplifies future maintenance if static addressing is not truly needed

possibleSolutions: Correct the IP address, subnet mask, gateway, and DNS to match the actual network
Switch to automatic (DHCP) configuration if static addressing is not required
Use a DHCP reservation instead of manual static configuration for easier management
prevention: Document all static IP configurations clearly and keep them updated
Use DHCP reservations instead of manual static IPs where possible to reduce human error
Double check all four key values (IP, subnet, gateway, DNS) when configuring manually

description: The subnet mask configured on a device does not match the rest of the network, preventing proper communication even within the same physical network.
symptoms: Device cannot communicate with other devices on what should be the same local network
May show a valid-looking IP address but still fail to connect properly
Problem often appears after manual network configuration
possibleCauses: Subnet mask manually entered incorrectly
Subnet mask copied from a different network with a different addressing scheme
Confusion between common subnet mask values, such as 255.255.255.0 versus 255.255.0.0
diagnosticQuestions: What subnet mask is currently configured on this device?
What subnet mask do other working devices on the same network use?
Was this configuration entered manually, and if so, where did the values come from?

commands.purpose: Check the currently configured subnet mask
commands.expectedResult: Subnet mask matches what is used by other devices on the same network
commands.abnormalResult: A different or unusual subnet mask value indicates a misconfiguration

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the subnet mask on a known-working device on the same network for comparison
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides the correct reference value to fix the misconfigured device

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct the subnet mask on the affected device to match the rest of the network exactly
troubleshootingSteps.reason: All devices on the same logical network segment must use the same subnet mask to communicate properly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the network adapter or the device after making the change
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures the corrected setting is fully applied

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test connectivity to another local device and to the internet after the correction
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the subnet mask was indeed the cause and the fix worked

possibleSolutions: Correct the subnet mask to match the rest of the network
Switch to automatic (DHCP) configuration if manual entry is error-prone
Restart the adapter after making changes
prevention: Use DHCP where possible to avoid manual subnet mask errors
Document the correct subnet mask for the network for reference
Double-check subnet values when setting up any static configuration

description: The default gateway configured on a device is wrong or missing, so the device can communicate on the local network but cannot reach the internet or other networks.
symptoms: Local devices are reachable, but internet and other network segments are not
ipconfig shows an incorrect, missing, or unreachable gateway address
Ping to the configured gateway fails
possibleCauses: Gateway IP manually entered incorrectly
Gateway address does not match the router's actual IP
Router's IP address changed but the device's static configuration was not updated
DHCP misconfiguration providing a wrong gateway value
diagnosticQuestions: What gateway address is currently configured on the affected device?
What is the router's actual current IP address?
Is this device using a static IP with a manually entered gateway, or DHCP?
Can you ping the configured gateway address successfully?

commands.purpose: Check the currently configured default gateway
commands.expectedResult: Gateway address matches the router's actual IP, for example 192.168.1.1
commands.abnormalResult: Gateway is missing, blank, or does not match the router's real address

commands.purpose: Test if the configured gateway address is actually reachable
commands.expectedResult: Replies received
commands.abnormalResult: Timeout confirms the configured gateway address is wrong or unreachable

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the router's actual current IP address, usually printed on the router or found in its admin interface
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides the correct value the device's gateway setting should match

troubleshootingSteps.action: Compare this to the gateway currently configured on the affected device using ipconfig /all
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether there is a mismatch

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct the static gateway setting to match the router's actual IP address, or switch the device to automatic (DHCP)
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Restores the device's ability to route traffic beyond the local network

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the corrected gateway address to confirm it now responds
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Verifies the fix resolved the connectivity issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: If using DHCP and the gateway is still wrong, check the router's DHCP configuration for an incorrect gateway value being handed out
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Points to a router-side misconfiguration rather than a device-side one

possibleSolutions: Correct the static gateway to match the router's actual IP address
Switch the device to automatic (DHCP) configuration
Fix an incorrect gateway value in the router's DHCP settings if applicable
prevention: Keep static IP documentation updated whenever the router's address changes
Use DHCP where possible to avoid manual gateway errors
Regularly verify network configuration after any router changes

description: Two or more devices on the network are attempting to use the same IP address at the same time, causing connectivity problems for one or both devices.
symptoms: Windows warning: 'There is an IP address conflict with another system on the network'
Intermittent connectivity, or one device losing connection when the other is active
Problem may resolve temporarily on its own then return
possibleCauses: Duplicate static IP configuration on two devices
A device with a static IP within the router's DHCP pool clashing with a dynamically assigned device
DHCP server assigning the same address twice due to a lease table issue
diagnosticQuestions: Are any devices on the network manually configured with static IP addresses?
Does the conflict warning mention a specific IP address, and do you recognize which devices might be using it?
Did this start after adding a new device to the network?
Does releasing and renewing the IP, or restarting the router, temporarily resolve it?

commands.purpose: Identify the exact IP address in conflict on this device
commands.expectedResult: Shows the current IP address involved in the conflict warning
commands.abnormalResult: N/A - this simply identifies the address to investigate further

commands.purpose: View which MAC addresses are associated with IP addresses on the local network, to help identify the conflicting device
commands.expectedResult: Each IP maps to a single consistent MAC address
commands.abnormalResult: Unexpected or unfamiliar MAC address entries can help identify an unknown or conflicting device

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact IP address mentioned in the conflict warning
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides the specific address to investigate rather than searching broadly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check all devices on the network for a static IP configuration matching that address
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Duplicate static configuration is the most direct and common cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Change one of the conflicting devices to a different static IP outside the DHCP pool, or switch it to automatic (DHCP)
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolves the conflict by ensuring only one device uses that specific address

troubleshootingSteps.action: Release and renew the IP address on the affected DHCP-based device if no static conflict is found
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Requests a fresh address from the router, which can resolve a stale DHCP lease table entry

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router to rebuild its DHCP lease table if conflicts continue to recur without a clear static IP cause
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears any internal inconsistency in how the router is tracking assigned addresses

possibleSolutions: Change a conflicting static IP to a unique address outside the DHCP range
Switch a statically configured device to automatic (DHCP)
Release and renew the IP address
Restart the router to rebuild the DHCP lease table
prevention: Reserve a specific address range for static IP devices, separate from the DHCP pool
Use DHCP reservations for devices needing a consistent address
Document all static IP assignments across the network

description: Attempting to renew the IP address using ipconfig /renew fails with an error, and the device cannot obtain a valid address.
symptoms: ipconfig /renew returns an error such as 'The RPC server is unavailable' or 'An error occurred while renewing interface'
Device remains without a valid IP address or keeps an APIPA address
No network connectivity as a result
possibleCauses: DHCP Client service not running on the computer
Router's DHCP server not responding at all
Physical or wireless connection unstable during the renewal attempt
Network adapter driver issue preventing proper DHCP communication
diagnosticQuestions: What exact error message appears when running ipconfig /renew?
Is the DHCP Client service running in Windows Services?
Is the physical or WiFi connection to the router stable during this attempt?
Does restarting the computer or router change the result?

commands.purpose: Attempt to obtain a new IP address and observe the specific error, if any
commands.expectedResult: A new valid IP address is successfully assigned
commands.abnormalResult: A specific error message appears, which helps identify whether the problem is the DHCP Client service, the adapter, or the router

commands.purpose: Check whether the DHCP Client service is running in Windows
commands.expectedResult: DHCP Client service status is 'Running'
commands.abnormalResult: Service is stopped or disabled, which will directly prevent successful IP renewal

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the exact error message returned by ipconfig /renew
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Different errors point to different root causes, such as a service issue versus no router response

troubleshootingSteps.action: Open Services (services.msc) and confirm the DHCP Client service is running and set to automatic
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This Windows service is required for the renewal process to function at all

troubleshootingSteps.action: Start the DHCP Client service if it is stopped, then retry ipconfig /renew
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly resolves the issue if this specific service was the cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router to reset its own DHCP server if the client-side service is running normally but renewal still fails
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms and resolves a router-side DHCP service problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update or reinstall the network adapter driver if the problem persists on this device only
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A driver-level fault can prevent the renewal request from being sent or received correctly

possibleSolutions: Start the DHCP Client service if stopped
Restart the router to reset its DHCP server
Update or reinstall the network adapter driver
Restart the computer to reset the network stack fully
prevention: Keep the DHCP Client service set to automatic startup
Keep network drivers updated
Keep router firmware updated for DHCP reliability
keywords: unable to renew ip address error

description: The device's DHCP-assigned IP address lease has expired and could not be renewed, resulting in a loss of network connectivity.
symptoms: Device loses network connectivity after previously working fine
ipconfig shows an expired or invalid lease, or an APIPA address
Reconnecting or restarting sometimes temporarily restores access
possibleCauses: Router unreachable at the exact time of lease renewal
Device was offline (asleep, powered off) during the scheduled renewal window
Router's DHCP service issue preventing lease renewal
Very short DHCP lease time configured on the router causing frequent renewal attempts
diagnosticQuestions: Did this happen after the device was asleep, in standby, or away from the network for a period of time?
What is the DHCP lease time configured on the router, if known?
Does manually renewing the IP address resolve it?
Does this happen to this device only, or to multiple devices?

commands.purpose: Check the current lease status and details for the adapter
commands.expectedResult: Shows a valid, current lease with 'Lease Obtained' and 'Lease Expires' dates in the future
commands.abnormalResult: Lease already expired, or an APIPA address present, confirming the renewal failed

commands.purpose: Manually attempt to renew the expired lease
commands.expectedResult: A new valid lease and IP address obtained
commands.abnormalResult: Renewal fails again, indicating a persistent DHCP server issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the current lease details with ipconfig /all to confirm expiration
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms this is specifically a lease expiration issue rather than another type of DHCP failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Manually renew the IP address using ipconfig /renew
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Often immediately resolves the issue by obtaining a fresh, valid lease

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the router if manual renewal fails, to reset its DHCP service
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Addresses a router-side problem preventing successful lease renewals

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check and consider increasing the DHCP lease time in the router settings if this happens frequently
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A longer lease time reduces how often devices need to successfully renew, lowering the chance of failure during a renewal attempt

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ensure the device stays connected to the network consistently, especially avoiding long sleep/standby periods away from the router if this is a recurring issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Devices offline during their renewal window are more likely to experience this problem

possibleSolutions: Manually renew the IP address
Restart the router to reset the DHCP service
Increase the DHCP lease time in router settings
Keep the device connected to avoid missing renewal windows
prevention: Configure a reasonable DHCP lease time for the environment, balancing renewal frequency and address availability
Keep router firmware updated for DHCP reliability
Monitor for devices with frequent lease expiration issues as a sign of a larger network problem

description: The device's overall network configuration is invalid or inconsistent, combining multiple incorrect values that together prevent normal network use.
symptoms: Device cannot reliably connect to the network or internet
ipconfig shows a combination of unusual or mismatched values across IP, subnet, gateway, and DNS
Problem may have appeared after manual changes or software that modifies network settings
possibleCauses: Multiple manually entered settings are individually or collectively incorrect
Conflicting network profiles or leftover settings from VPN or virtualization software
Corrupted network stack requiring a full reset
Static configuration left over after switching from static to DHCP incompletely
diagnosticQuestions: Have any manual network changes been made recently, including VPN or virtual machine software installations?
Does resetting the adapter to automatic (DHCP) resolve the issue?
Is this affecting one adapter only, or all network adapters on the device?
Would a full network reset be acceptable to attempt as a troubleshooting step?

commands.purpose: Review the complete current network configuration for inconsistencies
commands.expectedResult: All values (IP, subnet, gateway, DNS) are valid and consistent with the network
commands.abnormalResult: Multiple mismatched, missing, or clearly invalid values across the configuration

commands.purpose: Reset the entire TCP/IP stack to default settings
commands.expectedResult: Command completes and prompts for a restart, after which networking behaves normally
commands.abnormalResult: Networking issues persist even after the reset and restart, suggesting a deeper hardware or driver problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the full output of ipconfig /all for any values that look incorrect or inconsistent
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides a complete picture of what specifically is misconfigured

troubleshootingSteps.action: Reset the network adapter to automatic (DHCP) configuration for both IP and DNS settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Removes any incorrect manual settings and lets the router provide a fresh, correct configuration

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for and uninstall any recently added VPN or virtualization software that may have altered network settings, if suspected
