troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps narrow down whether the problem is specifically with the routing configuration or a different part of the network path

possibleSolutions: Correct VLAN assignment if devices are not actually on the same VLAN as assumed
Configure or correct inter-VLAN routing on the router/Layer 3 switch
Bring up or correct the VLAN interface (SVI) configuration
Adjust access control lists or firewall rules blocking intended traffic
prevention: Document intended inter-VLAN communication requirements and routing configuration
Regularly verify VLAN interface status on routing devices
Review ACL and firewall rules periodically for unintended blocks
keywords: devices same vlan cant reach each other

description: The native VLAN configured on a trunk link does not match on both ends, causing subtle connectivity issues and potential security concerns for untagged traffic.
symptoms: Switch logs may show native VLAN mismatch warnings on a trunk link
Untagged traffic behaves unexpectedly or fails to reach its intended destination across the trunk
Some VLANs work fine over the trunk while the native VLAN's traffic specifically has issues
possibleCauses: Native VLAN configured differently on each end of a trunk link, such as VLAN 1 on one switch and VLAN 99 on the other
Default native VLAN left unchanged on one switch while intentionally changed on the other for security reasons
Configuration oversight during trunk setup between two switches
diagnosticQuestions: What native VLAN is configured on each end of this specific trunk link?
Does the switch report any native VLAN mismatch warnings in its logs?
Was this trunk recently configured or modified on one or both ends?
Is there an intentional security practice of changing the native VLAN away from the default that might not have been applied consistently?

commands.command: show interface trunk (on a managed switch CLI)
commands.purpose: View the native VLAN configuration for the trunk port on both connected switches
commands.expectedResult: Native VLAN matches exactly on both ends of the trunk link
commands.abnormalResult: Different native VLAN values configured on each end, confirming the mismatch

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the native VLAN configuration on both ends of the specific trunk link in question
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly identifies whether a mismatch exists and what the two conflicting values are

troubleshootingSteps.action: Determine which native VLAN value should be the correct, standardized one for this network
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes the target configuration before correcting either side

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the native VLAN setting on the incorrectly configured end of the trunk to match the correct, standardized value
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly resolves the mismatch causing the untagged traffic issues

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify the switch no longer reports native VLAN mismatch warnings after the correction
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the configuration change was successful and the mismatch is resolved

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review other trunk links in the network for the same native VLAN consistently, preventing similar issues elsewhere
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A native VLAN mismatch on one link often indicates the same inconsistency may exist on other trunk connections in the network

possibleSolutions: Correct the native VLAN on the mismatched end of the trunk to match the other end
Standardize on a single native VLAN value across the entire network
Verify no mismatch warnings remain after the correction
prevention: Use a consistent native VLAN value across all trunk links network-wide
Document the standardized native VLAN choice clearly for all administrators
Verify native VLAN configuration whenever setting up a new trunk link

description: A trunk link between two switches has a general configuration error beyond just native VLAN or allowed VLANs, preventing it from properly carrying multi-VLAN traffic.
symptoms: Trunk link fails to pass traffic for any or most VLANs
Switches may not even establish a proper trunk negotiation between them
Port may fall back to acting as a regular access port instead of a trunk
possibleCauses: Trunk encapsulation type mismatch between switch platforms that support multiple types
One end configured as 'access' mode while the other is configured as 'trunk' mode
Trunking protocol negotiation (such as DTP) failure or misconfiguration
Physical layer issue on the trunk link masking as a configuration problem
diagnosticQuestions: Are both ends of this link explicitly and correctly configured as trunk ports?
If applicable to this switch platform, does the encapsulation type match on both ends?
Is there any automatic trunk negotiation protocol involved, and could it be failing?
Has basic physical connectivity (cable, link light) been confirmed on this specific link?

commands.command: show interface <port> switchport (on a managed switch CLI)
commands.purpose: Check the administrative and operational trunk mode for the port
commands.expectedResult: Both administrative and operational mode show as trunk with matching encapsulation
commands.abnormalResult: Mismatch between administrative and operational mode, or a mode showing as access instead of trunk, revealing the specific configuration problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm basic physical connectivity on the link first, including cable integrity and link lights
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out a physical layer problem before investigating deeper configuration issues

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check both the administrative and operational trunk mode on both ends of the link
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reveals whether the configuration intent (administrative) matches what is actually happening (operational), which can differ due to negotiation failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ensure both ends are explicitly configured as trunk ports rather than relying on automatic negotiation, if the platform allows this
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Explicit configuration is generally more reliable and easier to troubleshoot than automatic trunk negotiation protocols

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify encapsulation type compatibility if the switch platform supports multiple trunking encapsulation methods
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A mismatch here will prevent the trunk from forming correctly even with otherwise correct configuration

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct any identified configuration mismatches and verify the trunk comes up correctly, carrying traffic for all intended VLANs
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the specific fix fully resolved the trunk formation and traffic-carrying issue

possibleSolutions: Explicitly configure both ends of the link as trunk ports
Correct encapsulation type mismatches if applicable
Verify and correct any trunk negotiation protocol issues
Confirm physical link integrity
prevention: Use explicit trunk configuration rather than relying solely on automatic negotiation
Document trunk configuration standards for the network
Test new trunk links thoroughly before relying on them for production traffic

description: A switch port intended to be a simple access port for a single end device, such as a computer or printer, has an incorrect configuration causing connectivity issues.
symptoms: Device connected to this port has no connectivity or unexpected VLAN behavior
Port may be incorrectly configured as a trunk instead of access mode
Port may be assigned to the wrong single VLAN for an access port
possibleCauses: Port configured as trunk mode instead of the intended simple access mode
Port assigned to an incorrect VLAN for the connected device's needs
Port configuration copied from a different port type during setup without adjustment
Voice VLAN misconfiguration if this port is meant to support both a computer and a VoIP phone
diagnosticQuestions: Is this port intended to be a simple single-device access port, or does it need special configuration like a voice VLAN for an IP phone?
What VLAN should this access port be assigned to?
Is the port currently configured as 'access' mode or 'trunk' mode?
If a voice VLAN is involved, is it configured correctly alongside the data VLAN?

commands.command: show interface <port> switchport (on a managed switch CLI)
commands.purpose: Check the current mode (access vs trunk) and VLAN assignment for the port
commands.expectedResult: Port mode shows as 'access' with the correct single VLAN assigned
commands.abnormalResult: Port mode shows as 'trunk' when access was intended, or the VLAN assignment is incorrect

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the port's intended purpose, specifically whether it should be a simple access port for one device
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Establishes the correct target configuration, distinguishing from trunk ports meant for switch-to-switch links

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the port's current mode and VLAN assignment through the switch's management interface
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reveals whether the port is incorrectly set to trunk mode or has the wrong VLAN assigned

troubleshootingSteps.action: Change the port mode to 'access' if it was incorrectly configured as a trunk
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures the port behaves as intended for a simple single-device connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct the VLAN assignment to the proper single VLAN for this access port
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly resolves connectivity issues stemming from an incorrect VLAN assignment

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a voice VLAN is needed for an attached IP phone, configure it correctly alongside the data VLAN according to the phone manufacturer's and switch's requirements
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Voice VLANs have specific configuration requirements distinct from standard data-only access ports

possibleSolutions: Change the port mode to access if incorrectly set to trunk
Correct the VLAN assignment for the access port
Configure voice VLAN correctly if applicable for an attached IP phone
prevention: Use a standard, documented configuration template for access ports
Clearly distinguish access port configuration from trunk port configuration in documentation
Verify voice VLAN configuration when deploying IP phones
keywords: port should be access not trunk

description: An attempt to assign a port or device to a specific VLAN fails, or traffic for that VLAN does not work, because the VLAN itself was never actually created on the switch.
symptoms: Error when attempting to assign a port to a VLAN number that does not exist
Traffic for the intended VLAN does not work anywhere on the switch
VLAN is missing entirely from the switch's VLAN database when checked
possibleCauses: VLAN was planned and referenced in documentation or configuration but never actually created on this specific switch
VLAN was created on some switches in the network but not consistently on all of them
VLAN was accidentally deleted during a cleanup or configuration change
diagnosticQuestions: What VLAN number or name is expected to exist but appears to be missing?
Was this VLAN successfully created on other switches in the network, just not this particular one?
Is there any chance this VLAN was recently and accidentally deleted during other configuration work?
Do you have documentation specifying which VLANs should exist on which switches?

commands.command: show vlan brief (on a managed switch CLI)
commands.purpose: List all VLANs currently defined in the switch's VLAN database
commands.expectedResult: The expected VLAN appears in the list with its correct ID and name
commands.abnormalResult: The expected VLAN is missing entirely from the list, confirming it was never created or was deleted

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the switch's VLAN database to confirm the specific VLAN is indeed missing
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly confirms the root cause before taking any corrective action

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check other switches in the network to see if the VLAN exists there, helping determine if this is an isolated gap or a broader inconsistency
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps understand the scope of the issue and whether other switches need the same fix

troubleshootingSteps.action: Create the missing VLAN on this switch with the correct VLAN ID and name, matching what is used elsewhere in the network
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly resolves the root cause by making the VLAN available for port assignment and traffic

troubleshootingSteps.action: Assign the intended ports to this newly created VLAN as originally planned
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Completes the configuration now that the underlying VLAN exists

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify traffic for this VLAN now works correctly, including across any trunk links to other switches
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the VLAN is not only created but properly functioning end-to-end

possibleSolutions: Create the missing VLAN with the correct ID and name
Ensure the VLAN is consistently created across all relevant switches in the network
Assign intended ports to the newly created VLAN
prevention: Maintain a master VLAN documentation list covering all switches where each VLAN should exist
Use a checklist when deploying new VLANs to ensure consistency across all switches
Be cautious when performing VLAN cleanup to avoid accidental deletions

description: A firewall, either on the local computer or on a network device, is blocking internet access entirely, even though the underlying network connection is otherwise working.
symptoms: No internet access despite a valid IP address, gateway, and DNS configuration
Local network access may still work fine, isolating the problem to outbound/internet traffic
Disabling the firewall temporarily restores internet access
possibleCauses: Overly restrictive firewall rule blocking all or most outbound traffic
Firewall software recently installed or updated with default overly strict settings
Firewall rule accidentally created or modified, blocking legitimate traffic
Corrupted firewall configuration causing unintended blocking behavior
diagnosticQuestions: Does disabling the firewall temporarily restore internet access, confirming it as the cause?
Is this the Windows built-in firewall, or third-party security software?
Was any firewall software recently installed, updated, or reconfigured?
Does this affect all internet traffic, or just specific applications or ports?

commands.purpose: Check the current status of the Windows Firewall across all profiles
commands.expectedResult: Shows current firewall state and can help identify if it is unexpectedly blocking traffic
commands.abnormalResult: Firewall in an unexpected state or with overly restrictive default rules blocking normal outbound traffic

troubleshootingSteps.action: Temporarily disable the firewall to confirm it is indeed the cause of the internet access problem
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly verifies the firewall as the culprit before spending time on detailed rule investigation

troubleshootingSteps.action: If confirmed, review the firewall's outbound rules for anything overly restrictive or recently changed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Identifies the specific rule or setting causing the block

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for recently installed or updated security software that may have introduced new default restrictive rules
troubleshootingSteps.reason: New security software installations are a common trigger for unexpected internet blocking

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct or remove the specific rule causing the block, or reset the firewall to a known-good default configuration if the exact rule cannot be identified
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly resolves the blocking issue while preserving as much of the intended security posture as possible

troubleshootingSteps.action: Re-enable the firewall with the corrected configuration and verify internet access is restored
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the fix while ensuring the device remains protected by an active, properly configured firewall

possibleSolutions: Adjust or remove the overly restrictive firewall rule
Reset firewall settings to default if the cause cannot be isolated
Update firewall/security software to the latest version
Re-enable the firewall promptly after testing, replacing it with a proper corrected configuration
prevention: Test firewall rule changes carefully before wide deployment
Keep firewall software updated
Document intentional firewall rules and their purposes

description: A firewall on the computer or network is blocking communication with a printer, preventing print jobs, scanning, or the printer from even being discovered on the network.
symptoms: Printer cannot be found during network setup, or existing print jobs fail to reach the printer
Printing works fine when the firewall is temporarily disabled
Scan-related network features may also be affected if applicable
possibleCauses: Firewall blocking the specific ports or protocols used for printer discovery and communication
Printer's network discovery traffic blocked by network profile settings, such as the network being marked as 'Public' instead of 'Private'
Third-party security software with more restrictive default printer/network rules than the built-in firewall
Recently updated firewall or security software resetting previously allowed printer rules
diagnosticQuestions: Does disabling the firewall temporarily allow the printer to be found or used, confirming the firewall as the cause?
Is the network connection currently set as 'Public' or 'Private' in Windows network settings?
Was any firewall or security software recently installed or updated?
Did printing work before, and if so, what changed around the time it stopped?

commands.command: netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name=all | findstr /i print
commands.purpose: Search for existing firewall rules related to printing to see their current status
commands.expectedResult: Relevant printing rules exist and are enabled
commands.abnormalResult: Printing-related rules are missing, disabled, or overly restrictive

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check whether the network connection is set to 'Private' rather than 'Public' in Windows network settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Windows Firewall applies significantly more restrictive rules, including blocking printer discovery, on networks marked as Public

troubleshootingSteps.action: Change the network profile to 'Private' if this is a trusted home or office network
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Allows the appropriate, less restrictive firewall rules for local device discovery and communication to apply

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Windows Firewall's allowed apps list to confirm printing and network discovery related rules are enabled
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Specific built-in rules govern printer discovery and communication, and these can become disabled unintentionally

troubleshootingSteps.action: If using third-party security software, check its specific settings for network/printer related blocking rules
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Third-party firewalls often have their own separate rule sets that can be more restrictive than the built-in Windows Firewall

troubleshootingSteps.action: Add a specific allow rule for the printer's IP address or the relevant printing ports if the general settings above do not resolve the issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides a targeted fix when broader profile and default rule adjustments are not sufficient

possibleSolutions: Set the network profile to Private for trusted networks
Enable printing and network discovery rules in Windows Firewall
Adjust third-party security software's printer/network blocking settings
Add a specific firewall allow rule for the printer if needed
prevention: Set network profiles correctly when first connecting to a new network
Review firewall/security software settings after installation or major updates
Document specific firewall rules needed for critical network printers

description: A specific application cannot connect to the internet or a network resource because a firewall is blocking its network traffic, while other applications work normally.
symptoms: The specific application shows a connection error, timeout, or cannot reach its servers
Other applications and general internet browsing work fine
Disabling the firewall allows the specific application to work normally
possibleCauses: Firewall rule specifically blocking this application's executable or the ports it uses
Application not yet granted permission in the firewall's allowed apps list
New version of the application requires different or additional firewall permissions than before
Firewall profile settings blocking the application on the current network type
diagnosticQuestions: Does this specific application fail while others work fine, confirming it is application-specific?
Does disabling the firewall temporarily resolve the issue for this application?
Is the application listed in the firewall's allowed apps/programs list, and if so, is it enabled for the correct network profile?
Was the application recently updated, which might explain a sudden change in its firewall requirements?

commands.command: netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name=all | findstr /i "<application_name>"
commands.purpose: Search for existing firewall rules specifically related to this application
commands.expectedResult: A rule exists allowing the application's necessary traffic
commands.abnormalResult: No rule exists for the application, or an existing rule is set to block rather than allow its traffic

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the problem is specific to this one application by testing other applications and general internet access
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Verifies this is an application-specific firewall issue rather than a broader connectivity problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the firewall's allowed apps list for an entry for this specific application
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines whether the application has ever been granted the necessary firewall permission

troubleshootingSteps.action: Add or enable the application in the firewall's allowed list for the appropriate network profile (Private/Public)
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly grants the necessary permission for the application to communicate through the firewall

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the application requires specific ports rather than a simple program-based rule, create a specific inbound/outbound port rule as needed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some applications require explicit port-based rules rather than relying on a simple program-based allow entry

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the application after making firewall changes to ensure it properly establishes its network connections
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some applications cache connection failures and need a restart to retry successfully after a firewall change

possibleSolutions: Add or enable the application in the firewall's allowed apps list
Create specific port rules if required by the application
Restart the application after firewall changes
Reinstall the application if its firewall rule entry appears corrupted
prevention: Review and update firewall permissions after major application updates
Document required firewall rules for critical business applications
Test application connectivity after any firewall software changes

description: A firewall is configured to block ICMP echo requests (ping), causing ping tests to fail even though the actual network connection and other services may be working completely normally.
symptoms: ping to a specific device or server times out or shows 'Destination host unreachable'
The actual service on that device, such as a website or file share, works completely normally despite the failed ping
This may be entirely intentional security configuration rather than an actual problem
possibleCauses: Firewall intentionally configured to block ICMP for security reasons, which is a common and often recommended practice
Default firewall profile blocking ICMP on certain network types, such as Public networks
Firewall rule change accidentally blocked ICMP that was previously allowed
Confusion about whether ping failure indicates a real problem when the actual service works fine
diagnosticQuestions: Does the actual service on the target device, like a website or shared folder, work fine despite the failed ping?
Is this ICMP blocking intentional as part of a documented security policy?
Was ICMP working before, and did something change recently that might have accidentally blocked it?
Is understanding whether ping should work here more about troubleshooting methodology than an actual functional problem?

commands.command: netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name=all | findstr /i icmp
commands.purpose: Check for existing firewall rules specifically related to ICMP traffic
commands.expectedResult: Rules exist and are configured as intended, whether allowing or blocking ICMP based on policy
commands.abnormalResult: ICMP rules are missing, or configured opposite to what is intended by current policy

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether the actual service on the target device works fine despite the failed ping
troubleshootingSteps.reason: If the real service works, this is very likely expected security behavior rather than an actual problem needing to be fixed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check whether ICMP blocking is documented as an intentional security policy for this network or device
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many organizations intentionally block ping for security reasons, considering this normal and correct behavior

troubleshootingSteps.action: If ICMP should be allowed and previously was, check for a recent, possibly accidental firewall rule change that blocked it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Identifies whether this represents an unintended regression from previously working behavior

troubleshootingSteps.action: Add or correct a firewall rule to allow ICMP echo requests if it is determined that ping access should indeed be permitted
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Directly resolves the issue if ping functionality is genuinely needed and was unintentionally blocked

troubleshootingSteps.action: Document the decision, whether to allow or continue blocking ICMP, for future reference and consistency
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Prevents this question from repeatedly coming up as a false alarm in future troubleshooting

possibleSolutions: Recognize that ICMP being blocked while the actual service works is often not a real problem
Add a firewall rule to allow ICMP if ping access is genuinely required
Document the organization's ICMP policy for future reference
prevention: Establish and document a clear organizational policy on ICMP/ping filtering
Train staff that a failed ping does not always indicate a real connectivity problem
Review firewall rule changes carefully to avoid accidentally affecting ICMP policy

description: One or more firewall rules have been set up incorrectly, causing unintended blocking of legitimate traffic, unintended allowing of traffic that should be blocked, or general confusing network behavior.
symptoms: Specific, seemingly inconsistent network behavior that does not match expectations
Some traffic types work while similar traffic types unexpectedly fail
Security concerns if rules are found to be unintentionally too permissive
possibleCauses: Rule created with incorrect source, destination, port, or protocol values
Rule order/priority causing an unintended rule to take precedence over the intended one
Overly broad or overly narrow rule scope not matching the actual intended traffic pattern
Leftover or forgotten rules from previous troubleshooting or testing left in place
diagnosticQuestions: What specific traffic or behavior is not working as expected?
Can you review the full current list of firewall rules to look for anything unexpected or overly broad/narrow?
Were any firewall rules recently added, removed, or reordered?
Is there any chance old testing or temporary rules were left in place and forgotten?

commands.command: netsh advfirewall firewall show rule name=all
commands.purpose: List all current firewall rules for review
commands.expectedResult: Rules match the intended, documented security policy
commands.abnormalResult: Unexpected, overly broad, overly narrow, or conflicting rules found during review

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the complete current list of firewall rules methodically, comparing against documented intended policy if available
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Provides a full picture of the current configuration to identify inconsistencies or errors

troubleshootingSteps.action: Identify any rules with incorrect source, destination, port, or protocol values that do not match their intended purpose
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Pinpoints specific rules that need correction

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the order/priority of rules, since firewalls typically process rules in order and an earlier rule can override a later, more specific one
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rule order issues are a common and often overlooked source of unexpected firewall behavior

troubleshootingSteps.action: Remove or correct any identified problematic, outdated, or leftover testing rules
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Cleans up the configuration and directly resolves the specific issues found during review

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test the affected traffic patterns after making corrections to confirm the intended behavior is now occurring
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Verifies the fixes actually resolved the reported issue without introducing new problems

possibleSolutions: Correct rules with incorrect source, destination, port, or protocol values
Reorder rules if priority conflicts are causing unintended behavior
Remove outdated or leftover testing rules
Document the corrected configuration clearly
prevention: Maintain clear, up-to-date documentation of intended firewall policy
Use a change control process for firewall rule modifications
Periodically audit firewall rules for accuracy and necessity

description: The built-in Windows Firewall has been turned off entirely, whether intentionally or accidentally, leaving the computer without this layer of network protection.
symptoms: Windows Security Center shows the firewall as off or not monitored
No firewall-related connection issues occur, since nothing is being blocked, but the device has reduced protection
May trigger a security warning notification in Windows
possibleCauses: Firewall was manually turned off by a user, sometimes to troubleshoot a connectivity issue and then forgotten
Third-party security software has taken over firewall duties and disabled the Windows Firewall as part of its normal operation
Malware or unauthorized software disabled the firewall
Group Policy on a managed device intentionally or unintentionally disabled it
diagnosticQuestions: Was the Windows Firewall intentionally turned off recently, perhaps during troubleshooting?
Is third-party security software installed that might legitimately be managing firewall duties instead?
Does Windows Security Center show any other unusual security settings alongside the disabled firewall?
Is this a personal or a managed work/school computer that might have Group Policy affecting this setting?

commands.purpose: Check the current on/off state of the Windows Firewall across all network profiles
commands.expectedResult: State shows as 'ON' for the relevant profiles
commands.abnormalResult: State shows as 'OFF' for one or more profiles, confirming the firewall is currently disabled

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if legitimate third-party security software is installed and intentionally managing firewall functions instead of the built-in Windows Firewall
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many third-party security suites disable the Windows Firewall as part of normal, expected operation while providing their own protection

troubleshootingSteps.action: If no legitimate third-party firewall is active, re-enable the Windows Firewall through Windows Security settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Restores this important layer of network protection for the device

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run a full malware scan if the firewall was found disabled with no clear legitimate explanation
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Unauthorized firewall disabling can be a sign of malware attempting to reduce the device's defenses

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Group Policy settings if this is a managed work or school computer that might be intentionally controlling this setting
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Administrators may have specific policies governing firewall state that should not be manually overridden

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the firewall shows as properly enabled afterward using Windows Security settings or the netsh command
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Verifies the protection has been successfully restored

possibleSolutions: Re-enable the Windows Firewall if no other legitimate firewall solution is active
Verify third-party security software is functioning correctly if it is intentionally managing firewall duties
Run a malware scan if the firewall was disabled unexpectedly without explanation
Check Group Policy settings on managed devices if applicable
prevention: Avoid manually disabling the firewall except for brief, necessary troubleshooting, and remember to re-enable it afterward
Ensure only one firewall solution is actively managing protection to avoid conflicts
Run regular malware scans to catch unauthorized security setting changes

description: The VPN client fails to establish a connection at all, showing an error or hanging indefinitely before the underlying internet connection is even a factor.
symptoms: VPN client shows 'Cannot connect' or a generic connection failure error immediately
Connection attempt hangs on 'Connecting...' before timing out
Regular internet access works fine without the VPN active
possibleCauses: VPN server address entered incorrectly
VPN client software outdated or corrupted
Firewall on the local computer or network blocking the VPN protocol entirely
VPN server itself is down or unreachable
Local network blocks VPN traffic, common on some public or restrictive WiFi
diagnosticQuestions: Is the exact VPN server address correct and current?
Does the regular internet connection work normally without the VPN?
Have you connected successfully to this VPN before from this exact network?
Is this a public or restrictive WiFi network (hotel, airport, school) that might block VPN protocols?

commands.purpose: Test basic reachability to the VPN server before the VPN protocol itself is involved
commands.expectedResult: Replies received
commands.abnormalResult: Timeout suggests the server is unreachable or the network is blocking traffic to it entirely

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the regular internet connection works normally without the VPN enabled
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A VPN cannot connect at all without a working underlying internet connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Double-check the VPN server address and any port/protocol settings against the values provided by the VPN administrator
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A simple typo in the server address is a very common cause of an immediate connection failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try connecting from a different network, such as mobile data, to see if the current network is blocking VPN traffic
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some restrictive networks, like hotel or airport WiFi, intentionally block VPN protocols

troubleshootingSteps.action: Temporarily disable the local firewall or antivirus to test if it is blocking the VPN client entirely
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Security software can block VPN connections outright, especially after a fresh install

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the VPN client software to the latest version
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Outdated VPN clients can lose compatibility with current server configurations

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the VPN administrator to confirm the server is currently online and check if other users are affected
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out a server-side outage as the root cause

possibleSolutions: Correct the VPN server address or connection settings
Try connecting from a different, less restrictive network
Temporarily disable firewall/antivirus to confirm it as the cause, then add a proper exception
Update the VPN client software
Confirm server status with the VPN administrator
prevention: Keep VPN client software updated
Document correct server addresses and settings for reference
Test VPN connectivity before relying on it while traveling

description: The VPN client reaches the server and begins the connection process, but is rejected specifically during authentication, distinct from a complete connection failure.
symptoms: Error specifically mentions authentication failure, invalid credentials, or access denied
Connection progresses further than an immediate failure before being rejected
Other users may or may not be experiencing the same authentication issue
possibleCauses: Incorrect username or password entered
Account locked, expired, or disabled on the VPN server side
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) code expired or not entered in time
Client certificate missing, expired, or not properly installed
VPN account permissions not yet provisioned for this user
diagnosticQuestions: Are you certain the username and password are correct and current?
Does this VPN require multi-factor authentication, and was the code entered before it expired?
Does this account use a certificate for authentication, and if so, is it installed and valid?
Have you successfully authenticated to this VPN before, or is this a new account?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Carefully re-enter the username and password, checking for typos and case sensitivity
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Simple credential entry mistakes are the most common cause of authentication failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: If multi-factor authentication is required, ensure the code is entered promptly, since these codes typically expire within 30-60 seconds
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A delayed MFA code is a common and easily overlooked cause of authentication rejection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with the VPN administrator whether the account is locked, expired, or not yet fully provisioned for VPN access
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Account-level issues on the server side cannot be resolved by the end user and require administrator action

troubleshootingSteps.action: For certificate-based authentication, confirm the required client certificate is installed and has not expired
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An expired or missing certificate will cause authentication to fail even with a correct password

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try resetting the VPN account password if repeated failures occur despite confidence in the credentials
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Rules out a server-side password mismatch that the user may not be aware of

possibleSolutions: Re-enter credentials carefully, checking for typos
Enter MFA codes promptly before they expire
Have an administrator check and unlock or provision the account if needed
Install or renew a required client certificate
Reset the VPN password if authentication continues to fail
prevention: Use a password manager to avoid credential entry errors
Keep MFA apps and devices synced and accessible
Track certificate expiration dates for certificate-based VPN accounts

description: The VPN connection establishes successfully but drops repeatedly during use, requiring frequent reconnection and interrupting work.
symptoms: VPN shows connected, then disconnects after a period of time, ranging from minutes to hours
Reconnecting temporarily restores the connection until it drops again
May correlate with network changes, such as switching WiFi networks or the computer sleeping
possibleCauses: Underlying internet connection itself is unstable
VPN client's keep-alive settings not configured aggressively enough for this network
Computer's power-saving settings disconnecting the network adapter periodically
VPN server session timeout configured shorter than expected
Firewall or network equipment interrupting the long-lived VPN connection
diagnosticQuestions: Does the underlying internet connection stay stable, or does it also drop around the same time as the VPN?
How long does the VPN typically stay connected before dropping?
Does this happen more when the computer is idle, or during active use?
Have you checked the VPN client's connection/keep-alive settings?

commands.purpose: Continuously monitor the connection to the VPN server to correlate drops with the VPN client's disconnect events
commands.expectedResult: Continuous replies with no gaps
commands.abnormalResult: Periodic timeouts matching when the VPN disconnects, suggesting an underlying network instability rather than a VPN client issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether the underlying internet connection remains stable during VPN disconnects, using a continuous ping test
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Separates a genuine VPN-specific problem from a broader network instability issue that would affect the VPN as a symptom

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the computer's power management settings and disable network adapter power saving
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Aggressive power saving can briefly disconnect the network adapter, breaking the VPN tunnel

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the VPN client's settings for a keep-alive or reconnect option and enable/adjust it if available
troubleshootingSteps.reason: More frequent keep-alive signals can prevent the connection from being dropped by network equipment that closes idle connections

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with the VPN administrator about the configured session timeout on the server side
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A short server-side timeout will disconnect the client regardless of local settings

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the VPN client software to the latest version
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Connection stability bugs are commonly addressed in newer client releases

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try switching networks, such as from WiFi to a wired connection, to see if the instability follows the network rather than the VPN
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Helps isolate whether the specific network connection is contributing to the drops

possibleSolutions: Disable network adapter power saving
Enable or adjust VPN client keep-alive settings
Request a longer session timeout from the VPN administrator
Update the VPN client software
Use a more stable network connection, such as wired instead of WiFi
prevention: Keep VPN client software updated
Disable power-saving features on the network adapter for devices regularly using VPN
Use wired connections for long VPN sessions when possible

description: The VPN connects successfully and stays connected, but internet speed and responsiveness are significantly worse while connected compared to browsing without the VPN.
symptoms: Web pages, file transfers, and video calls are noticeably slower while connected to the VPN
Speed tests show a large drop in speed compared to the connection without VPN active
High latency or lag specifically while the VPN is active
possibleCauses: VPN server is geographically distant, adding natural latency
VPN server is overloaded with too many simultaneous users
VPN encryption overhead is significant on lower-powered hardware
Local internet connection itself is the bottleneck, not the VPN
Split tunneling not configured, routing all traffic unnecessarily through the VPN
diagnosticQuestions: How does speed compare with and without the VPN connected, ideally tested back-to-back?
Is the VPN server geographically close to your actual location, or very far away?
Does the VPN client offer a choice of different server locations to test?
Is split tunneling available and configured, so only necessary traffic goes through the VPN?

commands.purpose: Measure baseline latency to the VPN server itself
commands.expectedResult: Reasonably low latency appropriate for the server's geographic distance
commands.abnormalResult: Very high latency, suggesting the server's location or path is contributing significantly to the slowdown

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run a speed test with the VPN connected, then disconnect and run the same test again for direct comparison
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Quantifies exactly how much the VPN is impacting speed, providing a baseline to work from

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different VPN server location if the client offers multiple options, choosing one geographically closer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Distance to the VPN server directly affects latency and can significantly impact perceived speed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the VPN client supports split tunneling, and configure it so only traffic that actually needs the VPN uses it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Routing all traffic through the VPN unnecessarily adds overhead to activities that do not require it

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different VPN protocol if the client offers options, since some protocols have less encryption overhead than others
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Certain protocols are faster at the cost of some security trade-offs, which may be an acceptable trade for the use case

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the VPN administrator to check if the server is currently overloaded with many simultaneous users
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A server nearing its capacity will provide degraded performance to all connected users

possibleSolutions: Switch to a geographically closer VPN server
Enable split tunneling if available and appropriate
Try a different, faster VPN protocol if offered
Report server overload to the VPN administrator
Verify the underlying internet connection is not the actual bottleneck
prevention: Choose VPN server locations close to actual usage location when possible
Use split tunneling for traffic that does not require VPN protection
Monitor VPN server load if administering the infrastructure

description: The VPN client authenticates successfully but the secure tunnel itself fails to establish, so no traffic actually passes through the VPN despite an apparent successful login.
symptoms: VPN client shows 'connected' status but no internet traffic actually flows, or only local network traffic works
Error specifically mentions tunnel establishment failure rather than authentication
Websites and applications behave as if there is no internet connection at all while the VPN shows connected
possibleCauses: Firewall blocking the specific VPN tunneling protocol (such as IPsec, OpenVPN, or WireGuard) after authentication succeeds
Routing table not properly updated after the tunnel attempts to establish
MTU (maximum transmission unit) size mismatch causing packets to be dropped silently
Conflicting network adapter or VPN software creating a routing conflict
diagnosticQuestions: Does the VPN client show as fully connected, but no actual internet traffic works?
What specific VPN protocol is being used, such as IPsec, OpenVPN, SSL, or WireGuard?
Has this exact VPN connection worked before from this network, or is this a new setup?
Is any other VPN software or virtual network adapter installed that might conflict?

commands.purpose: Check whether a VPN virtual network adapter appears with a valid IP address after the tunnel attempt
commands.expectedResult: VPN adapter present with a valid assigned IP address
commands.abnormalResult: No VPN adapter appears, or it has no valid IP, confirming the tunnel did not actually establish despite a 'connected' status

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check ipconfig /all for a VPN virtual adapter and confirm whether it received a valid IP address
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms whether the tunnel genuinely established at the network level, regardless of what the client's status indicator shows

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check firewall settings for rules that might specifically block the VPN's tunneling protocol, such as IPsec (UDP 500/4500) or OpenVPN's configured port
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A firewall can allow the initial authentication handshake while still blocking the actual tunnel protocol traffic

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try lowering the MTU setting in the VPN client's advanced settings, if available
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An MTU mismatch can cause larger packets to be silently dropped, breaking the tunnel's actual data flow even after a successful handshake

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for and temporarily disable any other VPN software or virtual network adapters that might be conflicting
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Multiple VPN or virtual networking tools can create routing conflicts that prevent a new tunnel from properly taking over traffic

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the computer to clear any stuck network adapter or routing table state from a previous failed attempt
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears leftover configuration from prior connection attempts that could be interfering with a fresh tunnel

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try a different VPN protocol if the client and server support more than one option
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some protocols are more likely to be blocked by certain firewalls or networks than others

possibleSolutions: Adjust firewall rules to allow the specific VPN tunneling protocol and ports
Lower the MTU setting in VPN client advanced settings
Disable conflicting VPN or virtual networking software
Restart the computer to clear stuck network state
Try a different VPN protocol if available
prevention: Document the specific ports and protocols required by the VPN for firewall configuration
Avoid running multiple VPN clients or virtual networking tools simultaneously
Test VPN tunnel functionality after any firewall changes

description: The VPN connects and internet traffic flows, but DNS name resolution behaves incorrectly, either failing entirely, leaking outside the VPN, or resolving internal company names incorrectly.
symptoms: Websites fail to load by name while connected to the VPN, though pinging IP addresses works fine
Internal company resources, like internal websites or file servers, cannot be reached by name while on VPN
DNS leak tests show the ISP's DNS server is being used instead of the VPN's DNS server
possibleCauses: VPN client not configured to use the VPN's designated DNS server
Split tunneling configuration excluding DNS traffic from the tunnel unintentionally
Local DNS cache holding outdated entries from before connecting to the VPN
Operating system DNS settings conflicting with those pushed by the VPN
diagnosticQuestions: Do regular public websites work fine using their IP address, but fail by name while on VPN?
Are internal company resources specifically failing to resolve by name while others work?
Has a DNS leak test been run to check which DNS server is actually being used while connected?
Is split tunneling enabled, and could it be unintentionally excluding DNS traffic from the VPN tunnel?

commands.purpose: Check which DNS server responds and whether it resolves the domain correctly while connected to the VPN
commands.expectedResult: Resolves correctly using the VPN's intended DNS server
commands.abnormalResult: Fails to resolve, or resolves using an unexpected DNS server, such as the ISP's instead of the VPN's

commands.purpose: Clear the local DNS cache which may hold outdated entries from before the VPN connected
commands.expectedResult: Cache successfully flushed
commands.abnormalResult: N/A - this is a corrective action

troubleshootingSteps.action: Flush the local DNS cache after connecting to the VPN using ipconfig /flushdns
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Clears any entries cached before the VPN connected, which could otherwise continue to be used incorrectly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run nslookup on both an internal company domain and a public domain to see exactly which DNS server is responding and whether resolution succeeds
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Pinpoints whether the issue is with DNS server selection, internal-only records, or a broader failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the VPN client's settings for a DNS configuration option, ensuring it is set to use the VPN-provided DNS server rather than the local network's
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some VPN clients require this to be explicitly configured, especially for accessing internal-only company resources

troubleshootingSteps.action: If split tunneling is enabled, check whether it is unintentionally excluding DNS traffic from the tunnel
troubleshootingSteps.reason: DNS queries need to go through the VPN tunnel specifically when resolving internal, VPN-only resources

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the VPN connection after making DNS configuration changes to ensure they are fully applied
troubleshootingSteps.reason: DNS settings are often only fully applied at the time the tunnel is established

possibleSolutions: Flush the DNS cache after connecting to the VPN
Configure the VPN client to use the VPN-provided DNS server
Adjust split tunneling settings to include DNS traffic
Restart the VPN connection after DNS configuration changes
prevention: Configure DNS settings correctly as part of initial VPN client setup
Periodically run DNS leak tests on security-sensitive VPN connections
Document required DNS configuration for accessing internal company resources

description: The computer is configured to use a proxy server for internet access, but that proxy server cannot be reached, resulting in a complete loss of internet access through the browser and any proxy-aware applications.
symptoms: Browser shows an error such as 'Unable to connect to the proxy server'
No websites load in any browser or application configured to use the proxy
Applications not using the proxy, if any, may still work normally
possibleCauses: Proxy server is down or has crashed
Incorrect proxy server address or port configured
Network path to the proxy server is blocked or broken
Proxy server overloaded and not responding to new connections
diagnosticQuestions: What is the configured proxy server address and port, and is it correct?
Is the proxy server on the local network, or hosted elsewhere?
Do other users on the same network also have proxy connectivity issues right now?
Does disabling the proxy temporarily restore direct internet access, confirming the proxy itself is the point of failure?

commands.purpose: Test basic network reachability to the configured proxy server
commands.expectedResult: Replies received
commands.abnormalResult: Timeout confirms the proxy server is unreachable at the network level

commands.purpose: Test if the specific proxy port is open and accepting connections
commands.expectedResult: Connection succeeds
commands.abnormalResult: Connection refused or times out, indicating the proxy service itself is not listening or is blocked

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the exact proxy server address and port currently configured on the computer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures troubleshooting is directed at the correct, actual configured server rather than an assumption

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the proxy server address to test basic network reachability
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines if the problem is a network path issue or specifically the proxy service itself

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test the specific proxy port using telnet to see if the proxy service is actually listening and accepting connections
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A server can be reachable via ping while the specific proxy service on it has crashed or stopped

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users or the network administrator whether the proxy server is known to be down for everyone
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Determines if this is a widespread outage requiring administrator action, rather than a local configuration issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Temporarily disable the proxy setting to confirm that direct internet access works, isolating the proxy itself as the specific point of failure
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Confirms the underlying internet connection is fine and the proxy server is genuinely the blocking factor

possibleSolutions: Wait for the proxy server to be restored if it is confirmed down administrator-side
Correct the proxy server address or port if misconfigured
Temporarily disable the proxy setting if direct access is acceptable and permitted
Escalate to the network administrator if the proxy server itself has failed
prevention: Monitor proxy server uptime and health on the administrator side
Document the correct proxy configuration for end users
Consider a backup or redundant proxy server for critical environments

description: The proxy settings configured on a computer or in a browser are wrong, causing internet access to fail or behave unexpectedly even though the actual proxy server, if reached, may be working fine.
symptoms: Browser shows a proxy-related error even though the proxy server itself is confirmed to be online
Internet access works with the proxy disabled, but fails with it enabled using current settings
Websites load slowly, inconsistently, or with certificate warnings due to proxy misconfiguration
possibleCauses: Wrong proxy server address or port entered
Proxy configured for the wrong protocol, such as HTTP settings applied where HTTPS or SOCKS is required
Automatic proxy configuration (PAC) script URL incorrect or unreachable
Proxy exceptions list not configured correctly, causing internal sites to also route through the proxy unnecessarily
diagnosticQuestions: What proxy address, port, and protocol type are currently configured, and do they match what the administrator provided?
Is the proxy configured manually, or through an automatic configuration script (PAC file)?
Are there any exceptions configured, and are internal/local sites included in those exceptions appropriately?
Has the correct proxy configuration information been provided by the network administrator recently?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Obtain the correct, current proxy configuration details directly from the network administrator or official documentation
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures troubleshooting is working toward the actual correct target configuration rather than guessing

troubleshootingSteps.action: Compare the currently configured proxy address, port, and protocol against the correct values
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Identifies the specific discrepancy causing the misconfiguration

troubleshootingSteps.action: If using an automatic configuration (PAC) script, verify the PAC file URL is correct and accessible
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect or unreachable PAC file will prevent proper automatic proxy configuration from loading at all

troubleshootingSteps.action: Correct the proxy settings in the operating system's network settings and confirm the browser is set to use system proxy settings, or configure the browser directly if it manages its own settings separately
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures consistency between the operating system and browser configurations, avoiding a mismatch

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review and correct the proxy exceptions list to ensure internal/local resources are appropriately excluded from proxying if required
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Prevents internal-only resources from failing due to being unnecessarily routed through an external-facing proxy

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the browser after making changes to ensure the new configuration is fully applied
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Browsers often cache proxy settings and require a restart to pick up changes reliably

possibleSolutions: Correct the proxy server address, port, and protocol type
Fix an incorrect or unreachable PAC file URL
Update the proxy exceptions list appropriately
Ensure browser and system proxy settings are consistent
Restart the browser after making changes
prevention: Document correct proxy configuration details clearly for end users
Test proxy configuration changes on a single machine before wide deployment
Keep PAC file URLs stable and monitored for availability

description: The proxy server requires a username and password to use it, but authentication is being rejected, preventing internet access even though the proxy server itself is reachable.
symptoms: Browser repeatedly prompts for a proxy username and password, rejecting what is entered
Error message specifically mentions proxy authentication required or failed
Internet access fails specifically at the authentication step, not at basic connectivity
possibleCauses: Incorrect username or password entered for the proxy
Account credentials expired or changed on the server side
Browser or application not properly passing saved credentials to the proxy on each request
Proxy authentication method not supported by the specific browser or application being used
diagnosticQuestions: Are you certain the username and password being entered for the proxy are correct and current?
Have these credentials worked before, or is this a new proxy setup?
Does this happen in all browsers/applications, or just one specific one?
Has your account password been changed recently, which might not yet be reflected in saved proxy credentials?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Carefully re-enter the proxy username and password, checking for typos and case sensitivity
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Simple credential entry errors are a common cause of repeated authentication rejection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Clear any saved/cached proxy credentials in the browser and enter them fresh when prompted
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Outdated cached credentials, especially after a recent password change, will continue to fail until refreshed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm with the network administrator whether the proxy account is active, unlocked, and using the expected authentication method
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Account-level issues on the server side require administrator intervention and cannot be resolved by re-entering the same credentials

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test the same credentials in a different browser or application to determine if the issue is specific to one program's handling of proxy authentication
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some applications handle proxy authentication differently, and isolating this helps determine the true scope of the problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the proxy uses a specific authentication method, such as NTLM or Basic, and confirm the browser or application supports it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A mismatch in supported authentication methods will cause every attempt to fail regardless of how correct the credentials are

possibleSolutions: Re-enter proxy credentials carefully
Clear cached proxy credentials and re-enter fresh
Confirm account status with the network administrator
Verify the browser/application supports the proxy's authentication method
prevention: Use a password manager to reduce credential entry errors
Update saved proxy credentials promptly after any password change
Document the proxy's required authentication method for reference

description: A web browser is using an unintended or outdated proxy configuration, different from what the operating system or the user actually intends, causing inconsistent or failed internet access specifically in that browser.
symptoms: One specific browser fails to access the internet or behaves differently, while other browsers or applications work normally
Browser's own proxy settings differ from the operating system's configured proxy
Websites that should be excluded via proxy exceptions still route through the proxy in this specific browser
possibleCauses: Browser configured to use its own manual proxy settings instead of the system's settings
Browser extension silently changing or overriding proxy configuration
Old proxy settings cached in the browser from a previous network or job
Browser profile corruption affecting stored network settings
diagnosticQuestions: Does this specific browser have its own separate proxy settings, distinct from the operating system's configuration?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the specific browser's own network/proxy settings and compare them against the operating system's configured proxy
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reveals whether the browser is using its own separate, possibly outdated, configuration instead of following the system settings

troubleshootingSteps.action: Set the browser to use the system's proxy settings if it offers this option, rather than maintaining a separate manual configuration
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Ensures consistency and reduces the chance of the browser drifting out of sync with the correct, current proxy configuration

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check installed browser extensions for anything that could be modifying proxy or network settings, and disable them one at a time to test
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some extensions, particularly those related to privacy, ad blocking, or VPN services, can silently override proxy configuration

troubleshootingSteps.action: Clear the browser's cached network configuration or reset browser settings to default, then reconfigure the correct proxy settings fresh
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Removes any lingering incorrect configuration from a previous network or job that may still be cached

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test in a new browser profile to rule out a corrupted profile as the source of the incorrect proxy behavior

possibleSolutions: Set the browser to use system proxy settings rather than its own separate configuration
Disable browser extensions that may be overriding proxy settings
Reset browser network settings to default and reconfigure correctly

prevention: Prefer system-wide proxy configuration over per-browser settings where possible

Update browser proxy settings promptly after any network or job change

description: Attempting to access a shared folder by its network path results in a specific 'network path was not found' error, distinct from a permissions-related access denial.

The computer name in the path is incorrect or cannot be resolved
