problem: Cannot delete or rename a file because it is locked
description: The user tries to delete or rename a file on a shared drive, but the action fails with a message indicating the file is currently in use or locked by another process or user.
symptoms: Error message stating the file is 'in use by another program' when trying to delete or rename
The action fails even though the file appears normal when simply viewing it
The operation succeeds after waiting or after the other user closes their session
May happen consistently with certain frequently used files
possibleCauses: Another user currently has the file open in an editing program
A background process, such as antivirus scanning or a sync client, is temporarily accessing the file
A stale lock remains from a previous session that did not close properly
The file is set as a template or is actively referenced by another running application
diagnosticQuestions: Do you know if anyone else might currently have this file open?
Could a background program, such as antivirus or a backup tool, be scanning this file right now?
Does this specific error happen consistently with this file, or was this a one-time occurrence?
Have you tried waiting a few minutes and attempting the action again?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with colleagues to see if anyone currently has this specific file open
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A genuinely open file by another user is one of the most common and simple explanations for this type of lock

troubleshootingSteps.action: Wait a few minutes and attempt the delete or rename action again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Temporary locks from background processes, such as a brief antivirus scan, often clear on their own after a short time

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the file is confirmed to not be open by anyone, consider whether a background process like antivirus or a backup and sync tool might be actively scanning or accessing it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: These background tools can briefly lock files during their normal operation, which resolves once their specific task completes

troubleshootingSteps.action: Close any related applications that might have automatically opened this file type in the background, even if not visibly open on screen
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some applications hold files open in the background even when their main window is not actively visible or in use

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the lock persists for an extended period despite confirming no one has it open, contact the file server administrator to check for and manually clear a stale lock
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Administrators have server-side tools to view and release locks that a standard user cannot access directly

troubleshootingSteps.action: As an alternative approach for an urgent need, consider making a copy of the file under a different name if renaming the original is not strictly necessary
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides a practical workaround for immediate needs while the underlying lock issue with the original file is being resolved

possibleSolutions: Wait for another user or background process to release the file
Close background applications that may be holding the file open silently
Have the administrator manually clear a persistent stale lock
Work with a copy of the file as a temporary workaround if appropriate
prevention: Properly close files when finished rather than leaving programs running in the background
Coordinate file access timing with colleagues for frequently used shared files
Report frequently recurring lock issues on specific files to the administrator
keywords: file in use by another program

description: When a file that syncs between multiple locations, such as offline files or a sync client, is edited by more than one person or device around the same time, a conflict occurs, resulting in multiple versions of the file needing to be reconciled.
symptoms: A notification or conflict file appears, such as 'filename (Conflicted Copy).docx'
Two or more versions of what should be the same file now exist
A sync client shows a specific conflict warning icon on the file
Recent changes from one person or device appear to be missing
possibleCauses: Two people edited the same file at the same time while both were offline or briefly disconnected from the server
A device went offline while editing and made changes that conflicted with changes made elsewhere in the meantime
Sync timing caused two versions to be saved before either could be properly merged
The file was edited directly on the server while a separate offline or cached copy was also being edited
diagnosticQuestions: Do you see a specific 'conflicted copy' file, or a conflict warning within your sync tool?
Were you working on this file while offline or disconnected from the network recently?
Do you know if someone else was also editing this same file around the same time?
Which version appears to have the most complete or recent legitimate changes?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Identify all versions of the file involved in the conflict, including the original and any conflicted copies created
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Understanding exactly how many versions exist is the first step before deciding how to properly reconcile them

troubleshootingSteps.action: Open each version and carefully compare their content to understand what changes exist in each one
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine which version contains the most complete or important set of legitimate changes

troubleshootingSteps.action: If possible, contact anyone else who may have been editing the file around the same time to understand what changes they made
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides important context to help decide how the different sets of changes should be properly combined

troubleshootingSteps.action: Manually merge the important changes from all versions into a single, correct final version
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures no legitimate work from any contributor is lost during the conflict resolution process

troubleshootingSteps.action: Save the properly merged version as the main file, and delete or archive the extra conflicted copies once you are confident the merge is complete and accurate
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This cleans up the confusion of multiple versions once the correct final content has been properly consolidated

troubleshootingSteps.action: If this type of conflict happens frequently, discuss with your team establishing a clearer process for who edits which files and when, especially for frequently offline users
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps prevent repeated conflicts by improving how the team coordinates around shared file editing

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider using a collaborative online editing tool for frequently co-edited documents, if available, since these are specifically designed to handle simultaneous editing without creating conflicts
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Purpose-built collaborative tools handle simultaneous edits far more gracefully than simple file syncing, preventing this type of conflict from occurring in the first place

possibleSolutions: Carefully compare and manually merge changes from all conflicted versions
Consult with other contributors to understand their specific changes
Save a single, correctly merged final version and clean up extra copies
Establish clearer team processes for editing frequently shared files
Use a purpose-built collaborative editing tool for frequently co-edited documents
prevention: Coordinate editing schedules for frequently shared documents
Use collaborative online editing tools designed for simultaneous access
Minimize extended offline editing periods for actively shared files
Communicate clearly when beginning and finishing edits to shared files

problem: Domain authentication failed when accessing a shared resource
description: The user tries to access a shared folder that requires domain authentication, but the connection attempt fails specifically at the authentication stage, even though the network connection itself is working.
symptoms: Error message specifically mentioning domain authentication or trust failure
A credential prompt appears repeatedly without accepting valid-seeming credentials
The share is reachable at the network level but authentication consistently fails
Problem may be isolated to domain-based shares while workgroup shares work fine
possibleCauses: The user's computer has lost its trust relationship with the domain
The user's domain account password has recently changed and cached credentials are outdated
A time synchronization difference between the client computer and the domain controller
The domain controller itself is temporarily unreachable, preventing authentication
The user is attempting to authenticate with an incorrect domain prefix or format
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen with all domain-based shares, or just one specific one?
Have you changed your domain password recently?
Is your computer's date and time set correctly, including the correct time zone?
Are other domain-joined computers able to access this same share successfully?

commands.purpose: Check the secure channel (trust relationship) status between the computer and the domain
commands.expectedResult: Message shows the trust test completed successfully
commands.abnormalResult: Message shows a failure, confirming a broken trust relationship affecting all domain authentication

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether this authentication failure happens with all domain-based shares, or is isolated to just one specific share
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A problem affecting all domain shares points to a broader issue with your computer's domain trust, while an isolated issue points to something specific to that one share's permissions

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm your domain account password has not recently changed without your cached credentials being updated
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An outdated cached password is a common and simple cause of repeated authentication failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check and correct your computer's date, time, and time zone settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Domain authentication (Kerberos) is sensitive to time differences, and a significant clock discrepancy between your computer and the domain controller can cause authentication to fail

troubleshootingSteps.action: Clear any outdated saved credentials for the specific share in Windows Credential Manager, then try accessing it again with fresh credentials
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Old, cached, incorrect credentials can interfere with a new authentication attempt even when the currently entered credentials are correct

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the domain controller is currently reachable, since authentication cannot succeed if the domain controller itself cannot be contacted
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Domain-based authentication requires successfully communicating with a domain controller, and this being unreachable would explain widespread authentication failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the trust relationship between your computer and the domain appears broken, this typically requires an administrator to properly rejoin the computer to the domain
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A broken domain trust relationship needs administrator-level access to repair by removing and rejoining the computer to the domain

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the IT department or domain administrator if the issue persists, providing specific details about which shares are affected and any exact error messages
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Domain trust and authentication issues typically require administrator-level tools to properly diagnose and resolve

possibleSolutions: Update outdated cached credentials with the current password
Correct the computer's date, time, and time zone settings
Clear old saved credentials in Credential Manager and reauthenticate
Have the administrator repair a broken domain trust relationship
Wait for a temporarily unreachable domain controller to become available again
prevention: Keep computer date and time settings synced automatically
Update saved credentials promptly after any password change
Avoid restoring very old backups of domain-joined computers without proper preparation

problem: Guest access is denied when trying to access a share
description: The user, often on a different network or without a proper domain account, tries to access a shared folder expecting guest-level access to work, but is denied, since modern systems often restrict or disable guest access by default.
symptoms: Error specifically mentioning guest access being denied or disabled
Anonymous or guest-level connection attempts fail even though a valid account would work
Older devices or systems relying on guest access may be specifically affected
Message may reference network security policy restricting guest logins
possibleCauses: Modern Windows versions disable insecure guest access to SMB shares by default for security reasons
The share was never actually configured to allow guest or anonymous access
A security policy update disabled previously working guest access
The connecting device or older operating system is specifically relying on an outdated, insecure guest authentication method
diagnosticQuestions: Do you have a proper user account that could be used instead of guest access?
Did guest access to this specific share work previously, or is this a new attempt?
What type of device or operating system are you connecting from?
Do you know if this share was ever intentionally configured to support guest access?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Determine whether a proper individual user account exists that could be used instead of relying on guest access
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Modern security best practice strongly favors using individual accounts over guest access, and this is often the most appropriate and secure solution

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a proper user account is available, use it to authenticate instead of attempting guest access
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides a secure, supported way to access the share without needing to weaken security settings to allow insecure guest access

troubleshootingSteps.action: If guest access is genuinely required for a legitimate business reason, such as older equipment that cannot use modern authentication, discuss this specific need with the IT security team
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Enabling guest access involves a security trade-off that should be carefully considered and approved by those responsible for network security policy

troubleshootingSteps.action: If IT approves enabling guest access for a specific, understood reason, they can adjust the relevant security policy or share settings to allow it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is an administrator-level change that should be made deliberately and with an understanding of the associated security implications

troubleshootingSteps.action: For older devices needing to connect, consider whether they can be updated or reconfigured to support modern, secure authentication methods instead of relying on legacy guest access
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This addresses the root cause at the device level rather than reducing security at the network level

troubleshootingSteps.action: As a longer-term solution, consider replacing outdated equipment that cannot support current security standards with something more modern and compatible
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is often the most sustainable path forward, since maintaining outdated insecure guest access indefinitely increases overall security risk

possibleSolutions: Use a proper individual user account instead of guest access
Discuss a legitimate business need for guest access with the IT security team
Have IT deliberately enable guest access if appropriately justified and approved
Update or replace older devices to support modern secure authentication
prevention: Avoid relying on guest access for ongoing business needs
Use proper individual accounts for all regular file share access
Plan for updating or replacing equipment that only supports outdated authentication methods

problem: Cannot ping the file server or its IP address is unreachable
description: The user or administrator tries to test basic connectivity to the file server using a ping command, but receives no response, indicating a fundamental network-level problem reaching the server.
symptoms: Ping command returns 'Request timed out' for every attempt
No other network services on that server are reachable either
Other servers or devices on the network may still be reachable normally
Problem may be consistent or intermittent
possibleCauses: The file server is powered off or has crashed
A network cable or switch port connected to the server has failed
The server's IP address has changed without being properly communicated
A firewall is specifically blocking ICMP ping requests, even though other services might still work
A routing problem exists between the user's network segment and the server's segment
diagnosticQuestions: Are other servers or devices on the network reachable normally at the same time?
Has the file server's IP address changed recently?
Do you know if a firewall might be specifically configured to block ping requests to this server?
Is this happening from one specific location or network, or from everywhere?

commands.purpose: Directly test basic network reachability to the server's known IP address
commands.expectedResult: Replies received from the server
commands.abnormalResult: Request timed out consistently, confirming a fundamental network-level unreachability

commands.purpose: Trace the network path to the server to identify where along the route the connection is failing
commands.expectedResult: Shows a complete path of hops reaching the destination server
commands.abnormalResult: The trace stops or times out at a specific point before reaching the destination, indicating where the network path is broken

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm other servers and devices on the network are reachable normally at the same time
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is specific to this one server, or reflects a broader network issue affecting your connection generally

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the IP address being used for the file server is still current and correct
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An outdated or incorrect IP address would naturally fail to respond, even though the actual server might be perfectly healthy at its real current address

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use tracert to see how far the network path successfully reaches before failing
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps identify whether the problem is close to your own network, somewhere in the middle of the path, or specifically at the final destination server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider whether a firewall might be specifically configured to block ICMP ping requests to this server, even while normal file sharing services might still work
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some security configurations intentionally block ping responses as a security measure, which would not necessarily mean the actual file sharing service is down

troubleshootingSteps.action: If ping is blocked by design, try directly testing an actual file share connection instead of relying solely on ping results
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps confirm whether the underlying service is truly unreachable, or if it was simply ping specifically that was blocked

troubleshootingSteps.action: This type of network-level unreachability, if confirmed genuine, typically requires network or server administrator investigation into the physical server status and network infrastructure
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Diagnosing and fixing server power, cabling, switch, or routing issues requires administrative and often physical access

troubleshootingSteps.action: Report the issue to the network administrator, providing the specific server, its expected IP address, and confirming whether other network resources remain reachable
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides essential diagnostic information for the administrator to investigate the physical server and network infrastructure

possibleSolutions: Confirm and use the server's current, correct IP address
Test an actual file share connection if ping is intentionally blocked by firewall policy
Report a confirmed unreachable server to the network administrator for physical/infrastructure investigation
Use tracert results to help pinpoint where along the network path the failure occurs
prevention: Keep documented, current IP addresses for important servers
Communicate IP address changes proactively to relevant users and systems
Maintain redundant network connections for critical file servers

problem: DNS cannot resolve the file server's hostname
description: The user tries to access a shared folder using the file server's name, but the connection fails because the name cannot be translated into the correct IP address, even though the server itself may be online.
symptoms: Error message such as 'The specified server cannot be found' when using the server name
Accessing the same share by IP address works correctly
The problem may affect only this one server name, while others resolve normally
Nslookup or ping by name fails, while ping by IP succeeds
possibleCauses: The DNS record for the file server is missing, incorrect, or outdated
The user's computer is using an incorrect or unreachable DNS server
A recent change to the file server's IP address was not updated in DNS
Local DNS cache contains outdated, incorrect information for this specific server name
The user is on a different network without access to the internal DNS server hosting this record
diagnosticQuestions: Does accessing the same share work correctly when using its IP address instead of its name?
Do other server or computer names resolve correctly from your current location?
Has the file server's IP address changed recently?
Are you connected to the internal company network, or a different network such as a home or public Wi-Fi?

commands.purpose: Directly query DNS to see if and how the server name resolves
commands.expectedResult: Returns the correct, current IP address for the file server
commands.abnormalResult: 'Non-existent domain' or an incorrect/outdated IP address, confirming a DNS resolution problem

commands.purpose: Clear the local DNS cache in case it holds outdated information for this server name
commands.expectedResult: Confirmation that the DNS cache was successfully flushed
commands.abnormalResult: Not applicable; this is a maintenance command rather than a diagnostic one

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try accessing the same share using the file server's IP address instead of its name
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly confirms whether the underlying server and share are actually reachable, isolating the problem specifically to name resolution

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use nslookup to directly query DNS for this specific server name and see what result, if any, is returned
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This shows exactly what your computer's DNS resolution process is currently returning for this name

troubleshootingSteps.action: Flush the local DNS cache using ipconfig /flushdns, then try accessing the share by name again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This clears any outdated or corrupted cached DNS information that might be causing the resolution failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether you are connected to the correct network, such as the internal company network or an active VPN, since internal server names often only resolve through internal DNS servers
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Internal server names typically cannot be resolved from external networks like home Wi-Fi without a proper VPN connection providing access to internal DNS

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users on the same network to see if they can successfully resolve this same server name
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is specific to your computer's DNS configuration, or reflects a broader DNS record problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the server's IP address changed recently, confirm with the network administrator whether the corresponding DNS record was properly updated
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An outdated DNS record pointing to an old, no-longer-valid IP address would explain resolution succeeding but connecting to the wrong or no destination

troubleshootingSteps.action: Report the issue to the network or DNS administrator if it persists, providing the specific server name and confirming that the IP address connection works correctly
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides clear evidence that the issue is specifically DNS-related, helping the administrator focus their investigation accordingly

possibleSolutions: Use the server's IP address as an immediate workaround
Flush the local DNS cache
Connect to the correct internal network or VPN for internal DNS resolution
Have the administrator correct an outdated DNS record after a server IP change
prevention: Update DNS records promptly whenever a server's IP address changes
Ensure remote users have proper VPN access to internal DNS when needed
Periodically verify critical server DNS records remain accurate

problem: Firewall is blocking file sharing access
description: The user has a working network connection to the general area of the file server, but a firewall, either on their own computer, the server, or a network device in between, is specifically blocking the ports needed for file sharing to function.
symptoms: The server responds to a basic ping, but shares still cannot be accessed
Error messages specifically related to connection refusal rather than the server being unreachable
Problem may have started after installing new antivirus or security software
Access works fine on some networks but not others, such as a new office location
possibleCauses: Windows Firewall on the user's computer is blocking outgoing file sharing connections
Windows Firewall on the file server is blocking incoming file sharing connections
A network firewall or security appliance between the two networks is blocking the specific SMB ports
Newly installed antivirus or security software introduced its own firewall blocking file sharing
A recent security policy update tightened firewall rules affecting file sharing
diagnosticQuestions: Does the server respond to a basic ping, even though the actual share connection fails?
Did this start right after installing new antivirus or security software?
Does this happen on all networks, or specifically one location, such as a new office or remote connection?
Are other users on the same network experiencing the same specific issue?

commands.purpose: Test if the SMB file sharing port (445) is open and reachable on the file server
commands.expectedResult: Connection succeeds or shows a blank screen, meaning the port is open
commands.abnormalResult: 'Could not open connection', confirming the specific SMB port is being blocked somewhere along the path

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the server responds to a basic ping, which helps establish that general network connectivity exists, even if the specific file sharing ports are blocked
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This narrows the problem down specifically to file sharing ports being blocked, rather than a complete network unreachability issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test whether the specific SMB port (typically port 445) is reachable using a tool like telnet
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly tests whether the specific port required for file sharing is open, isolating the problem to that exact port rather than general connectivity

troubleshootingSteps.action: Temporarily disable Windows Firewall on your own computer to test if it is the source of the block, remembering to turn it back on afterward
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This quickly confirms whether your own computer's firewall is the cause, versus something on the server or network side

troubleshootingSteps.action: If disabling your firewall resolves the issue, add an appropriate exception for file and printer sharing in Windows Firewall rather than leaving it permanently disabled
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This maintains your computer's security while specifically allowing the necessary file sharing traffic

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a newly installed antivirus or security program is suspected, check its separate firewall settings for file sharing exceptions
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many antivirus programs include their own independent firewall that can block traffic even when Windows Firewall itself is properly configured

troubleshootingSteps.action: If your own computer's firewall settings appear correct, check with the network or server administrator whether the file server's firewall allows incoming connections from your specific network location
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The block could be on the receiving end rather than your own computer, especially if this is a new office or network location

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a network firewall or security appliance sits between your location and the server, such as when connecting from a different office, ask the network administrator to confirm the necessary file sharing ports are allowed between these specific network segments
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Inter-office or inter-segment firewalls are a common but often overlooked source of blocked file sharing traffic in larger organizations

possibleSolutions: Add a file and printer sharing exception in Windows Firewall
Adjust third-party antivirus firewall settings to allow file sharing
Have the administrator open the necessary port on the file server's firewall
Request the network administrator allow file sharing traffic between specific network segments
prevention: Document required firewall exceptions for file sharing across the organization
Test file sharing access after installing new security software
Coordinate firewall rule changes with IT before connecting from new network locations

problem: VPN is not connected, preventing access to shared folders
description: The user is working remotely and tries to access internal shared folders, but access fails because the required VPN connection to the company network is not currently active.
symptoms: Shared folders and internal resources are completely unreachable
Internet browsing and other non-internal resources may work normally
VPN client shows as disconnected or not running
Access works fine when physically in the office, but not remotely
possibleCauses: The VPN client was not started or connected before attempting to access internal resources
The VPN connection dropped unexpectedly at some point during the work session
Incorrect VPN credentials or an expired VPN certificate is preventing connection
A local internet connectivity issue is preventing the VPN itself from establishing
diagnosticQuestions: Is your VPN client currently showing as connected or disconnected?
Are you able to access general internet websites normally at the moment?
Have you successfully connected to this VPN and accessed shares before?
Did the VPN connection possibly drop partway through your work session?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your VPN client's current status to confirm whether it shows as connected or disconnected
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the most direct and immediate check, since internal shares are typically completely unreachable without an active VPN connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: If disconnected, start and connect the VPN client using your normal credentials
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly establishes the required connection to the internal company network needed to reach shared folders

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm your general internet connection is working normally, since a working internet connection is required before the VPN itself can even attempt to connect
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A VPN cannot establish a connection without a working underlying internet connection to build upon

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once the VPN shows as successfully connected, try accessing the shared folder again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This confirms whether the VPN connection alone was the missing piece needed to restore access

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the VPN fails to connect with an error, such as an authentication failure, follow standard VPN troubleshooting, including double-checking your credentials
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A failed VPN connection attempt itself needs to be resolved before shared folder access, which depends on it, can be expected to work

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the VPN was connected but access still fails, or the VPN disconnects shortly after connecting, check for a stable, strong internet connection, since an unstable connection can cause VPN drops
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An intermittently dropping VPN connection would explain access that seems to work briefly before failing again

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact IT support if the VPN consistently fails to connect or maintain a stable connection despite correct credentials and a working internet connection
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Persistent VPN connectivity issues may require administrator-level investigation into the VPN server or your specific account configuration

possibleSolutions: Start and connect the VPN client before accessing internal shares
Confirm and restore general internet connectivity first if needed
Resolve VPN authentication issues if the connection attempt itself fails
Contact IT support for persistent VPN connectivity problems
prevention: Always connect the VPN before attempting to access internal resources remotely
Keep VPN client software updated
Maintain a stable, reliable internet connection when working remotely

problem: SMB service is unavailable or has stopped
description: The underlying Server Message Block (SMB) service responsible for Windows file sharing has stopped or is not functioning, preventing any file sharing connections to or from the affected computer.
symptoms: All file sharing connections to a specific computer fail simultaneously
The computer may still respond to ping but not to any sharing-related requests
Other network services on the same computer, unrelated to file sharing, may work normally
Restarting the computer often temporarily resolves the issue
possibleCauses: The Server service (which handles SMB file sharing) has stopped or crashed on the host computer
A recent Windows update affected the SMB service configuration
A conflict with security software interfering with the SMB service
SMB has been intentionally disabled as part of a security hardening configuration
diagnosticQuestions: Does this affect all file sharing from this specific computer, or just one particular share?
Does the affected computer respond normally to a basic ping?
Has this computer been restarted recently, and did that temporarily resolve the issue?
Did this start after a recent Windows update or security software change?

commands.purpose: Check the status of the 'Server' service, which is responsible for SMB file sharing, on the host computer
commands.expectedResult: The Server service shows a status of 'Running'
commands.abnormalResult: The service is stopped, confirming it as the direct cause of the complete file sharing failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: On the host computer, open the Services management console and check the status of the 'Server' service
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the core Windows service responsible for SMB file sharing, and confirming its status directly identifies whether it is the cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the Server service is stopped, start it manually and set its startup type to Automatic if it is not already configured that way
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly restores file sharing functionality and helps ensure it starts properly on future restarts

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the host computer, since this often resolves an underlying issue that caused the service to stop in the first place
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A fresh restart clears many temporary conditions that can cause core Windows services to become unresponsive

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for and install any pending Windows updates on the host computer, since some update-related issues affecting SMB have been resolved in subsequent updates
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Keeping the system current addresses known bugs that may be specifically affecting the SMB service

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check third-party security software installed on the host computer for any settings that might be interfering with or blocking the SMB service
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some security software can interfere with core Windows services, including those responsible for file sharing

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether SMB has been intentionally disabled as part of a security policy, especially if this is a recently hardened or newly configured computer
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some organizations intentionally disable or restrict SMB for security reasons, which would mean this behavior is expected rather than a malfunction

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the Server service repeatedly stops on its own after being restarted, check the Windows Event Viewer for specific error details, and escalate to IT support for deeper investigation
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A service that repeatedly crashes indicates an underlying problem that requires more detailed log analysis to properly diagnose and fix

possibleSolutions: Start the Server service and set it to Automatic startup
Restart the host computer
Install pending Windows updates that may address known SMB issues
Adjust third-party security software interfering with the service
Escalate a repeatedly crashing service to IT for deeper investigation
prevention: Keep the host computer's Windows updates current
Set the Server service to Automatic startup
Monitor for repeated service crashes as an early warning sign of a deeper issue

description: The user's computer and the file server use different, incompatible versions of the SMB file sharing protocol, causing the connection to fail even though both systems are otherwise online and reachable.
symptoms: Connection specifically fails with an error referencing protocol or version compatibility
Older devices cannot connect to newer, more securely configured servers, or vice versa
The server and client both respond to basic network tests, but sharing specifically fails
Problem is more common when connecting older equipment to modern, hardened servers
possibleCauses: The server has disabled older, insecure SMB versions (such as SMBv1) that an older client still relies on
The client computer has disabled a newer SMB version that the server requires
A significant version gap exists between very old and very new systems with no overlapping compatible version
Security hardening on one side removed support for a protocol version still needed by the other side
diagnosticQuestions: Is this an older computer or device trying to connect to a newer, more recently configured server, or the reverse?
Do other, more modern computers connect to this same server successfully?
Do you know if SMBv1 has been intentionally disabled anywhere in this environment for security reasons?
What operating system versions are involved on both the client and server side?

commands.purpose: Check which SMB protocol versions are currently enabled on a Windows computer acting as the server (run in PowerShell)
commands.expectedResult: Shows the currently enabled SMB protocol versions
commands.abnormalResult: Shows that the specific version needed by the client, or by the server for the client, is disabled

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether the issue involves an older device connecting to a newer server, or the reverse, and note the specific operating systems involved
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps identify which side is likely missing support for a version the other side requires

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other, more modern computers to see if they can connect to the same server successfully
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps confirm whether the issue is specific to the older or differently configured client, rather than a broader server problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Recognize that older, insecure SMB versions like SMBv1 are increasingly disabled by default on modern systems for important security reasons
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Understanding this context helps frame the appropriate solution as updating the outdated component rather than simply re-enabling an insecure legacy protocol

troubleshootingSteps.action: Where possible, prioritize updating or replacing the outdated device or operating system to support modern, secure SMB versions
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This addresses the root cause properly by bringing the outdated component up to current security standards, rather than weakening the more modern, secure system

troubleshootingSteps.action: If updating the outdated device is not immediately possible, and after careful security consideration, an administrator may need to temporarily enable an older SMB version specifically for that legacy connection
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is a security trade-off that should only be made deliberately, ideally paired with a plan to fully phase out the legacy dependency as soon as possible

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use the Get-SmbServerConfiguration PowerShell command on the relevant Windows computer to check exactly which SMB versions are currently enabled
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides precise technical confirmation of the current configuration, useful for the administrator making any necessary adjustment

troubleshootingSteps.action: Document any legacy SMB version support that is enabled as a temporary exception, along with a plan and timeline to eventually remove the outdated dependency
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the security trade-off remains temporary and intentional, rather than becoming an unmanaged, permanent weakness

possibleSolutions: Update or replace the outdated device or operating system to support modern SMB versions
Have an administrator deliberately and temporarily enable an older SMB version if truly necessary
Document and plan to phase out any legacy SMB version dependency
Confirm exact current SMB configuration using PowerShell commands
prevention: Keep all devices updated to support modern, secure SMB versions
Plan proactively to retire legacy equipment relying on outdated protocols
Avoid re-enabling insecure legacy protocols except as a carefully managed, temporary exception

problem: File sharing or Network Discovery is disabled
description: The computer's overall settings have file sharing or network discovery turned off, preventing it from either sharing its own folders with others, seeing other computers on the network, or both.
symptoms: The computer cannot see other computers when browsing the network
Other computers cannot see or access shares hosted on this computer
Network and Sharing Center shows sharing options as turned off
Problem affects this specific computer while others on the same network work normally
possibleCauses: File sharing and Network Discovery were never enabled on this computer
These settings were turned off intentionally or accidentally at some point
The network location profile is set to 'Public' rather than 'Private', which uses more restrictive default settings
A security policy specifically disabled these features on this computer
diagnosticQuestions: Is this happening on your own computer (unable to share out), another computer you are trying to reach, or both?
Do you know what network profile, such as Private or Public, this computer is currently using?
Has file sharing worked on this specific computer before?
Is this a personal computer or a company-managed one with possible policy restrictions?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Open Network and Sharing Center (or the equivalent Network settings) and check the current status of Network Discovery and File and Printer Sharing
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly shows whether these essential features are currently turned on or off

troubleshootingSteps.action: If disabled, turn on both Network Discovery and File and Printer Sharing
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Both of these features generally need to be enabled for a computer to properly participate in file sharing on the network, either as a host or a client browsing for others

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the current network profile assigned to your active connection, confirming whether it is set to Private or Public
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Windows applies more restrictive default sharing settings automatically to networks marked as Public, which is intended to protect computers on unfamiliar or public networks

troubleshootingSteps.action: If you are on a trusted network, such as your home or office, and it is incorrectly marked as Public, change the network profile to Private
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This applies the more permissive default settings appropriate for a trusted network, which typically includes enabling file sharing features more readily

troubleshootingSteps.action: On a company-managed computer, check with IT whether these settings are being centrally controlled by a security policy
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Organizations sometimes intentionally restrict these features by policy, meaning a manual change might be reverted, or might not be the appropriate expected solution

troubleshootingSteps.action: After making changes, restart the computer or at least the relevant network services to ensure the new settings are fully applied
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some sharing-related services need to be restarted or the computer rebooted for changes to take full effect

troubleshootingSteps.action: Test both browsing to other computers and confirming other computers can now see and access shares on this one
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This confirms both directions of the desired functionality are now working properly

possibleSolutions: Enable Network Discovery and File and Printer Sharing
Change the network profile from Public to Private for trusted networks
Confirm and align with any company IT policy governing these settings
Restart the computer or relevant services after making changes
prevention: Confirm correct network profile assignment when connecting to new trusted networks
Document expected sharing settings for company computers
Understand your organization's policy on network discovery and sharing defaults

problem: File upload or download fails on a shared or web-connected folder
description: The user attempts to upload a file to a shared location or download one from it, but the transfer fails partway through, shows an error, or does not start at all.
symptoms: Error message during upload or download
Transfer progress stalls partway through and does not complete
The transferred file, if it does complete, is corrupted or incomplete
Problem may happen with all files, or specifically large ones
possibleCauses: A network interruption occurred during the transfer
The file exceeds a size limit imposed by the destination or transfer method
Insufficient permissions at the source or destination for the specific transfer direction
Insufficient storage space at the destination
A temporary server-side issue affecting file transfer capability
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen with all files, or specifically large ones?
Is your network connection stable throughout the attempted transfer?
Have you successfully uploaded or downloaded files to this same location before?
Does the error give any specific reason, such as a size limit or permissions issue?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your network connection stability, since an interrupted connection during a transfer is one of the most common causes of upload or download failures
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A dropped connection partway through directly causes an incomplete or failed transfer

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the file is unusually large, check if there is a known size limit for this specific upload or download method
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many systems impose maximum file size limits, and exceeding this will cause the transfer to fail, sometimes without a very clear error

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the file is large, try compressing it or splitting it into smaller parts if the destination and use case allow this approach
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reducing the file size can bring it within allowed limits and also reduces the chance of a network interruption affecting the transfer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm you have the correct permissions for the specific direction of transfer, such as read access for downloading from the source, or write access for uploading to the destination
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient permissions for the specific transfer direction will block the operation even when general access to the location seems to work

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available storage space at the destination, since insufficient space will prevent an upload from completing successfully
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A destination that is full or nearly full cannot accept new files, causing the transfer to fail

troubleshootingSteps.action: Retry the transfer after a brief pause, in case this was a temporary, one-time network or server issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some transfer failures are caused by brief, non-repeating glitches that succeed on a subsequent attempt

troubleshootingSteps.action: If transfers of this type consistently fail despite these checks, report the issue to the system or network administrator with specific details about file size and the exact error encountered
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides the necessary information to investigate a potential systemic limit or server-side issue affecting file transfers

possibleSolutions: Ensure a stable network connection throughout the transfer
Reduce file size through compression or splitting if size limits are the issue
Confirm correct permissions for the specific transfer direction
Free up storage space at the destination
Report persistent transfer failures to the administrator with specific details
prevention: Maintain a stable network connection for important file transfers
Be aware of file size limits before attempting large transfers
Monitor destination storage space regularly
Compress large files proactively when appropriate

problem: File copy or move operation fails or is interrupted
description: The user tries to copy or move one or more files to or from a shared network location, but the operation fails partway through, shows an error, or is interrupted before completing.
symptoms: Error message appears partway through a copy or move operation
The progress bar stalls and does not complete
Some files in a batch copy succeed while others fail
The operation may fail consistently with certain files or folders
possibleCauses: A network interruption occurred during the operation
One or more files in the batch are locked or in use by another process
Insufficient permissions for specific files within a larger folder structure
The destination has run out of available storage space partway through
A very long file path or file name exceeding system limits for certain files
diagnosticQuestions: Does the failure happen with all files being copied or moved, or just some specific ones?
Is your network connection stable throughout the operation?
Do you know if any of the files involved might currently be open or in use?
How large is the overall amount of data being copied or moved?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note whether the failure affects the entire operation, or just specific individual files within a larger batch
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps distinguish between a broader connectivity or space issue and a problem specific to certain individual files

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your network connection stability throughout the operation, especially for very large transfers
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A network interruption partway through a large copy or move operation is a very common cause of failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: If specific files consistently fail, check whether they might currently be open or locked by another user or process
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Locked files cannot be successfully copied or moved until they are properly closed by whoever or whatever currently has them open

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available storage space at the destination, especially for very large copy operations
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Running out of space partway through a large operation will cause it to fail once the destination becomes full

troubleshootingSteps.action: For specific files that consistently fail, check if their full file path, including all folder names, might be unusually long, potentially exceeding system path length limits
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Very long, deeply nested file paths can sometimes exceed limits that cause specific files to fail while others in the same batch succeed

troubleshootingSteps.action: For very large batches, consider breaking the operation into smaller batches rather than attempting to copy or move everything at once
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Smaller batches are less likely to be affected by a single interruption and make it easier to identify exactly which specific files, if any, are problematic

troubleshootingSteps.action: If certain files consistently and specifically fail despite these checks, report them to the system administrator, since they may require special handling or indicate an underlying corruption or permissions issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Consistently failing specific files often point to a distinct, isolated issue with those particular items rather than a general operational problem

possibleSolutions: Ensure a stable network connection for large operations
Close files that are locked or in use before retrying
Free up destination storage space before large copy operations
Break very large batches into smaller, more manageable operations
Report consistently failing specific files to the administrator
prevention: Maintain a stable network connection for large file operations
Avoid excessively long, deeply nested folder and file naming structures
Monitor destination storage space before large copy or move operations
Close files properly before they need to be copied or moved by others

problem: Storage quota exceeded or disk is full
description: The user tries to save, upload, or copy a file to a shared location, but the action fails because the destination has reached its maximum allowed storage capacity or an assigned quota limit.
symptoms: Error message specifically mentioning insufficient disk space or quota exceeded
New files cannot be created or saved, while existing files remain accessible
The available space shown for the drive or folder is at or very near zero
Problem may affect only the user's specific quota while overall server space is fine
possibleCauses: The overall shared drive or server has genuinely run out of available physical storage space
The user has an individually assigned storage quota that has been reached
A specific folder has its own size limit that has been reached, separate from overall server space
Old or unnecessary files have accumulated over time, consuming available space
diagnosticQuestions: Does the error specifically mention a personal quota, or does it seem to reference the overall drive being full?
Do you know if you have an individually assigned storage quota for this location?
Are other users also experiencing storage-related errors on this same share?
Have you recently added a large amount of new data to this location?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Read the exact error message to determine if it references a personal quota specifically, or the destination being full in a more general sense
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This distinguishes between an individual quota limit and an overall storage capacity issue, which require different approaches to resolve

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are also experiencing storage-related errors on this same shared location
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is your individual quota specifically, or a broader problem with the overall available storage

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review your own files within this location for anything old, unnecessary, or duplicated that could be deleted or archived to free up space
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is often the most direct way to address a personal quota issue without needing to wait for an administrator

troubleshootingSteps.action: Delete or move unnecessary files to a different, more appropriate location, such as a personal archive or a location with less strict quota limits
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This frees up space within the quota-limited location while still preserving the files themselves elsewhere

troubleshootingSteps.action: If you believe your current quota is genuinely insufficient for legitimate business needs, contact the system administrator to discuss a possible quota increase
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This addresses situations where the underlying need for more space is legitimate and simply requires an appropriately adjusted limit

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the issue appears to be overall server storage capacity rather than an individual quota, report this to the administrator, since this typically requires expanding server storage or a broader cleanup effort
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An overall capacity issue is a larger infrastructure concern that needs administrator-level action to properly resolve

troubleshootingSteps.action: As a proactive habit, periodically review and clean up unnecessary files in frequently used shared locations
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps prevent storage issues from recurring and keeps shared locations more organized overall

possibleSolutions: Delete or archive unnecessary personal files to free up quota space
Move files to a different location with more available space
Request a quota increase from the administrator if genuinely needed
Report an overall server capacity issue to the administrator
prevention: Periodically review and clean up unnecessary files
Understand your assigned storage quota and monitor usage against it
Request appropriate quota levels proactively for known large storage needs
Archive completed or older project files to reduce active storage usage

problem: Shared folder opens slowly or File Explorer freezes while browsing it
description: The user tries to open a specific shared folder, and either it takes an unusually long time to display its contents, or File Explorer itself becomes unresponsive while attempting to load it.
symptoms: Noticeable delay between clicking the folder and its contents appearing
File Explorer shows 'Not Responding' specifically while opening this folder
The folder eventually loads after a long wait, or never completes
Other, smaller folders on the same share open normally and quickly
possibleCauses: The folder contains an extremely large number of files or subfolders
Network latency or a slow connection is delaying the folder listing from loading
Antivirus software is scanning each file as the folder listing loads
File Explorer is trying to generate thumbnails for a large number of image or video files
The file server itself is under heavy load, slowing down its response to browsing requests
diagnosticQuestions: Roughly how many files or subfolders are contained in this specific folder?
Does this happen with all folders on this share, or specifically this one large folder?
Are other users experiencing similar slowness opening this same folder?
Does the folder contain many images or videos that might be generating thumbnails?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check approximately how many files and subfolders exist within this specific folder
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An extremely large number of items is one of the most common and straightforward reasons a specific folder takes a long time to open compared to others

troubleshootingSteps.action: Switch the folder's view to a simpler list view rather than large icons or thumbnails, if not already using one
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Generating thumbnail previews, especially for many images or videos, adds significant processing time that a simple list view avoids

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they experience similar slowness opening this same specific folder
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is specific to your computer and connection, or reflects a genuine characteristic of this particular folder or the server's current load

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your own network connection stability and speed, since a slow connection will make browsing any large folder feel more sluggish
troubleshootingSteps.reason: General network performance directly affects how quickly a large folder listing can be transferred and displayed

troubleshootingSteps.action: If antivirus software is configured to scan network locations in real time, check if this might be contributing to the delay when browsing this particular folder
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Real-time scanning of many files as they are listed can add significant overhead, especially for folders with a large number of items

troubleshootingSteps.action: If this specific folder has grown to contain an excessive number of files over time, consider working with the folder owner to reorganize its contents into logical subfolders
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Breaking up an extremely large flat folder structure into smaller, better-organized subfolders significantly improves browsing performance

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the slowness seems related to overall server performance rather than this specific folder's size, report the pattern to the system administrator
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps distinguish a folder-specific organizational issue from a broader server performance problem that needs administrator attention

possibleSolutions: Switch to a simple list view instead of thumbnails
Reorganize an excessively large folder into logical subfolders
Adjust antivirus real-time scanning settings for network locations if contributing to delays
Report broader server performance issues to the administrator
prevention: Proactively organize large folders into logical subfolders as they grow
Use list view rather than thumbnail view for folders with many files
Periodically review and archive old files from frequently browsed large folders

problem: Offline files are not synchronizing correctly
description: The user relies on Windows Offline Files or a similar feature to work with cached copies of shared folder content while disconnected, but recent changes are not properly syncing back to the server, or updates from the server are not appearing locally.
symptoms: Changes made while offline do not appear on the server once reconnected
Files on the server are not reflected in the local offline cache
Sync Center shows errors or a stalled sync status
Files may show as 'Always Available Offline' but content appears outdated
possibleCauses: The computer has not successfully reconnected to the network since changes were made offline
A sync conflict occurred and requires manual resolution before syncing can continue
Offline Files caching is not properly configured or was recently disabled
The sync process is stuck or encountered an error that needs to be manually cleared
Insufficient local disk space for the offline cache to properly store recent changes
diagnosticQuestions: Has your computer successfully reconnected to the company network since you made your offline changes?
Does Sync Center show any specific errors or conflicts needing attention?
Do you know if Offline Files is properly enabled and configured for this specific folder?
How much free disk space is available for the local offline cache?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the computer is properly connected to the network, either directly in the office or through a stable VPN connection
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Offline Files can only sync changes back to the server once a proper network connection to it is established

troubleshootingSteps.action: Open Sync Center and check for any specific error messages or conflicts that might be blocking the sync process
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Sync Center typically provides specific details about exactly what is preventing a successful synchronization

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a sync conflict is shown, review it and manually choose which version, local or server, should be kept, or merge changes as appropriate
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Sync conflicts require explicit user decision before the sync process can continue past that specific conflicting item

troubleshootingSteps.action: Manually trigger a sync through Sync Center rather than waiting for an automatic sync to occur
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides an immediate, direct attempt to synchronize and can reveal errors more quickly than waiting for a scheduled sync

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available local disk space, since insufficient space can prevent the offline cache from properly storing and syncing changes
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The offline files cache requires adequate local storage space to function correctly, and a nearly full drive can cause sync failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the specific folder is still properly configured to be 'Always Available Offline', since this setting may have been changed or reset
troubleshootingSteps.reason: If offline availability was disabled for this folder, changes would not be properly cached and synced as expected

troubleshootingSteps.action: If sync issues persist despite these steps, contact the IT department, since Offline Files configuration is sometimes managed centrally through Group Policy and may need administrator review
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Persistent sync issues may point to a deeper configuration problem that requires administrator-level tools to properly diagnose

possibleSolutions: Ensure a proper network or VPN connection before expecting sync to complete
Manually resolve sync conflicts shown in Sync Center
Manually trigger a sync rather than waiting for an automatic one
Free up local disk space for the offline cache
Contact IT if centrally managed Offline Files settings may need review
prevention: Regularly connect to the network to allow timely synchronization
Resolve sync conflicts promptly when they occur
Maintain adequate free local disk space for the offline cache
Avoid extended periods of offline work without reconnecting

problem: Antivirus software is blocking access to a shared folder
description: The user tries to access or work with files in a shared folder, but the antivirus software installed on their computer interferes, either blocking access entirely or significantly slowing down every file operation.
symptoms: A notification from the antivirus software appears when trying to access the share
File operations within the shared folder are unusually slow specifically for this location
Certain files are quarantined or blocked without a clear reason
Disabling the antivirus temporarily resolves the issue
possibleCauses: The antivirus software's real-time scanning is configured to closely scan all network locations, causing slowdowns
A specific file was falsely flagged as a threat by the antivirus
The antivirus has a specific rule blocking network share access as a security precaution
A recent antivirus definition update introduced a false positive affecting common file types
diagnosticQuestions: Do you see a specific notification or alert from your antivirus software when this happens?
Does disabling the antivirus temporarily, just for testing, resolve the issue?
Is this affecting all files in the share, or a specific one that might have been flagged?
Did this start after a recent antivirus update or definition change?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for any specific notification or quarantine alert from the antivirus software related to this shared folder or a specific file within it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides direct evidence and specific detail about what the antivirus software is doing and why

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a specific file was flagged, review the antivirus quarantine to confirm whether it appears to be a legitimate threat or a likely false positive
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine the appropriate next step, whether restoring a mistakenly flagged file or properly addressing a genuine security concern

troubleshootingSteps.action: If confident a specific file is a false positive, restore it from quarantine and consider adding a specific exception for it if your antivirus software supports this
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This resolves the immediate access issue while properly documenting the exception for future reference

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the antivirus software's settings for real-time scanning specifically applied to network locations, and consider whether these settings are appropriately balanced for performance and security
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Overly aggressive real-time scanning of network locations can cause significant slowdowns without necessarily providing proportional security benefit, especially for already-trusted internal file servers

troubleshootingSteps.action: If considering adjusting antivirus settings for a trusted internal share, consult with the IT security team before making changes, since this involves an important security trade-off
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Antivirus settings changes should be made thoughtfully and ideally with proper authorization, especially in a business environment

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the antivirus update that introduced the issue is recent, check if the vendor has released a corrected update addressing the false positive
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reputable antivirus vendors typically quickly correct widely reported false positive issues in subsequent updates

troubleshootingSteps.action: Report persistent or unusual antivirus interference with shared folder access to the IT security team, providing specific details about affected files and the exact behavior observed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the issue is properly documented and addressed at an appropriate level, especially if it affects multiple users

possibleSolutions: Restore a mistakenly quarantined file identified as a false positive
Add an appropriate antivirus exception for a confirmed false positive, in consultation with IT security
Adjust real-time scanning settings for trusted network locations with proper security team involvement
Wait for or apply a corrected antivirus definition update addressing a known false positive
prevention: Keep antivirus software updated to benefit from corrected definitions
Coordinate with IT security before making antivirus exception changes
Report false positives to the antivirus vendor and internal IT team promptly

problem: Backup of a shared folder fails
description: A scheduled or manually initiated backup job responsible for backing up a shared folder does not complete successfully, potentially leaving the folder's data unprotected against loss.
symptoms: Backup job log shows a failure or error status
Backup completes but with warnings about specific files being skipped
The scheduled backup does not appear to have run at all
Restore testing reveals gaps in expected backed-up data
possibleCauses: The backup software lacks sufficient permissions to access all files in the shared folder
Specific files were locked or in use at the exact moment the backup attempted to read them
Insufficient storage space at the backup destination
A network interruption occurred during the backup process
The backup job itself is misconfigured or was accidentally disabled
diagnosticQuestions: Does the backup log provide any specific error message or reason for the failure?
Has this backup job worked successfully before, or is this a new or recently changed job?
Do you know if certain files are frequently open or in use during the scheduled backup time?
Is there sufficient free space at the backup destination?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the backup job's log file or report for the specific error message or reason given for the failure
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Backup software typically provides detailed logs that point directly to the specific cause of a failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the backup software's service account has sufficient read permissions across the entire shared folder structure being backed up
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient permissions for the backup process itself is a common cause of failures or incomplete backups, especially after permission changes on the source folder

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if specific files are commonly open or in use by users at the exact time the backup is scheduled to run
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Files locked by active use can sometimes be skipped or cause errors during a backup attempt, depending on how the backup software handles open files

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider adjusting the backup schedule to a time when the shared folder is less likely to be actively in use, such as late at night
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This reduces the likelihood of file lock conflicts interfering with a complete, successful backup

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available storage space at the backup destination to confirm it has not run out of room to store the backup data
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient destination storage will cause a backup job to fail partway through or not start at all

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the network connection between the source shared folder and the backup destination remained stable throughout the scheduled backup window
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A network interruption during a long-running backup process is a common cause of failure, especially for large data sets

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the backup job configuration itself may have been accidentally changed or disabled, review its settings and schedule carefully, correcting any issues found
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly addresses a misconfiguration that could explain the backup simply not running as expected or failing consistently

troubleshootingSteps.action: This is typically an administrator-level task; if you are not the backup administrator, report the failure with all gathered details to the person or team responsible for backups
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Backup infrastructure is usually managed centrally, and detailed reporting helps the responsible administrator quickly diagnose and resolve the issue

possibleSolutions: Correct insufficient backup service account permissions
Adjust the backup schedule to avoid peak file usage times
Free up storage space at the backup destination
Ensure stable network connectivity during the backup window
Correct a misconfigured or accidentally disabled backup job
prevention: Regularly review backup logs for early signs of recurring issues
Schedule backups during low-usage periods when possible
Monitor backup destination storage capacity proactively
Periodically test restores to confirm backup integrity

problem: Error 0x80070035 - The network path was not found
description: Windows displays the specific error code 0x80070035 along with the message 'The network path was not found' when attempting to access a network share, printer, or other network resource.
symptoms: Error dialog specifically showing code 0x80070035
Message states 'The network path was not found'
Occurs when trying to access a specific share by name or IP
May affect one specific resource while others work normally
possibleCauses: The target computer's name cannot be resolved on the network
The target computer is off, disconnected, or on a different, unreachable network segment
File and printer sharing is disabled on the target computer
A firewall is blocking the necessary network discovery or file sharing protocols
An incorrect path was typed, containing a typo
diagnosticQuestions: Does the exact same error happen when using the target computer's IP address instead of its name?
Is the target computer definitely powered on and connected to the network?
Have you successfully connected to this same resource before?
Are you on the same local network as the target computer, or connecting from elsewhere?

commands.purpose: Test whether the computer name resolves and responds
commands.expectedResult: Replies received, confirming the name resolves and the computer is reachable
commands.abnormalResult: 'Ping request could not find host', confirming a name resolution or reachability failure matching this error

troubleshootingSteps.action: Double-check the exact spelling of the network path being used for any typos
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A simple typo is one of the most common and easily overlooked causes of this specific error

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the target computer by name to determine if the name resolves and the computer responds
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly tests the two most common underlying causes: name resolution failure and the target being unreachable

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the name does not resolve or respond, try using the target's IP address directly instead

Adopt a co-authoring compatible application or file format for frequently shared documents
Implement file checkout or locking practices for documents prone to conflicts

Encourage team communication before extended offline editing of shared files
