description: A user attempts to restore an earlier version of a file or folder using the Previous Versions feature, but no earlier versions are listed, or the feature appears entirely unavailable.
symptoms: The Previous Versions tab shows no available versions for the file or folder
The Previous Versions tab or option is missing entirely
Earlier versions were available before but are no longer shown
The feature works for some files or folders but not others
possibleCauses: Shadow Copy is not enabled on the server volume hosting this share
Shadow Copy is enabled but no snapshots have been taken recently enough to include this file
The user lacks sufficient permissions to view previous versions
The specific file or folder was created after the last snapshot was taken
diagnosticQuestions: Have Previous Versions worked for other files on this same share before?
Roughly when was the file last known to have an earlier recoverable version?
Do you have standard read access to the file, separate from the Previous Versions feature specifically?
Is this issue specific to one file or does it affect the entire share?

commands.purpose: List existing shadow copy snapshots on the server, when run directly on the server with appropriate rights
commands.expectedResult: Shows a list of recent shadow copy snapshots available for the relevant volume
commands.abnormalResult: Shows no snapshots, or none recent enough, indicating Shadow Copy is not configured or not running as expected

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether Previous Versions has worked successfully for other files on this same share before
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This establishes whether Shadow Copy is generally functional on this server or the feature may not be enabled at all

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check whether the issue is specific to one file or folder versus affecting the entire share
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A single affected item points toward that item being newer than the last snapshot, while a share-wide issue suggests Shadow Copy itself is misconfigured

troubleshootingSteps.action: This issue requires server-side verification of Shadow Copy configuration and snapshot schedule
troubleshootingSteps.reason: End users cannot verify or configure Shadow Copy settings directly on the server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Have the administrator confirm Shadow Copy is enabled on the relevant volume and check the snapshot schedule
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Shadow Copy must be explicitly enabled and scheduled on the server for Previous Versions to have any data to show

troubleshootingSteps.action: If Shadow Copy is disabled or misconfigured, have the administrator enable it and adjust the snapshot schedule appropriately
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This restores the ability to recover previous versions going forward, though it cannot recover versions from before it is enabled

possibleSolutions: Have the administrator enable Shadow Copy on the relevant server volume if it is currently disabled
Adjust the Shadow Copy snapshot schedule to run more frequently going forward
Restore the needed file version from a separate backup system if Shadow Copy does not have it
Confirm and correct user permissions if access to Previous Versions is being blocked
prevention: Enable Shadow Copy on all volumes hosting important shared folders
Schedule Shadow Copy snapshots at a frequency appropriate to how often files change
Maintain a separate, independent backup system as a complement to Shadow Copy

Insufficient permissions for the backup service account on certain files or folders
Specific files were open or locked during the backup window, causing them to be skipped
The backup destination ran out of available storage space

diagnosticQuestions: What specific error or status does the backup job log show?
Does the failure affect the entire backup job or only specific files or folders?
Has this backup job been failing consistently, or did it just start failing recently?

commands.purpose: Verify the backup service account has appropriate read permissions on the source folder
commands.expectedResult: Shows the backup service account with sufficient read access to all necessary files
commands.abnormalResult: Shows the backup service account lacking access to certain files or subfolders, explaining partial backup failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the specific error message or status code from the backup job log
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The exact error provides the clearest indication of whether the cause is connectivity, permissions, storage, or something else

troubleshootingSteps.action: Determine whether the entire backup job failed or only specific files were skipped
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A full job failure points toward connectivity or destination issues, while selective failures point toward permissions or file locks

troubleshootingSteps.action: Verify that the backup service account has appropriate permissions across the entire folder structure
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient permissions on even a subset of files is a common and specific cause of partial backup failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the backup destination has sufficient available storage space
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A full backup destination will cause jobs to fail partway through or not start at all

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check whether the backup job's scheduled time window is sufficient for the current volume of data
troubleshootingSteps.reason: As data grows, backup jobs can begin exceeding their allotted time and get terminated before completing

troubleshootingSteps.action: Escalate to IT or the backup administrator with the specific findings for correction of the underlying configuration
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Resolving backup job configuration issues typically requires administrative access to the backup software

possibleSolutions: Correct backup service account permissions across the affected folder structure
Free up space on the backup destination storage
Extend the backup job's time window to accommodate current data volume
Investigate and resolve network connectivity issues occurring during the backup window
prevention: Regularly monitor backup job logs for early warning signs of failure
Proactively adjust backup windows and destination capacity as data grows
Test backup restores periodically to confirm the backup process is genuinely working end to end

troubleshootingSteps.action: If content-based search specifically fails while name-based search works, check whether the file types involved support content indexing

Periodically verify the Windows Search service is running and healthy
Communicate to users which shared folders support content search versus name-only search

description: The user double-clicks or launches a software program, but it does not open at all, showing no window, no error, and no visible sign of starting.

Insufficient system resources are preventing the program from starting

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Task Manager for any existing process related to this program and end it if found stuck

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available free disk space and system memory, freeing up resources if either is very low

possibleSolutions: End a stuck background process and try again
Run the program as administrator
Temporarily disable antivirus software to test
Free up disk space and memory
Repair or reinstall the application

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for and install any pending updates for the program

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use the program's repair option through Control Panel, or completely uninstall and reinstall it

Disable a problematic add-in using Safe Mode

Repair or completely reinstall the application

Back up configuration settings periodically for critical software

description: While the user is actively working within a software program, it stops responding to any clicks or keyboard input, with the window frozen and often labeled 'Not Responding' in its title bar.

Clicking anywhere within the program has no effect
The screen may appear greyed out or frozen in place

possibleCauses: A large or complex operation taking longer than expected
Insufficient system memory for the current task
A stuck background process related to the program
A network delay if the program is waiting on a server response
A bug in the software triggered by a specific action
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen during a specific action, such as saving, loading, or printing?
How long does the unresponsive state typically last?
Have you noticed this happen with a particular file or dataset?
Is the computer generally low on available memory?

commands.purpose: Check the program's CPU and memory usage while it appears frozen, to determine if it is genuinely stuck or working intensively

commands.abnormalResult: The program remains at 0% CPU usage for an extended period with no progress, indicating a genuine freeze

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Task Manager to see if the program is using high CPU, suggesting it is still actively processing rather than truly frozen
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps decide whether to keep waiting for a legitimate operation to finish, or consider it a genuine freeze

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a large operation, such as opening a big file or generating a report, was just triggered, allow extra time for it to complete
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some legitimate operations can genuinely take a long time and only appear frozen while working correctly in the background

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the program does recover, save your work immediately and consider restarting the program for a fresh session
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This protects recent work and reduces the chance the same freeze will happen again during the current session

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the freeze consistently happens with a specific file or dataset, note this pattern and avoid it temporarily while investigating further
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This isolates the cause to a specific file rather than the software in general, helping direct further troubleshooting

troubleshootingSteps.action: Close other unnecessary programs to free up system memory
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient available memory is a common contributor to programs becoming unresponsive, especially during memory-intensive tasks

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the program does not recover after a reasonable wait, end the task through Task Manager and reopen the program
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This allows you to resume work in a fresh session when the original one cannot be recovered

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for and install any pending software updates, since known freezing bugs are often addressed in newer releases
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Keeping software current resolves many known stability issues that cause unresponsiveness

possibleSolutions: Wait for a large legitimate operation to complete
Restart the program for a fresh session after recovery
Free up system memory by closing other programs
End the unresponsive task and reopen the program
Install pending software updates
prevention: Save work frequently while using the software
Keep the software updated to its latest version
Avoid running too many memory-intensive programs at once

description: During normal use, well after successfully opening, the software suddenly stops responding to input, with the freeze happening mid-task rather than at startup, sometimes recovering after a wait and sometimes requiring a forced restart.

A specific feature or function within the software triggering a bug
Background processes competing for system resources
An outdated graphics or other driver affecting the software's stability
A large or growing file the software is working with
diagnosticQuestions: Does the freeze happen randomly, or during a specific repeated action?
Does this happen more often the longer the program has been open?
Have you noticed the program's memory usage climbing steadily in Task Manager?
Has this become more frequent recently, or has it always happened occasionally?

commands.purpose: Monitor the program's memory usage over time to check for a steadily increasing pattern suggesting a memory leak

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note whether the freeze happens randomly, or specifically after performing a certain repeated action within the software
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A specific, repeatable trigger points toward a bug in that particular feature, while a freeze that worsens over time points toward a memory leak

troubleshootingSteps.action: Monitor the program's memory usage in Task Manager over an extended working session to check for a steadily increasing pattern
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A memory leak is confirmed by memory usage that continuously climbs without releasing, eventually leading to a freeze once resources are exhausted

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a memory leak is suspected, periodically save your work and restart the program during long sessions rather than leaving it open indefinitely
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Restarting the program releases leaked memory, providing a practical workaround while a permanent fix is pursued

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for and install any pending updates for the software, since memory leaks and specific bugs are commonly addressed in updates
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Software vendors frequently release updates that fix known memory leak and stability issues

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update your graphics driver and other relevant drivers, since outdated drivers can contribute to instability in software that relies on them for rendering
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Driver-related instability is a common but often overlooked contributor to software freezing during use

troubleshootingSteps.action: Close unnecessary background programs to reduce competition for system resources
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This frees up memory and processing power, reducing the likelihood of a resource-related freeze

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the freeze is tied to a specific large or growing file, consider whether that file needs to be optimized, split, or cleaned up
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An excessively large or complex file can push the software beyond its comfortable performance limits, leading to freezing

troubleshootingSteps.action: Report the specific pattern, including the trigger and frequency, to the software vendor's support team if the issue continues despite updates
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Detailed information helps the vendor diagnose and address the underlying bug in a future release

possibleSolutions: Periodically restart the program during long sessions to release leaked memory
Install pending software updates addressing known stability issues
Update graphics and other relevant drivers
Close unnecessary background programs to free resources
Optimize or reduce the size of an overly large working file
prevention: Save work frequently and restart the program periodically during long sessions
Keep the software and drivers updated
Avoid working with excessively large files without periodic cleanup

Completely remove any previous version before reinstalling
Install missing prerequisite components first

Fully uninstall old software versions before installing updates
Check prerequisites before beginning an installation

The software version remains unchanged after the update attempt
The software may become unstable or fail to open after a failed update
The update download may stall or fail to complete

Insufficient disk space for the update to complete
A conflict with the currently installed version
The update server is temporarily unavailable
Antivirus software blocking parts of the update process

How much free disk space is currently available?
Does the software still function normally at its current, older version?
What exact error message, if any, appears during the failed update?

troubleshootingSteps.reason: This establishes whether there is an immediate functional problem or just an update that has not yet succeeded

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your internet connection stability, then retry the update

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check available disk space and free up space if it is low

troubleshootingSteps.action: Close the software completely before attempting the update, if it was left running

troubleshootingSteps.action: Temporarily disable antivirus software and attempt the update again

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the update continues to fail, download the latest full installer directly from the vendor's website rather than relying on the in-app update mechanism
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A full reinstallation using the latest complete installer often succeeds where an incremental update mechanism fails

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the vendor's status page or support resources for any known issues with the specific update or update servers
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Sometimes update failures are caused by a temporary problem on the vendor's end rather than anything on the user's computer

possibleSolutions: Ensure a stable internet connection and retry
Free up disk space before attempting the update
Close the software completely before updating
Download and run the latest full installer directly from the vendor
Check for known vendor-side update issues

Keep adequate free disk space available
Close the software before applying updates

description: The user tries to remove a piece of software using the normal uninstall process, but the uninstallation fails, hangs, or the program remains listed as installed even after the process appears to complete.

The uninstall process hangs indefinitely
The program still appears in the installed programs list after uninstalling
Program files or folders remain on the disk after uninstallation
possibleCauses: A file needed for uninstallation is missing or corrupted
The program or a related process is currently running and locking files
Insufficient administrator permissions to complete the removal
The uninstaller itself has a bug or was not properly included with the installation
Leftover registry entries from a previous incomplete removal
diagnosticQuestions: What exact error message, if any, appears during the failed uninstallation?
Is the program or any related background process currently running?
Do you have administrator rights on this computer?
Has this program been partially uninstalled or reinstalled before?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Close the program completely, along with any related background processes, before attempting to uninstall
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A running program or its background processes can lock files needed for a clean uninstallation

troubleshootingSteps.action: Right-click the uninstaller and select 'Run as administrator' if not already doing so

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the computer and immediately attempt the uninstallation again before opening any other programs
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures no related processes are running and no files are locked when the uninstall attempt begins

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use the official vendor's dedicated removal tool, if one is provided, since many software vendors offer a specific tool designed to fully remove stubborn installations
troubleshootingSteps.reason: These specialized tools are designed to handle exactly this type of situation more thoroughly than the standard uninstaller

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the program still appears in the installed programs list after an apparently successful uninstall, use the Windows built-in 'Fix problems that block programs from being installed or removed' troubleshooter
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This official Microsoft tool is specifically designed to clean up stuck or incomplete program listings that a normal uninstall could not fully resolve

troubleshootingSteps.action: Manually delete any remaining program folders from Program Files after the uninstaller has run, if files are confirmed to be leftover
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This removes any lingering files that the uninstaller failed to clean up completely

troubleshootingSteps.action: As a more advanced step, and with appropriate caution, remove any obviously related leftover registry entries, or seek assistance if not comfortable doing this yourself
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Leftover registry entries can sometimes interfere with future reinstallation attempts, though registry editing carries some risk if done incorrectly

possibleSolutions: Close the program and related processes before uninstalling
Run the uninstaller as administrator
Use the vendor's official dedicated removal tool
Use the Windows program install/uninstall troubleshooter
Manually remove leftover files after the uninstaller runs
prevention: Always close a program completely before attempting to uninstall it
Use official vendor removal tools when available
Avoid manually deleting program files instead of using the proper uninstaller

problem: Invalid username or password when logging into software
description: The user enters their credentials to log in to a software application, but receives a specific error stating the username or password is invalid, even though they believe their credentials are correct.
symptoms: Specific error message stating 'Invalid username or password'
The error appears immediately after submitting the login form
Message does not specify which part is incorrect
May happen consistently or only occasionally
possibleCauses: The username or password was typed incorrectly, including Caps Lock being on
The password was recently changed and the old one is being used
The account uses a different username format than what is being entered
The account does not exist or was never properly set up in this system
A trailing space or hidden character was accidentally included
diagnosticQuestions: Are you certain of the exact username format expected, such as email versus a short username?
Was your password changed recently, either by you or an administrator?
Is Caps Lock currently on?
Are you copying and pasting the password, or typing it manually?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if Caps Lock or Num Lock is currently on before retyping the credentials
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An accidentally enabled Caps Lock is one of the most common reasons correct credentials appear to be rejected

troubleshootingSteps.action: Carefully retype both the username and password directly, rather than relying on autofill
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Browser or system autofill can sometimes store an outdated or incorrect version of credentials

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the correct username format expected by this specific software, such as a full email versus a short account name
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Different applications expect different username formats, and using the wrong format will always result in this error

troubleshootingSteps.action: If copying and pasting the password, first paste it into a plain text field to check for accidental extra spaces or hidden characters
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Copying from certain sources can accidentally include invisible characters that cause the password to not match

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether the password was recently changed, and ensure you are using the most current version
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Using an old, previously valid password after a change is a common and simple explanation for this error

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use the software's official password reset option if available, to set a fresh, known password
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides a definitive way to rule out any uncertainty about the current correct password

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the reset process indicates no account exists for the given username, contact the system administrator to confirm the account was properly created and is active
troubleshootingSteps.reason: In some cases, the underlying account itself may not exist or was never fully set up, requiring administrator involvement

possibleSolutions: Turn off Caps Lock and retype credentials carefully
Confirm and use the correct username format
Remove hidden characters when pasting a password
Use the most recently updated password
Use the official password reset option
prevention: Use a password manager to store credentials accurately
Update saved passwords promptly after any change
Be aware of the specific username format required by each application

description: The user tries to log in to a software application, but the login process fails generally, without a highly specific error, or gets stuck without completing successfully.
symptoms: Login screen rejects credentials or shows a generic error
The login button appears to do nothing when clicked
The login page reloads back to itself after submitting
The login process gets stuck loading indefinitely
possibleCauses: Incorrect username or password
The application's login server is down or unreachable
The user's account has been locked or disabled
A network connectivity problem preventing the login request from completing
A software bug or corrupted local cache affecting the login process
diagnosticQuestions: What exact message or behavior happens when you try to log in?
Have you logged in successfully before, or is this your first attempt?
Are other users able to log in right now?
Are you connected to the correct network or VPN required for this software?

commands.purpose: Check if the computer can reach the server the software authenticates against
commands.expectedResult: Replies received from the server
commands.abnormalResult: Request timed out, meaning the server cannot be reached, which would prevent login

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the exact username and password are being entered correctly, checking for Caps Lock and typing mistakes
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Simple credential entry errors are the most common cause of login failures and should be ruled out first

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are able to log in to the same application right now
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This quickly determines if the problem is isolated to your account or computer, or affects the application more broadly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the computer has a working network connection, connected to any required VPN if the software is only accessible internally
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Without the correct network path, the login request may never actually reach the authentication server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Clear the software's local cache or temporary files, if this option is available within its settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A corrupted local cache can sometimes interfere with the login process even when credentials are entered correctly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the software completely, or restart the computer, then attempt to log in again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This clears any temporary session state issues that could be interfering with a successful login

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the problem affects multiple users, check the software vendor's status page or contact the system administrator about a possible outage
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A widespread login failure often points to a server-side outage rather than an individual account or computer problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: If only this one user is affected, contact the system administrator to check if the account has been locked, disabled, or needs a password reset
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Account-specific restrictions require administrator access to review and correct

possibleSolutions: Correct mistyped username or password
Reconnect to the required network or VPN
Clear the software's local cache
Restart the software or computer
Have the administrator unlock or reset the affected account
prevention: Use a password manager to avoid credential entry mistakes
Keep track of VPN requirements for internal software
Report suspected outages promptly

description: The user tries to log in to a software application, but instead of a normal password prompt or error, receives a message specifically indicating the account has been locked, usually after several failed login attempts.
symptoms: Message specifically stating the account is locked
Login is blocked entirely, even with the correct password
Message may mention a lockout duration or instructions to contact an administrator
May follow a series of recent failed login attempts
possibleCauses: Too many incorrect password attempts triggered an automatic security lockout
An administrator manually locked the account for security or policy reasons
Suspicious login activity was detected, triggering an automatic protective lockout
The account was locked as part of an offboarding or role change process
diagnosticQuestions: Do you recall making several incorrect password attempts recently?
Does the lockout message mention a specific wait time before automatic unlock?
Have you contacted your IT department about this account recently for any other reason?
Is there any chance someone else may have attempted to log in to your account unsuccessfully?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Read the lockout message carefully to see if it specifies an automatic unlock time or specific instructions
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many lockout policies are temporary and will resolve automatically after a set waiting period, which the message may clearly state

troubleshootingSteps.action: If an automatic unlock time is mentioned, wait for that period to pass before attempting to log in again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Attempting to log in repeatedly during an active lockout period can sometimes extend the lockout duration further

troubleshootingSteps.action: Avoid making further login attempts while investigating the cause, since additional failed attempts can worsen the situation
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Continuing to guess at the password or retry repeatedly can trigger longer or more severe lockout periods on some systems

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the system administrator or IT help desk to confirm the reason for the lockout and request it be lifted if needed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Administrators can typically see the specific reason for a lockout and can manually unlock the account if appropriate

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the lockout was triggered by forgetting the correct password, use this opportunity to also reset the password through the official process once unlocked
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This prevents a repeat lockout from continuing to use an uncertain or forgotten password

troubleshootingSteps.action: If suspicious login activity is suspected as the cause, inform the IT security team so they can investigate whether the account may have been targeted
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A security-related lockout may indicate an attempted unauthorized access, which should be properly investigated rather than simply unlocked and ignored

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once access is restored, confirm normal login works correctly with the current password
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This verifies the lockout has been fully resolved and access is genuinely restored

possibleSolutions: Wait for an automatic lockout period to expire
Contact the administrator to manually unlock the account
Reset the password after unlocking if it was the original cause
Report suspected suspicious activity to the IT security team
prevention: Use a password manager to avoid repeated incorrect password attempts
Report forgotten passwords early rather than repeatedly guessing
Enable multi-factor authentication where available

description: The user tries to access a specific area, feature, or record within the software, but is met with an error stating access is denied, preventing them from proceeding despite being logged in successfully.
symptoms: Error message stating 'Access denied' or 'You do not have permission'
Certain menu options or buttons are missing or greyed out
Access works for some areas of the software but not others
Problem may follow a role change or new task assignment
possibleCauses: The user's account role does not have the required permissions for this specific area or action
A recent change to the user's role or group membership reduced their access
The specific record or area has additional restrictions beyond general application access
The user is trying to access a feature not licensed or enabled for their account type
diagnosticQuestions: What specific area, feature, or record were you trying to access when this error appeared?
Have you had successful access to this same area before, or is this your first attempt?
Do you know if your role or job responsibilities have changed recently?
Are other users with a similar role able to access this same area successfully?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact area, feature, or record you were trying to access, along with the exact error message
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This specific detail is essential for the administrator to properly review and correct the relevant permissions

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether you have successfully accessed this same area before, or if this is a new task or responsibility
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps distinguish between a genuine, unexpected loss of previously working access, versus a new access requirement that has simply never been granted

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with colleagues in a similar role to see if they can access this same area successfully
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is specific to your individual account, or reflects a broader role-based access configuration that may need updating

troubleshootingSteps.action: Log out and log back in to the application, since some permission changes require a fresh session to take full effect
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Newly granted permissions sometimes do not apply to an already active session until it is refreshed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the system administrator or your manager to request the appropriate access, providing the specific area or feature needed and the business reason
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly addresses the root cause by ensuring the correct permissions are properly granted through the appropriate approval process

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once updated access is confirmed, log out and log back in again, then verify the previously denied area is now accessible
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This confirms the access change has been fully and correctly applied

possibleSolutions: Log out and log back in after a permissions change
Request appropriate access from the administrator or manager with business justification
Confirm the correct role-based permissions with colleagues in similar positions
Report an unexpected loss of previously working access to the administrator
prevention: Request necessary access proactively when taking on new responsibilities
Understand your role's expected access scope within the application
Report unexpected access changes to the administrator promptly

problem: Permission denied for a specific action within the software
description: The user can access a general area of the software, but when trying to perform a specific action, such as editing, deleting, or approving, they receive an error stating they do not have permission for that particular action.
symptoms: Error message such as 'Permission denied' when attempting a specific action
Can view content but cannot edit, delete, or approve it
Certain action buttons are greyed out or missing
Permission works for some records but not others of the same type
possibleCauses: The user's role allows viewing but not the specific action being attempted, such as editing or approving
The specific record has additional ownership or approval-level restrictions
A workflow or approval process requires a different, more senior role to perform this action
The user's permissions were recently and intentionally scoped down for this type of action
diagnosticQuestions: What specific action were you trying to perform, such as editing, deleting, or approving?
Have you been able to perform this same action successfully before on other records?
Do you know if this specific action is meant to be restricted to certain roles, such as managers or approvers?
Does this happen with all records, or just specific ones?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact action being attempted and the exact wording of the permission denied message
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps distinguish between a general access restriction and one specific to a particular action, such as approval rights

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider whether this specific action is a business process intentionally restricted to certain roles, such as managers or designated approvers
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some actions are deliberately limited by business rule, and understanding this context helps determine if the restriction is actually expected rather than a technical error

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if this happens with all records of this type, or just specific ones, which might indicate an ownership-based restriction
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some systems restrict certain actions only to the original creator or assigned owner of a specific record, rather than applying a blanket restriction

troubleshootingSteps.action: If you believe you should have this permission based on your role or responsibilities, contact your manager or the system administrator to confirm and request the correct access level
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the request goes through the appropriate approval process if the restriction does need to be adjusted for your role

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the action needs to be performed but is correctly restricted to a different role, identify and coordinate with the appropriate person, such as a manager or approver, to complete the action instead
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides a practical way to get the necessary action completed while respecting appropriate business controls

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once any permission change is confirmed and applied, log out and log back in to ensure the update is properly recognized
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the newly granted permission is correctly reflected in your active session

possibleSolutions: Confirm whether the restriction is an intentional business rule
Request an appropriate permission update from the administrator or manager if warranted
Coordinate with the correctly authorized person to complete a restricted action
Log out and back in after any permission change is applied
prevention: Understand which actions are intentionally restricted by role within the software
Request necessary permissions proactively for new responsibilities
Communicate with the administrator about expected access needs for your position

description: The user tries to use a piece of software, but is met with a message stating the license has expired, restricting access to some or all features until the license is renewed.
symptoms: Message specifically stating the license has expired
The software may open in a limited or read-only mode
Certain features are unavailable with a notice about license status
The software may refuse to open entirely, showing only the license message
possibleCauses: The subscription or license term has genuinely reached its end date
A renewal payment failed to process successfully
The license server cannot be reached to verify a currently valid license
An administrator has not yet renewed or reassigned the license
The computer's date and time are set incorrectly, causing a valid license to appear expired
diagnosticQuestions: Do you know when this software's license or subscription was last renewed?
Is your computer's date and time set correctly?
Are other users of the same software experiencing the same expired license message?
Is this software licensed individually to you, or centrally managed by your organization?

commands.purpose: Check the computer's currently set date to rule out an incorrect system clock causing a false expiration
commands.expectedResult: Shows the correct, current date
commands.abnormalResult: Shows an incorrect date, which could cause a valid license to be mistakenly evaluated as expired

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your computer's date and time settings to confirm they are accurate
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect system clock can cause software to mistakenly evaluate a genuinely valid license as expired

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users of the same software to see if they are also experiencing the same expired license message
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if this is an individual license issue, or a broader organizational licensing problem affecting everyone

troubleshootingSteps.action: If this is an individually purchased license, check your account or billing information to confirm whether a renewal payment was processed successfully
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A failed renewal payment is a common and straightforward cause of an unexpectedly expired license

troubleshootingSteps.action: If this is a centrally managed, organization-licensed software, contact your IT department or software administrator to confirm the organization's license status
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Organizational licenses are typically managed centrally, and individual users generally cannot renew or resolve this themselves

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm your computer has an internet connection if the software needs to reach a license verification server
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Without internet access, the software may be unable to verify a genuinely valid license, causing it to appear expired

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a payment or renewal issue is identified, complete the renewal process through the official vendor channel
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly resolves the issue by properly renewing the license, restoring full access to the software

troubleshootingSteps.action: After renewal, restart the software, and if necessary, the computer, to ensure the updated license status is properly recognized
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the software fully reflects the renewed license Instead of continuing to reference cached expired status information

possibleSolutions: Correct an inaccurate system clock
Complete a failed renewal payment through the vendor
Contact IT to renew or reassign an organizational license
Ensure internet connectivity for license verification
Restart the software after renewal to refresh license status
prevention: Keep the computer's date and time accurate
Set reminders for license or subscription renewal dates
Monitor organizational license status proactively as an administrator

description: After installing software, the user tries to activate it using a product key or account credentials, but the activation process fails, leaving the software in a trial, limited, or unactivated state.
symptoms: Error message during the activation attempt
The software remains in trial or limited mode despite entering a valid key
A message states the product key is invalid or already in use
Activation appears to hang without completing
possibleCauses: The product key was entered incorrectly
The product key has already reached its maximum number of allowed activations
No internet connection is available for online activation verification
The activation server is temporarily unavailable
The software was installed using media or a version that does not match the product key
diagnosticQuestions: Have you double-checked the product key for typing mistakes?
Do you have an active internet connection for online activation?
Has this product key been used to activate this software on another computer before?
Does the installed software version match what the product key is intended for?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Carefully re-enter the product key, checking closely for commonly confused characters such as 'O' and '0', or 'I' and '1'
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Simple typing mistakes when entering a long product key are a very common cause of activation failure

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the computer has an active, stable internet connection, since most modern activation processes require online verification
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Without internet access, the activation server cannot be reached to verify and process the product key

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the product key is intended for the specific version and edition of the software you have installed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A product key for a different edition or version will not successfully activate software that does not match it

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the key may have already been used on another computer, check whether it has reached its maximum allowed number of activations
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many product keys are limited to a specific number of simultaneous activations, and exceeding this will cause new activation attempts to fail

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a previous installation using this key is no longer in use, deactivate or transfer the license from that computer if the vendor provides a way to do so
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This frees up an activation slot, allowing the key to be successfully used on the current computer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try activation again after waiting a short period, in case the activation server was temporarily unavailable
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some activation failures are caused by brief server-side issues that resolve on a subsequent attempt

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the software vendor's support team if activation continues to fail despite a correct key and stable internet connection, providing the exact error message received
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The vendor can verify the key's status and assist with activation issues that cannot be resolved through standard troubleshooting

possibleSolutions: Carefully re-enter the product key to correct typing mistakes
Ensure a stable internet connection for online activation
Confirm the key matches the installed software version and edition
Deactivate the key from a previous computer if no longer in use
Contact vendor support if activation continues to fail
prevention: Keep product keys stored securely and accurately recorded
Deactivate licenses from old computers before decommissioning them
Confirm software version compatibility before purchasing a product key

description: The software requires a connection to a server to function fully, but repeatedly fails to establish this connection, displaying an error and preventing server-dependent features from working.
symptoms: Error message such as 'Cannot connect to server' or 'Connection failed'
The software's basic interface may load, but no server-dependent data appears
All server-dependent features are unavailable
May happen for one user or many at the same time
possibleCauses: No active internet or network connection on the user's computer
The software's server is down or restarting
A required VPN connection is not active for internal software
A firewall or network configuration is blocking the connection
Incorrect server address configured in the software's settings
diagnosticQuestions: Are you connected to the correct network or VPN required for this software?
Are other users able to connect to the server right now?
Does your computer have a working internet or network connection overall?
Has this software worked correctly before on this same network connection?

commands.purpose: Test basic network connectivity to the software's server
commands.expectedResult: Replies received from the server, confirming a network path exists
commands.abnormalResult: Request timed out, meaning the server cannot be reached from this network location

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the computer has a working internet or network connection independent of this specific software
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This determines if the problem is specific to reaching this software's server, or a broader network issue affecting everything

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the software requires a VPN connection, confirm the VPN is currently active and stable
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many internal business applications are only reachable through a company VPN, and without it, connection attempts will always fail

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the software's server address to test basic network reachability
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly confirms whether a network path currently exists to the server from this specific computer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are experiencing the same connection failure right now
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This quickly indicates whether the problem is isolated to this one user or represents a broader server outage

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the software, or refresh the connection, to rule out a temporary connection state issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A fresh restart can resolve connection problems caused by a stuck or corrupted session on the client side

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the software's configured server address, if accessible in its settings, to confirm it has not been accidentally changed or is outdated
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect server address will prevent the software from ever finding the correct server, regardless of network health

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the problem affects multiple users, contact the system administrator immediately, since this likely indicates a server outage or network infrastructure issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A widespread connectivity issue requires administrator-level investigation into the server and network infrastructure itself

possibleSolutions: Restore a working internet or network connection
Reconnect the VPN if required for this software
Restart the software or refresh the connection
Correct an incorrect server address in software settings
Report a widespread outage to the system administrator
prevention: Maintain a stable VPN connection when required
Keep server settings correctly configured
Stay informed of scheduled server maintenance windows

description: The user tries to access the software and receives a specific message stating the server is unavailable, distinct from a generic connection failure, suggesting the server itself is not currently operational.
symptoms: Specific error message stating 'Server unavailable' or 'Service unavailable'
May include an HTTP error code such as 503
Problem persists across multiple attempts and refreshes
May affect one specific application or an entire suite of related systems
possibleCauses: The server is undergoing scheduled maintenance
The server has crashed or stopped responding due to an unexpected error
The server is overloaded with too many requests at once
A recent deployment or update to the software caused the server to fail to start correctly
diagnosticQuestions: Does the error include a specific code, such as 503 Service Unavailable?
Have you received any communication about scheduled maintenance for this system?
