Is the recipient's email address definitely correct?
Does this happen with all email attempts, or specific recipients?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact error message shown when the email fails to send
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Specific error details often point directly to whether the issue is a configuration, connectivity, or delivery problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the computer has a working network connection at the time of sending
troubleshootingSteps.reason: The software cannot send email without a working connection to its configured email server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Double-check the recipient's email address for typing mistakes
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrectly typed address is one of the most common reasons an email fails to reach its intended recipient

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users of the same software to see if they are also experiencing email sending failures
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is isolated to your account, or reflects a broader configuration or server issue affecting everyone

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the software's email settings, such as SMTP server details, are accessible to you, confirm they match what is officially documented as correct
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Misconfigured email server settings will prevent the software from successfully sending any email

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ask the intended recipient to check their junk or spam folder for the missing email
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Automated emails sent from business software are sometimes filtered as spam by the recipient's email provider, even though the software reports successful sending

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the email settings appear correct and connectivity is confirmed, report the issue to the system administrator, since it may indicate a problem with the configured email server itself
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Server-side email configuration and delivery issues typically require administrator-level access to properly diagnose and fix

possibleSolutions: Restore network connectivity before sending
Correct a mistyped recipient email address
Verify and correct the software's email server configuration
Ask the recipient to check their spam folder
Report a suspected server-side email issue to the administrator
prevention: Keep the software's email server settings correctly configured
Double-check recipient addresses before sending important emails
Maintain a stable network connection when sending automated emails

description: The software displays an error specifically related to its configuration or settings, preventing it from functioning correctly, often appearing at startup or when a specific misconfigured feature is used.
symptoms: Error message specifically mentioning configuration, settings, or setup
The software may partially function while a specific feature fails
The error may appear consistently at every startup
A specific configuration file or setting is referenced in the error
possibleCauses: A configuration file has become corrupted or contains invalid values
A recent change to settings introduced an incompatible or incorrect configuration
A required configuration value, such as a server address, is missing
An update to the software changed configuration requirements without properly migrating old settings
Manual editing of a configuration file introduced a syntax error
diagnosticQuestions: What exact error message appears, and does it reference a specific setting or file?
Did this start after a recent update, or after changing any settings?
Has anyone manually edited the software's configuration files recently?
Does the error happen at every startup, or only when using a specific feature?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact error message and any specific setting, file, or value it references
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Specific error details help pinpoint exactly which configuration element is causing the problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Consider whether this started after a recent update, or after any manual changes to the software's settings
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This timing correlation helps identify what specifically triggered the configuration error

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a specific setting was recently changed, try reverting it back to its previous, working value
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly undoes a change that may have introduced the incompatible or incorrect configuration

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if the software offers a 'Reset to defaults' option for its configuration
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides a clean, known-good starting configuration, which can resolve issues caused by an accumulation of problematic custom settings

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a configuration file was manually edited, carefully review it for syntax errors, such as missing commas, brackets, or quotation marks
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Manual configuration file edits are a common source of syntax errors that can break the entire configuration

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a backup copy of a previously working configuration file exists, restore it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly replaces the problematic configuration with a known working version

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the software vendor's documentation or support resources for the specific error message, since configuration requirements and known issues are often documented
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Vendor documentation can provide precise guidance on required configuration values and common configuration-related errors

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the error persists and cannot be resolved through configuration review, consider reinstalling the software, which will typically reset the configuration to its default state
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides a fresh, clean configuration when other troubleshooting steps cannot resolve the underlying issue

possibleSolutions: Revert a recently changed setting to its previous value
Reset the software's configuration to defaults
Correct a syntax error in a manually edited configuration file
Restore a backup copy of a previously working configuration
Reinstall the software to reset the configuration
prevention: Back up configuration files before making manual changes
Document configuration changes as they are made
Test configuration changes in a non-production environment when possible

problem: Missing DLL or other required dependency
description: The software shows an error stating a specific DLL file or other required software component is missing, preventing the program from opening or a specific feature from functioning.
symptoms: Error message such as 'xxxxx.dll is missing from your computer'
The affected software or feature will not open or function at all
The error may appear right when the computer starts if the program runs at startup
Other software may continue to work normally
possibleCauses: The required file was accidentally deleted or moved
A malware scan removed the file, mistaking it for a threat
The software itself is corrupted or was not installed completely
A required software package, like a runtime or framework, is missing
The dependency exists but is registered incorrectly
diagnosticQuestions: What is the exact name of the missing file or component mentioned in the error?
Does this happen with one specific program, or many programs?
Did this start after a Windows update, antivirus scan, or manually deleting files?
Was this program working correctly before, or is this a fresh install?

commands.purpose: Scan and repair missing or corrupted Windows system files, which sometimes includes shared components
commands.expectedResult: No integrity violations found, or issues found and repaired
commands.abnormalResult: Corrupt files found that could not be repaired automatically

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact name of the missing file or dependency from the error message
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This tells you whether it is a common shared system component or something specific to this particular software

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if this happens with just one program or several, which helps identify whether the missing component is shared or program-specific
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A dependency missing across many programs usually points to a shared system component problem, while one affecting only one program points to that program's installation

troubleshootingSteps.action: Reinstall the affected software completely, uninstalling it first and downloading a fresh copy from the official source
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This restores any missing files that were part of the original software installation

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the missing dependency is a known common runtime or framework, download and install the latest version from its official source
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many programs rely on these shared packages, and a missing or outdated version causes this type of error across multiple programs

troubleshootingSteps.action: Run sfc /scannow to check for and repair missing or corrupted Windows system files
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This can restore shared system components that may have been accidentally deleted or damaged

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check antivirus quarantine or history logs to see if the missing file was removed as a false positive
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Antivirus software sometimes mistakenly flags legitimate program files as threats and removes them

troubleshootingSteps.action: Avoid downloading individual files from random websites, and instead reinstall the source program or required component from its official source
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Files from unofficial sources can be outdated, incompatible, or contain malware

possibleSolutions: Reinstall the affected software
Install or repair the required runtime or framework component
Repair Windows system files using sfc /scannow
Restore a falsely quarantined file from antivirus history
Reinstall the related component from its official source
prevention: Avoid manually deleting files from program installation folders
Keep antivirus software properly configured to avoid false positives
Install software only from official, trusted sources
Keep required runtime components updated

description: The user tries to log in to the company application using their normal credentials, but the login process fails without a specific clear reason, preventing them from accessing the system.
symptoms: Login screen rejects credentials or shows a generic error
Login button appears to do nothing when clicked
Login page reloads back to itself after submitting credentials
Error may or may not include a specific reason
possibleCauses: Incorrect username or password entered
The application server is down or unreachable
The user's account has been locked or disabled
A network connectivity problem preventing the login request from reaching the server
Browser cache or cookies interfering with the login session
The application itself is experiencing an outage or bug
diagnosticQuestions: What exact message or behavior happens when you try to log in?
Have you logged in successfully before, or is this your first attempt?
Are other users able to log in right now?
Are you connected to the correct network or VPN required for this application?

commands.purpose: Check if the computer can reach the server hosting the application
commands.expectedResult: Replies received from the server
commands.abnormalResult: Request timed out, meaning the server cannot be reached from this network, which would prevent login

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the exact username and password are being entered correctly, checking for Caps Lock and typing mistakes
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Simple credential entry errors are the most common cause of login failures and should be ruled out first

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are able to log in to the same application right now
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This quickly determines if the problem is isolated to one user's account or affects the application more broadly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the computer has a working network connection, and is connected to any required VPN if the application is only accessible internally
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Without the correct network path, the login request may never actually reach the application server

troubleshootingSteps.action: Clear the browser cache and cookies for the application's website, then try logging in again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Corrupted or outdated cached login data can sometimes interfere with a new login attempt

troubleshootingSteps.action: Try logging in using a different browser or an incognito/private browsing window
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is related to browser-specific settings, extensions, or stored data

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the application server's address, if known, to confirm basic network reachability
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps distinguish between a network connectivity problem and an application or account-specific issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the problem affects multiple users, check the application's status page or contact the system administrator to see if there is a known outage
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A widespread login failure often points to a server-side outage rather than an individual account or computer problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: If only this one user is affected, contact the system administrator to check if the account has been locked, disabled, or needs a password reset
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Account-specific restrictions require administrator access to review and correct

possibleSolutions: Correct mistyped username or password
Reconnect to the required network or VPN
Clear browser cache and cookies
Try a different browser or private browsing window
Wait out a confirmed application-wide outage
Have the administrator unlock, enable, or reset the affected account
prevention: Use a password manager to avoid credential entry mistakes
Keep track of VPN requirements for internal applications
Report suspected outages promptly to help administrators respond quickly
Periodically clear browser cache for frequently used web applications

description: The user enters their credentials to log in, but the application specifically responds with an 'invalid username or password' message, even though the user believes their credentials are correct.
symptoms: Specific error message stating 'Invalid username or password'
Error appears immediately after submitting the login form
Message does not specify which part, username or password, is incorrect
May happen consistently or only occasionally
possibleCauses: The username or password was typed incorrectly, including Caps Lock being on
The password was recently changed and the old one is being used
The account uses a different username format than expected, such as an email address instead of a short username
The account does not exist or was never properly created in this system
A trailing space or hidden character was accidentally included when typing or pasting credentials
diagnosticQuestions: Are you certain of the exact username format expected by this application, such as full email versus short username?
Was your password changed recently, either by you or by an administrator?
Is Caps Lock currently on?
Are you copying and pasting the password from somewhere, or typing it manually?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check if Caps Lock or Num Lock is currently on before retyping credentials
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An accidentally enabled Caps Lock is one of the most common reasons correct credentials appear to be rejected

troubleshootingSteps.action: Carefully retype both the username and password directly, rather than relying on autofill, to rule out saved incorrect credentials
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Browser autofill can sometimes store an outdated or incorrect version of a username or password

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the correct username format expected by this specific application, such as a full email address versus just a short account name
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Different applications expect different username formats, and using the wrong format will always result in this generic error

troubleshootingSteps.action: If copying and pasting the password, paste it into a plain text field first to check for accidental extra spaces or hidden characters
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Copying from certain sources can accidentally include invisible characters that cause the password to not match, even though it looks correct visually

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether the password was recently changed, and if so, ensure you are using the most current version
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Using an old, previously valid password after a change is a common and simple explanation for this error

troubleshootingSteps.action: Use the application's official 'Forgot Password' or password reset option if available, to set a fresh, known password
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides a definitive way to rule out any uncertainty about the current correct password

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the reset process indicates no account exists for the given username or email, contact the system administrator to confirm the account was properly created and is active
troubleshootingSteps.reason: In some cases, the underlying account itself may not exist or may not have been fully set up, which requires administrator involvement to resolve

possibleSolutions: Turn off Caps Lock and retype credentials carefully
Confirm and use the correct username format for this application
Remove hidden characters or spaces when pasting a password
Use the most recently updated password if it was changed
Use the official password reset option
Contact the administrator if the account may not exist or be active
prevention: Use a password manager to store credentials accurately
Update saved passwords promptly after any change
Be aware of the specific username format required by each application
Avoid relying solely on browser autofill for critical login credentials

problem: Password has expired and needs to be changed
description: When the user tries to log in, the application informs them that their password has expired and must be changed before they can continue, blocking normal access until this is completed.
symptoms: Message specifically stating the password has expired
User is redirected to a password change screen instead of the normal application
Login is blocked entirely until a new password is set
May happen suddenly based on a scheduled password expiration policy
possibleCauses: The organization enforces a password expiration policy after a set number of days
The password was not changed proactively before reaching its expiration date
An administrator manually flagged the account to require a password change at next login
diagnosticQuestions: Does the message specifically mention that your password has expired?
Do you know your organization's password expiration policy, such as every 60 or 90 days?
Are you able to proceed with the password change screen shown?
Do you have any specific password complexity requirements you need to follow for the new password?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Read the password expiration message and follow the provided prompt to set a new password
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Most applications provide a direct, guided process for changing an expired password right at login

troubleshootingSteps.action: Choose a new password that meets the organization's complexity requirements, such as minimum length and use of numbers or symbols
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A new password that does not meet policy requirements will likely be rejected, requiring another attempt

troubleshootingSteps.action: Avoid reusing a recently used previous password, since many systems block password reuse for a certain number of past passwords
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reused passwords are commonly rejected by security policy, which can cause confusion if the user does not realize this restriction applies

troubleshootingSteps.action: After successfully setting the new password, confirm you can log in normally using it
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This verifies the password change was fully successful and properly recognized by the system

troubleshootingSteps.action: Update the new password in any password manager or saved credential storage being used
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures future login attempts use the current, correct password rather than the old expired one

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the password change process itself fails or shows an error, contact the system administrator for assistance
troubleshootingSteps.reason: In some cases, expired passwords require administrator-level action, especially if the standard self-service change process encounters a problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Going forward, note your organization's password expiration schedule and change the password proactively a few days before it expires
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps avoid being unexpectedly blocked from logging in during an important task in the future

possibleSolutions: Follow the on-screen prompt to set a new password meeting policy requirements
Choose a new, unique password not recently used before
Update saved credentials in a password manager after changing
Contact the administrator if the change process itself fails
prevention: Change passwords proactively before their expiration date
Keep track of the organization's password expiration policy
Use a password manager to track and update passwords across systems

description: The user tries to log in, but instead of a normal password prompt or error, the application specifically indicates that the account has been locked, usually after several failed login attempts.
symptoms: Message specifically stating the account is locked
Login is blocked entirely, even with the correct password
Message may mention a lockout duration or instructions to contact an administrator
May follow a series of recent failed login attempts
possibleCauses: Too many incorrect password attempts triggered an automatic security lockout
An administrator manually locked the account for security or policy reasons
Suspicious login activity was detected, triggering an automatic protective lockout
The account was locked as part of an offboarding or role change process
diagnosticQuestions: Do you recall making several incorrect password attempts recently?
Does the lockout message mention a specific wait time before automatic unlock?
Have you contacted your IT department about this account recently for any other reason?
Is there any chance someone else may have attempted to log in to your account unsuccessfully?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Read the lockout message carefully to see if it specifies an automatic unlock time or specific instructions
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many lockout policies are temporary and will resolve automatically after a set waiting period, which the message may clearly state

troubleshootingSteps.action: If an automatic unlock time is mentioned, wait for that period to pass before attempting to log in again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Attempting to log in repeatedly during an active lockout period can sometimes extend the lockout duration further

troubleshootingSteps.action: Avoid making further login attempts while investigating the cause, since additional failed attempts can worsen the situation
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Continuing to guess at the password or retry repeatedly can trigger longer or more severe lockout periods on some systems

troubleshootingSteps.action: Contact the system administrator or IT help desk to confirm the reason for the lockout and request it be lifted if needed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Administrators can typically see the specific reason for a lockout and can manually unlock the account if appropriate

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the lockout was triggered by forgetting the correct password, use this opportunity to also reset the password through the official process once unlocked
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This prevents a repeat lockout from continuing to use an uncertain or forgotten password

troubleshootingSteps.action: If suspicious login activity is suspected as the cause, inform the IT security team so they can investigate whether the account may have been targeted
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A security-related lockout may indicate an attempted unauthorized access, which should be properly investigated rather than simply unlocked and ignored

troubleshootingSteps.action: Once access is restored, confirm normal login works correctly with the current password
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This verifies the lockout has been fully resolved and access is genuinely restored

possibleSolutions: Wait for an automatic lockout period to expire
Contact the administrator to manually unlock the account
Reset the password after unlocking if it was the original cause
Report suspected suspicious activity to the IT security team
prevention: Use a password manager to avoid repeated incorrect password attempts
Report forgotten passwords early rather than repeatedly guessing
Enable multi-factor authentication where available for added account security

problem: The system or application won't open
description: The user tries to launch the company application, whether a desktop program or a web-based system, but it fails to open, shows no window or page, or gets stuck before becoming usable.
symptoms: Nothing happens when trying to launch the application
A loading indicator appears but never completes
Error message appears before the application interface loads
Browser tab may show a blank page for web-based applications
possibleCauses: The application server is down or unreachable
A network connectivity problem preventing the application from loading
A corrupted local installation, for desktop applications
Outdated browser or missing browser components, for web-based applications
Insufficient system resources on the user's computer
A recent update introduced a compatibility issue
diagnosticQuestions: Is this a desktop application installed on the computer, or a web-based system accessed through a browser?
Does this happen every time, or only sometimes?
Are other users able to open the same application right now?
Did this start after a recent update, either to the application or your computer?

commands.purpose: Check if the computer can reach the server hosting the application
commands.expectedResult: Replies received from the server
commands.abnormalResult: Request timed out, meaning the server cannot be reached, which would prevent the application from loading

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether this is a desktop application or a web-based system, since troubleshooting differs between the two
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Desktop applications rely on local installation health, while web-based systems depend heavily on browser and network conditions

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are able to access the same application right now
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This quickly indicates whether the problem is isolated to this user's computer or represents a wider server or application outage

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the computer has a working network or internet connection, and any required VPN connection is active
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Without proper connectivity, the application cannot load or communicate with its server regardless of local settings

troubleshootingSteps.action: For web-based applications, try accessing it using a different browser or an incognito/private browsing window
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps rule out browser-specific issues like outdated cache, cookies, or conflicting extensions

troubleshootingSteps.action: For desktop applications, restart the computer completely and try launching the application again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A full restart clears many temporary software issues that could prevent an application from starting properly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for and install any pending updates for the application or, for web-based systems, ensure the browser itself is updated
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Compatibility issues from outdated software are a common cause of applications failing to open correctly

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the problem affects many users, check the application's status page or contact the system administrator about a possible server-side outage
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A widespread failure to open the application typically points to a server or infrastructure issue rather than individual computers

troubleshootingSteps.action: For a desktop application affecting only this one computer, consider reinstalling the application if a corrupted local installation is suspected
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This replaces potentially damaged program files that could be preventing normal startup

possibleSolutions: Restore network or VPN connectivity
Try a different browser or private browsing window for web-based systems
Restart the computer to clear temporary issues
Update the application or browser to the latest version
Wait out a confirmed server-side outage
Reinstall a corrupted desktop application installation
prevention: Keep applications and browsers updated regularly
Maintain a stable network and VPN connection
Report suspected outages to IT promptly
Restart the computer periodically to clear accumulated issues

description: While the user is actively working within the application, it suddenly closes completely, or a web-based version shows a crash or error page, interrupting the current task.
symptoms: Application window closes suddenly with no warning
Browser tab shows a crash message for web-based applications
Error report dialog may appear after the crash
Unsaved work may be lost
possibleCauses: A bug in the application triggered by a specific action
Insufficient system memory for the current task
A corrupted local installation, for desktop applications
Browser instability or conflicting extensions, for web-based applications
A server-side error causing the client to crash unexpectedly
Outdated application or browser version with a known compatibility issue
diagnosticQuestions: Does the crash happen during a specific action, such as saving, generating a report, or opening a certain record?
Does this happen consistently, or only occasionally?
Are other users experiencing the same crash under similar circumstances?
Did this start after a recent update to the application, browser, or operating system?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note exactly what action was being performed right before the crash occurred
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A specific, repeatable trigger helps narrow down the exact cause and gives useful information to report to support

troubleshootingSteps.action: Reopen the application and attempt to reproduce the same action carefully
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This confirms whether the crash is consistently reproducible, which is important information for diagnosing and reporting the issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they experience the same crash performing a similar action
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is a broader application bug affecting everyone, or something specific to this user's computer or data

troubleshootingSteps.action: For web-based applications, try the same action in a different browser or an incognito/private window
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps isolate whether the crash is related to browser-specific settings, extensions, or cached data

troubleshootingSteps.action: Close other unnecessary programs or browser tabs to free up system memory before retrying
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Insufficient available memory can sometimes cause applications to crash, especially during resource-intensive actions

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for and install any pending updates for the application or browser
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Known bugs causing crashes are often addressed in official updates released after the current version

troubleshootingSteps.action: For a desktop application, consider reinstalling it if crashes continue and are not related to a specific reproducible action
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This replaces potentially corrupted program files that could be causing general instability

troubleshootingSteps.action: Report the specific trigger, error details, and frequency of the crash to the system administrator or application support team
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Detailed, specific information significantly helps the support team diagnose and potentially fix the underlying bug

possibleSolutions: Avoid a specific identified trigger while it is investigated
Try a different browser for web-based applications
Free up system memory before performing demanding actions
Update the application or browser to the latest version
Reinstall a desktop application experiencing general instability
Report detailed crash information to application support
prevention: Save work frequently while using the application
Keep the application and browser updated
Report crash patterns to support promptly
Avoid running too many other resource-intensive programs simultaneously

description: While using the application, it stops responding to clicks, typing, or other input, with the screen frozen in its current state, sometimes requiring the user to wait or force close it.
symptoms: Application window shows 'Not Responding' in its title
Clicking buttons or typing has no effect
Loading indicator may spin indefinitely
Freeze may resolve on its own after a wait, or require closing the application
possibleCauses: A large or complex operation, such as generating a big report, taking longer than expected
A server-side delay causing the client application to appear frozen while waiting for a response
Insufficient system memory for the current task
A specific record or dataset causing the application to hang
A network slowdown affecting communication with the server
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen during a specific action, such as generating a report or loading a large amount of data?
How long does the unresponsive state typically last before recovering or needing to be closed?
Are other users experiencing similar slowness or freezing right now?
Is your network connection to the application's server currently stable?

commands.purpose: Check the application's CPU and memory usage while it appears frozen, to determine if it is truly stuck or working intensively
commands.expectedResult: High CPU usage suggests active processing, while 0% usage over a long period suggests a true freeze
commands.abnormalResult: The application shows 0% CPU usage for an extended period with no progress, indicating a genuine freeze rather than legitimate processing

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check Task Manager to see if the application is using high CPU, suggesting it is still actively processing rather than truly frozen
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps decide whether to keep waiting for a legitimate large operation to finish, or consider it a true freeze

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a large report or data operation was just triggered, allow extra time for it to complete, especially with large datasets
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some legitimate operations can take a genuinely long time and may only appear frozen while working correctly in the background

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your network connection stability to the application's server
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A slow or unstable connection can cause the client application to appear frozen while waiting for a delayed server response

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are experiencing similar slowness or unresponsiveness with the same application right now
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is isolated to your session or indicates a broader server-side performance problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the application does recover, save any work immediately and consider restarting the application for a fresh, stable session
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This protects recent work and reduces the chance of the same freeze recurring in the current session

troubleshootingSteps.action: If a specific record or dataset consistently causes the freeze, note this detail and avoid it temporarily while reporting it to the administrator or support team
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Certain records with unusual size or data issues can specifically trigger performance problems, and isolating this helps with a targeted fix

troubleshootingSteps.action: Close unnecessary other programs or browser tabs to free up system memory
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This ensures the application has adequate resources available, reducing the chance of memory-related freezing

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the application does not recover after a reasonable wait, close it and report the details, including what action triggered the freeze, to the system administrator or support team
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Detailed information helps identify whether this is a client-side, network, or server-side performance issue requiring further investigation

possibleSolutions: Wait for a large legitimate operation to complete
Improve network connection stability
Restart the application for a fresh session after recovery
Avoid a specific record or dataset causing repeated freezes
Free up system memory by closing other programs
Report persistent freezing details to the administrator or support team
prevention: Save work frequently while using the application
Maintain a stable network connection
Avoid running too many resource-intensive programs simultaneously
Report recurring freeze patterns to support for investigation

problem: Blank screen appears instead of the application content
description: The user opens the application, whether a desktop program or a web page, but instead of seeing the normal interface, the screen remains completely blank or white with no content displayed.
symptoms: Screen is entirely blank, white, or grey with no visible content
No error message is shown, just an empty screen
May happen for the entire application, or just a specific page or section
Browser tab may show as loaded, but the page itself displays nothing
possibleCauses: A JavaScript or rendering error preventing the web page content from displaying
An outdated or incompatible browser version
A browser extension interfering with page rendering
A slow or incomplete page load that has stalled partway through
A server-side error resulting in an empty response being sent to the client
Display or graphics driver issues affecting a desktop application's rendering
diagnosticQuestions: Is this a web-based application in a browser, or a desktop application?
Does the blank screen happen every time, or only sometimes?
Have you tried refreshing the page or restarting the application?
Are other users experiencing the same blank screen with this application right now?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Refresh the web page, or fully close and reopen the desktop application
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is the simplest first step and can resolve blank screens caused by a temporary loading glitch

troubleshootingSteps.action: For web-based applications, try opening the page in a different browser or an incognito/private browsing window
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the blank screen is related to browser-specific settings, cached data, or a conflicting extension

troubleshootingSteps.action: Clear the browser's cache and cookies for the application's website, then try loading it again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Corrupted or outdated cached files can sometimes prevent a web page from rendering its content correctly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Temporarily disable browser extensions, especially ad blockers or script blockers, and try loading the page again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Certain browser extensions can inadvertently block legitimate scripts needed for the application to display its content

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are experiencing the same blank screen with this application
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is isolated to your browser or computer, or represents a wider application or server-side problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the browser being used meets the application's minimum supported version, updating it if necessary
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Using an outdated, unsupported browser version is a common cause of rendering failures like a blank screen

troubleshootingSteps.action: For a desktop application, update the computer's graphics driver, since rendering issues can sometimes stem from an outdated driver
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Graphics driver issues can specifically affect how an application's interface is drawn on screen

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the blank screen persists across multiple browsers and computers, report the issue to the system administrator, since it likely points to a server-side rendering or data issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A widespread, consistent blank screen problem typically indicates something needs to be fixed on the application or server side rather than the individual user's setup

possibleSolutions: Refresh the page or restart the application
Try a different browser or private browsing window
Clear browser cache and cookies
Disable interfering browser extensions
Update the browser to a supported version
Update the graphics driver for desktop application rendering issues
Report a persistent, widespread blank screen to the system administrator
prevention: Keep the browser updated to a supported version
Periodically clear browser cache for frequently used applications
Be cautious with browser extensions on systems used for critical business applications
Keep graphics drivers updated for desktop applications

problem: Application appears to be loading forever
description: The user opens the application or navigates to a specific page, but a loading indicator, spinner, or progress bar continues indefinitely without the content ever finishing loading.
symptoms: Loading spinner or progress bar continues indefinitely
No error message appears, just continuous loading
May happen for the entire application, or a specific page or report
Waiting a long time does not resolve the issue
possibleCauses: A slow or unstable network connection preventing data from fully loading
The server is taking an unusually long time to respond, or has stalled processing the request
A very large amount of data being requested, exceeding normal loading times
A stuck or hung process on the server side handling this specific request
A client-side script error preventing the loading state from properly completing
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen with the entire application, or a specific page or report?
How long have you waited before concluding it is stuck rather than just slow?
Are other users experiencing the same continuous loading right now?
Is your network connection stable and reasonably fast at the moment?

commands.purpose: Check basic network connectivity and response time to the application server
commands.expectedResult: Consistent, reasonably fast reply times
commands.abnormalResult: Very slow or inconsistent replies, or timeouts, suggesting a network or server-side performance problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: Wait a reasonable amount of time, such as one to two minutes, in case a legitimately large amount of data is being processed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some operations, especially large reports, can genuinely take longer than usual without being truly stuck

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your network connection stability and speed
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A slow or intermittent connection can cause data to load extremely slowly, appearing as if it is stuck indefinitely

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are experiencing the same continuous loading issue with this application or specific page
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is isolated to your session or represents a broader server-side issue affecting everyone

troubleshootingSteps.action: Refresh the page or restart the application to cancel the stuck loading attempt and try again fresh
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This clears the current stuck state and gives the loading process a clean new attempt

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the loading is specific to one large report or dataset, try narrowing the request, such as using a smaller date range or fewer filters, to see if a smaller request loads successfully
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is related to the sheer size of the requested data rather than a general application problem

troubleshootingSteps.action: For web-based applications, try a different browser or clear the browser cache to rule out a client-side script issue preventing the loading state from resolving
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Sometimes the data does load successfully on the server, but a client-side display issue prevents the loading indicator from disappearing

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the problem persists and affects multiple users or specific known large operations, report it to the system administrator with details about what was being loaded
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This provides the necessary information for the administrator to investigate potential server-side performance bottlenecks or stuck processes

possibleSolutions: Allow extra time for a genuinely large operation to complete
Improve or stabilize the network connection
Refresh or restart to clear a stuck loading state
Narrow the request size, such as a smaller date range, for large reports
Try a different browser to rule out a client-side display issue
Report persistent loading issues to the system administrator with specifics
prevention: Avoid requesting excessively large reports or datasets when a smaller, filtered version would work
Maintain a stable network connection when using data-intensive features
Report recurring slow-loading patterns to help administrators identify bottlenecks

description: The user tries to use the application, but it displays an error indicating it cannot establish a connection to its server, preventing any data from being loaded or actions performed.
symptoms: Error message such as 'Cannot connect to server' or 'Connection failed'
Application loads its basic interface but cannot retrieve any data
All server-dependent features are unavailable
May happen for one user or many at the same time
possibleCauses: No active internet or network connection on the user's computer
The application server is down or restarting
A required VPN connection is not active for internal applications
A firewall or network configuration is blocking the connection
Incorrect server address configured in the application settings
diagnosticQuestions: Are you connected to the correct network or VPN required for this application?
Are other users able to connect to the application right now?
Does your computer have a working internet or network connection overall?
Has this application worked correctly before on this same network connection?

commands.purpose: Test basic network connectivity to the application server
commands.expectedResult: Replies received from the server, confirming a network path exists
commands.abnormalResult: Request timed out, meaning the server cannot be reached from this network location

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm the computer has a working internet or network connection independent of this specific application, such as by browsing a website
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This determines if the problem is specific to reaching this application's server, or a broader network issue affecting everything

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the application requires a VPN connection, confirm the VPN is currently active and stable
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many internal business applications are only reachable through a company VPN, and without it, connection attempts will always fail

troubleshootingSteps.action: Ping the application server's address to test basic network reachability
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly confirms whether a network path currently exists to the server from this specific computer

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are experiencing the same connection failure right now
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This quickly indicates whether the problem is isolated to this one user or represents a broader server outage

troubleshootingSteps.action: Restart the application, or refresh the web page, to rule out a temporary connection state issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A fresh restart can resolve connection problems caused by a stuck or corrupted session on the client side

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the application's configured server address, if accessible in its settings, to confirm it has not been accidentally changed or is outdated
troubleshootingSteps.reason: An incorrect server address will prevent the application from ever finding the correct server, regardless of network health

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the problem affects multiple users, contact the system administrator immediately, since this likely indicates a server outage or network infrastructure issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A widespread connectivity issue requires administrator-level investigation into the server and network infrastructure itself

possibleSolutions: Restore a working internet or network connection
Reconnect the VPN if required for this application
Restart the application or refresh the page
Correct an incorrect server address in application settings
Report a widespread outage to the system administrator
prevention: Maintain a stable VPN connection when required
Keep application server settings correctly configured
Stay informed of scheduled server maintenance windows
Report connectivity issues to IT promptly for faster resolution

description: The user tries to access the application and receives a specific message stating the server is unavailable, distinct from a generic connection failure, suggesting the server itself is not currently operational.
symptoms: Specific error message stating 'Server unavailable' or 'Service unavailable'
May include an HTTP error code such as 503
Problem persists across multiple attempts and refreshes
May affect one specific application or an entire suite of related systems
possibleCauses: The server is undergoing scheduled maintenance
The server has crashed or stopped responding due to an unexpected error
The server is overloaded with too many requests at once
A recent deployment or update to the application caused the server to fail to start correctly
An underlying infrastructure issue, such as a database or dependent service being down
diagnosticQuestions: Does the error include a specific code, such as 503 Service Unavailable?
Have you received any communication about scheduled maintenance for this system?
Are other users also seeing this same unavailable message right now?
Has this been happening consistently, or did it start very recently?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact error message and any accompanying error code shown
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Specific codes, such as 503, help confirm the nature of the problem and provide useful information for the administrator

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for any recent communication from IT about planned maintenance for this application or related systems
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Scheduled maintenance is a very common and expected cause of temporary server unavailability

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to confirm whether they are also seeing the same unavailable message
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This quickly establishes whether the problem is a genuine server-wide outage or possibly isolated to this one connection

troubleshootingSteps.action: Wait a reasonable amount of time, such as 10 to 15 minutes, and try again, in case this is a brief, temporary server issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Servers sometimes recover automatically from temporary overload or brief internal errors within a short period

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check the application's status page, if one is provided by the organization, for official updates on the outage
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many organizations maintain a status page specifically to communicate known outages and estimated resolution times

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the problem persists beyond a reasonable wait time, report it immediately to the system administrator, providing the exact error message, code, and time it started
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Detailed, specific information significantly speeds up the administrator's ability to diagnose and address the outage

troubleshootingSteps.action: Avoid repeatedly refreshing or retrying excessively while waiting, since this can add unnecessary additional load to an already struggling server
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Excessive retry attempts can worsen an already overloaded server situation for all affected users

possibleSolutions: Wait out scheduled maintenance
Wait for a brief, temporary server issue to resolve on its own
Check the official status page for outage updates
Report the outage promptly to the system administrator with specific details
Avoid excessive retry attempts that could add load to a struggling server
prevention: Stay informed of scheduled maintenance windows through official communication channels
Check the status page before assuming a widespread issue
Report outages promptly with specific details to help administrators respond quickly

description: The user attempts an action within the application, such as loading a page or saving data, but after waiting, receives a specific error stating the connection timed out, rather than a successful response.
symptoms: Error message specifically mentioning 'Connection timed out' or 'Request timed out'
The action seems to be attempted but never completes within the expected time
May happen with all actions, or specifically slow or large operations
Problem may be intermittent or consistent
possibleCauses: A slow or unstable network connection
The server is taking longer than the allowed time limit to process the request
A very large operation exceeding normal timeout thresholds
Network congestion between the user's location and the server
A firewall or proxy interrupting the connection before it can complete
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen with all actions, or specifically larger or more complex operations?
Is your network connection currently stable and reasonably fast?
Are other users experiencing similar timeout errors right now?
Does this happen consistently, or only occasionally?

commands.purpose: Check network response time and stability to the application server
commands.expectedResult: Consistent, reasonably fast reply times with no lost packets
commands.abnormalResult: Slow, inconsistent replies or significant packet loss, indicating network instability contributing to the timeout

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your network connection stability and speed, since a poor connection is a very common cause of timeout errors
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Timeouts often occur when data cannot be transmitted quickly or reliably enough to complete a request within the allowed time

troubleshootingSteps.action: Retry the same action to see if the timeout was a one-time, temporary occurrence
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some timeouts are caused by brief network hiccups that do not repeat on a subsequent attempt

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the timeout happens specifically with a large operation, such as a big report, try breaking it into smaller parts, such as a shorter date range
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This reduces the processing time needed, helping the operation complete within the allowed timeout period

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they are experiencing similar timeout errors with the same or similar actions
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is related to your specific network connection, or a broader server-side performance issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: If working remotely, check the stability of your VPN connection specifically, since VPN connections can sometimes introduce additional latency contributing to timeouts
troubleshootingSteps.reason: VPN connections add an extra layer of network complexity that can sometimes be a source of instability or slowdown

troubleshootingSteps.action: If timeouts happen consistently with specific types of actions, report this pattern to the system administrator, since it may indicate the timeout threshold needs adjustment or there is a server-side performance issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Consistent, predictable timeout patterns provide valuable diagnostic information that can lead to a proper server-side fix

troubleshootingSteps.action: As a temporary workaround for known slow operations, try performing them during off-peak hours when server load may be lower
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Reduced overall server load during quieter periods can sometimes allow operations to complete within the timeout limit that would otherwise fail during peak usage

possibleSolutions: Improve or stabilize the network connection
Retry the action after a brief pause
Break large operations into smaller parts
Ensure a stable VPN connection when working remotely
Report consistent timeout patterns to the system administrator
Perform known slow operations during off-peak hours as a workaround
prevention: Maintain a stable, reasonably fast network connection
Avoid requesting excessively large operations when smaller ones would suffice
Report recurring timeout patterns to help administrators adjust server settings
Use a stable VPN connection when required for remote access

description: The user tries to perform an action that requires retrieving or saving data, but the application shows a specific error indicating it could not connect to its underlying database.
symptoms: Error message specifically mentioning 'Database connection failed' or similar
The application's basic interface may load, but no data can be retrieved or saved
Error may include a technical code or reference number
Problem may affect one specific feature or the entire application
possibleCauses: The database server is down or restarting
The database server has reached its maximum number of allowed connections
A network problem between the application server and the database server
Database server maintenance is currently in progress
A configuration issue in the application preventing it from properly reaching the database
diagnosticQuestions: Does the error include any specific technical code or reference number?
Are other users experiencing the same database connection error right now?
Have you received any communication about scheduled database maintenance?
Does this error happen with all actions, or specific ones involving data retrieval or saving?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact error message and any technical code or reference number shown
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This detailed information is essential for the system administrator or database team to quickly diagnose the specific cause

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to confirm whether they are also experiencing the same database connection error
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is a database-level, typically server-side issue, and confirming its scope with others is important initial diagnostic information

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check for any recent communication from IT about scheduled database maintenance
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Planned database maintenance is a common and expected cause of temporary connection failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: Wait a short period, such as 5 to 10 minutes, and try the action again, in case this is a brief, temporary database connectivity issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Database connections can sometimes recover automatically from brief spikes in load or temporary internal issues

troubleshootingSteps.action: This type of error is generally not something an end user can resolve directly, since it relates to backend server infrastructure
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Database connectivity is managed at the server and infrastructure level, well beyond typical end-user troubleshooting capabilities

troubleshootingSteps.action: Report the issue promptly to the system administrator or database team, including the exact error message, code, and the specific time it started occurring
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This is a critical, backend infrastructure issue that requires immediate administrator attention, and detailed reporting speeds up resolution significantly

troubleshootingSteps.action: Avoid repeatedly retrying the same failed action many times while waiting for the issue to be resolved
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Repeated attempts can add unnecessary additional load to an already struggling database connection pool, potentially worsening the situation for all users

possibleSolutions: Wait out scheduled database maintenance
Wait for a brief, temporary connectivity issue to resolve
Report the issue immediately to the system administrator or database team with specific details
Avoid excessive retry attempts that could add load to the database
prevention: Stay informed of scheduled database maintenance windows
Report database connection errors promptly with specific details
Avoid excessive simultaneous requests during known high-load periods

description: The user tries to view a report, list, or record within the application, but instead of the expected data, they receive an error message stating the data could not be retrieved.
symptoms: Error message stating 'Failed to retrieve data' or similar
Empty results or a blank list where data is expected
May happen with all data, or specific reports or records
Problem may be intermittent or consistent
possibleCauses: A network or server connectivity problem interrupting the data request
A database issue preventing the underlying data from being accessed
The specific data being requested no longer exists or was moved
Insufficient permissions to view the requested data
A bug in a specific report or query causing it to fail
diagnosticQuestions: Does this happen with all data and reports, or a specific one?
Have you been able to successfully retrieve this same data before?
Are other users able to retrieve this same data right now?
Is your network connection currently stable?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note exactly what data, report, or record you were trying to retrieve when the error appeared
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This specific detail helps determine if the problem is isolated to one particular piece of data or a broader system issue

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your network connection stability, since interrupted connectivity during a data request can directly cause this type of error
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A dropped or unstable connection during data transfer is a very common and simple cause of retrieval failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: Retry the same request to see if it was a temporary, one-time failure
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some retrieval failures are caused by brief network or server hiccups that do not repeat on a subsequent attempt

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with other users to see if they can successfully retrieve the same specific data
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the problem is related to your access permissions or connection specifically, or a broader data or system issue affecting everyone

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm you have the correct permissions to view this specific data, especially if it is data you have not accessed before
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some retrieval failures are actually permission-related, presenting as a generic error rather than a clear access denied message

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the failure happens specifically with one report or query, note this pattern, since it may point to a bug or issue specific to that report rather than the whole application
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Isolating the problem to a specific report helps direct troubleshooting toward that specific piece of functionality rather than the entire system

troubleshootingSteps.action: Report the issue to the system administrator, including exactly what data or report was being requested and any error details shown
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Detailed, specific information helps the administrator or support team investigate the underlying data or query issue effectively

possibleSolutions: Restore network connectivity before retrying
Retry the request after a brief pause
Confirm and request correct permissions for the specific data
Report a specific broken report or query to the administrator
Wait for a server-side data or query issue to be resolved
prevention: Maintain a stable network connection during data-intensive operations
Confirm appropriate permissions are set up in advance for needed data
Report recurring retrieval failures for specific reports to help identify bugs

description: The user fills out a form or edits a record within the application and tries to save their changes, but the save fails with an error message instead of the data being properly stored.
symptoms: Error message such as 'Failed to save data' or 'Save unsuccessful'
Changes appear to be entered correctly but are not saved after the error
May happen with all save attempts, or specific forms or records
Data may partially save, causing incomplete or inconsistent records
possibleCauses: A network connectivity problem interrupting the save request
Required fields were left blank or contain invalid data
A validation rule within the application rejected the submitted data
The record being edited was changed by another user at the same time, causing a conflict
A database issue on the server side preventing the save from completing
Insufficient permissions to save changes to this specific record
diagnosticQuestions: Does the error message give any specific reason for the save failure?
Were all required fields filled in correctly before attempting to save?
Is it possible another user was editing the same record at the same time?
Does this happen with all records, or a specific one?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Read the exact error message carefully to see if it specifies a particular reason, such as a missing required field or validation issue
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Many save failures include specific, actionable details about exactly what needs to be corrected before saving can succeed

troubleshootingSteps.action: Review the form for any required fields that may have been accidentally left blank or contain improperly formatted data
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Missing or invalid data in required fields is one of the most common reasons a save attempt fails

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check your network connection stability, since an interrupted connection during the save process can directly cause this type of failure
troubleshootingSteps.reason: A dropped connection while data is being transmitted to the server is a common and straightforward cause of save failures

troubleshootingSteps.action: If corrections are needed based on the error message, make those specific corrections and attempt to save again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This directly addresses the root cause identified by the application's own validation feedback

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the error suggests a conflict with another user's changes, refresh the record to see the most current version, then carefully reapply your intended changes before saving again
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This resolves conflicts that occur when two people try to edit and save the same record at the same time

troubleshootingSteps.action: Before navigating away or refreshing, copy your entered data to a temporary location, such as a text document, in case it is lost during troubleshooting
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This protects the time and effort already invested in entering the data, in case the save process needs to be restarted

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm you have the correct permissions to edit and save changes to this specific record or type of record
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Some save failures are actually related to insufficient permissions, even if the initial view or edit screen was accessible

troubleshootingSteps.action: If the save failure continues without a clear reason, report it to the system administrator, providing the exact record, error message, and data you were trying to save
troubleshootingSteps.reason: Detailed information helps the administrator investigate whether this is a validation rule, permissions, or a deeper database issue

possibleSolutions: Fill in any missing required fields correctly
Restore network connectivity before saving
Refresh and reapply changes if a conflict with another user's edit is detected
Confirm correct permissions to save changes to this record
Report unclear or persistent save failures to the system administrator
prevention: Double check required fields before submitting a save
Maintain a stable network connection while working on important records
Communicate with team members to avoid simultaneous editing conflicts
Save work incrementally rather than making many changes before a single save attempt

Pages take longer than usual to load
Typing or interacting with forms feels laggy
Slowness may be constant or worsen at certain times of day

A slow or unstable network connection
Insufficient system resources on the user's own computer
A large amount of data being processed or displayed at once
Multiple browser tabs or other programs consuming system resources
A server-side performance issue affecting all users
diagnosticQuestions: Does this slowness happen at specific times of day, or throughout the entire day?
Are other users experiencing similar slowness with this application right now?
How many other browser tabs or programs do you typically have open at the same time?

commands.purpose: Check network response time to the application server to help distinguish network-related slowness from other causes

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note whether the slowness happens at specific times of day, such as during known busy periods for the business

possibleSolutions: Work around known peak usage times if flexible
Improve network connection speed and stability
Close unnecessary programs and browser tabs
Clear browser cache and cookies
Narrow large data requests with more specific filters
Report persistent, widespread slowness to the system administrator
prevention: Avoid running unnecessary resource-intensive programs while using the application
Maintain a stable, reasonably fast network connection
Use filters to request only necessary data rather than very large datasets
Report slowness patterns to help administrators identify and address bottlenecks

problem: Access denied error when using the application

symptoms: Error message stating 'Access denied' or 'You do not have permission'
Certain menu options or buttons are missing or greyed out
Access works for some areas of the application but not others
Problem may follow a role change or new task assignment
possibleCauses: The user's account role does not have the required permissions for this specific area or action
A recent change to the user's role or group membership reduced their access
The specific record or area has additional restrictions beyond general application access
The user is trying to access a feature not licensed or enabled for their account type
A temporary permissions synchronization delay after a recent access change
diagnosticQuestions: What specific area, feature, or record were you trying to access when this error appeared?
Have you had successful access to this same area before, or is this your first attempt?
Do you know if your role or job responsibilities have changed recently?
Are other users with a similar role able to access this same area successfully?

troubleshootingSteps.action: Note the exact area, feature, or record you were trying to access, along with the exact error message
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This specific detail is essential for the administrator to properly review and correct the relevant permissions

troubleshootingSteps.action: Confirm whether you have successfully accessed this same area before, or if this is a new task or responsibility
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps distinguish between a genuine, unexpected loss of previously working access, versus a new access requirement that has simply never been granted

troubleshootingSteps.action: Check with colleagues in a similar role to see if they can access this same area successfully
troubleshootingSteps.reason: This helps determine if the issue is specific to your individual account, or reflects a broader role-based access configuration that may need updating

troubleshootingSteps.action: If your role or job responsibilities have recently changed, this may explain a genuine need for updated access that has not yet been granted
